# C2-X-011

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The fence matcher receives that language, the title, the bracket label, parsed attributes and the code text value.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-012:
# C2-X-012

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A name without a declared and enabled matcher stays the core node that the parser built: an inline source extension, a div with its first class, or a code block.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-013:
# C2-X-013

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

An extension adds no sigil, line shape or delimiter in 0.2.0.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-014:
# C2-X-014

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

Two enabled matchers cannot claim one core node; registration of such a pair fails before parsing.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-015:
# C2-X-015

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A transform maps one claimed core node to one extension node of the same inline or block role. It may place further extension nodes that it produces inside the slots of that node, as the tabs transform places each `carve.tab` (C2-X-039).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-016:
# C2-X-016

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A transform leaves every core node outside its claimed node unchanged.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-017:
# C2-X-017

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A transform reads only the claimed node and its descendants.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-018:
# C2-X-018

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The extension node carries the declared qualified name and version, with the same version as its declaration.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-019:
# C2-X-019

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

`props` is a JSON object whose keys and value types are defined by the extension's registered schema.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-020:
# C2-X-020

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

`slots` is an object of named child lists. The registered extension schema fixes each slot's content kind. The root or envelope declaration names the slots in order, including slots absent from a node. A slot name is a lowercase identifier and has no number suffix that encodes position. Repeated children form an ordered list in one slot. A walker visits slots in declaration order without a registry. A validator refuses a slot the declaration does not name.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-021:
# C2-X-021

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

`payload` is an optional list of alternatives with a nonempty format and a non-null JSON value under C2-A-122.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-022:
# C2-X-022

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

`fallback` is mandatory for every qualified extension node. It is core content of the node's own role, block or inline: it contains no extension node and validates as core content.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-023:
# C2-X-023

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A reader without the extension resolves, renders and writes the fallback as core content, except where the Carve writer has a source form under C2-X-027. A writer without the extension writes that source form only when the written text parses back to one core node of that form and name whose canonical content is `body`, and otherwise writes the fallback and reports `structure-unspellable`. The source form it writes reports no loss: it reads back as that core node, which a reader with the extension claims again, and it is an exception to the equality of C2-W-002.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-024:
# C2-X-024

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A source transform carries a `source` record with `form`, `name`, canonical `body` text, and any quoted title or bracket label, plus the core node's attributes on the extension node. The class a div takes from its name (C2-B-119) is no attribute of the extension node: `{#t .k}` above `:::: tabs` gives the attributes `id` `t` and the class `k`. Where the fallback is the claimed core node, it is that node without these attributes, which the extension node holds, so the fallback HTML of C2-X-035 writes each of them once.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-025:
# C2-X-025

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

`source.form` is `inline`, `div` or `fence`, and `source.name` is the claimed source name. A reader refuses a `source.name` that no matcher of its form can claim: for `div` a name that makes no plain div (C2-B-127), for `fence` a language that opens no `code_block`, for `inline` a name that is no inline extension name (C2-I-094).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-026:
# C2-X-026

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

`source.body` is the canonical Carve spelling of the claimed node's content, without its opener, closer or attached outer attributes.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-027:
# C2-X-027

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A Carve writer with a source record writes the canonical `:name[body]`, colon-run div or fenced code block form under C2-W-039 and C2-W-040 and writes the extension node's attributes in the core attribute form.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-028:
# C2-X-028

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A Carve writer without a source record writes the fallback and reports `structure-unspellable` at the extension node.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-029:
# C2-X-029

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A transform gives the same node for the same claimed core node, extension version and configuration.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-030:
# C2-X-030

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A reader refuses more than 32 nested unqualified inline extension nodes along `children` used as fallback under C2-A-124, or more than 8 MiB of decoded payload on one extension node under C2-A-132. The nesting bound counts only that path, the `children` of unqualified inline extension nodes: a qualified fallback holds no extension node (C2-X-022), so it nests none.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-031:
# C2-X-031

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A reader refuses a `source.body` longer than 8 MiB in UTF-8 bytes and a qualified extension nesting depth greater than 32 through slots or children.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-032:
# C2-X-032

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

Resolution visits one view of an extension node: its `children` and named slots when a renderer is registered in the selected mode's channel (C2-X-033, C2-X-052) for its name and version or for an extension node whose slots hold it, and the profile admits the node (C2-H-163), and its fallback otherwise. So a node the profile degrades is resolved in its fallback, which its degraded form writes (C2-H-165). Validation and the limits visit all of them. Resolution does not execute or inspect props, payload or source text.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-033:
# C2-X-033

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A host registers a renderer by qualified name and version. The renderer receives the node, resolved child lists, fallback, rendering profile, URL policy, render `mode` (C2-H-122) and host helpers for escaped text, attributes, child lists and generated ids. Its `host.attributes(node, { block?, bare?, style? })` returns the attributes for an element, each with a leading space, in core writer order: `block: true` appends a generated `data-source-line` last when `host.sourceLines` is on and the node has a position; `bare: true` omits the node's authored id, classes and key-value attributes, so a synthesized row or row group can take only that generated line. With `style`, the helper merges the generated style declarations with an authored `style` into one attribute, at the authored key's position and with the value order of C2-H-009; without an authored `style` it writes the generated attribute in the order of C2-H-009. The host also exposes `sourceLines`, the effective boolean render option, and `blockDepth`, the current block indent in two-space units (C2-H-042).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-034:
# C2-X-034

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

An extension renderer is trusted host code. It returns an HTML string, which the host writes unchanged. The renderer uses the host helpers of C2-X-033 to apply escaping, the URL policy and the profile to its output. A host that renders untrusted documents registers only renderers it trusts. A structured output interface is left to a later version.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-050:
# C2-X-050

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A host transform or renderer exception does not escape the engine. When a transform throws, the engine retains the claimed core node and reports a diagnostic that names the extension. When a renderer throws or returns a value that is not a string, the engine renders the extension fallback and reports a diagnostic that names the extension. That fallback is written unresolved, since resolution visited the slots (C2-X-032): its references, footnote references and cross-references render as unresolved text (C2-H-085, C2-H-086) and its headings carry no generated id, and the diagnostic says that the fallback was written unresolved. The size of a renderer's HTML string is the host's responsibility.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-051:
# C2-X-051

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

If the engine cannot prepare a claim's canonical source record because the writer reports a loss (C2-W-134) or refuses a repair (C2-W-133), the engine retains the core node and reports `extension-transform-failed` naming the extension. Parsing and rendering continue with that core node.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-035:
# C2-X-035

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

With no matching renderer, the HTML renderer writes the fallback and reports `extension-fallback-rendered`. Where the HTML renderer writes the fallback of an extension node that carries attributes (an `id`, a class or a pair, C2-A-032), here or after a renderer fails (C2-X-050), it writes the fallback inside a `<div>` for a block extension and a `<span>` for an inline extension, and that element carries the attributes by the rules of every element (C2-H-010 to C2-H-014). A node without attributes adds no element.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-036:
# C2-X-036

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

Every profile restriction and URL policy check applies inside slots and fallback.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-037:
# C2-X-037

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

Equality compares an extension node's name, version, props, children, slots, fallback, payload, resource ids and source record under C2-A-161.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-038:
# C2-X-038

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A reader validates extension props and slot content kinds against its registered extension schema when it knows the extension. It validates slot names against the tree declaration even without a registry.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-052:
# C2-X-052

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

In `interactive` mode a registered interactive renderer handles the node. In `static` mode an explicitly registered build-time renderer handles it; registration for interactive mode alone does not select that channel. A build-time renderer returns self-contained HTML and receives the same host inputs and helpers as C2-X-033. With no renderer in the selected channel, C2-X-035 writes the fallback. Both channels obey C2-X-034 and C2-X-036.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-053:
# C2-X-053

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A host may register ordered document transforms. After includes and ordinary resolution, before HTML rendering, each receives a copy of the resolved render view and returns a view; registration order is execution order, and a later transform sees the earlier result. A transform may inspect the whole document, replace or insert nodes declared by its extension, claim existing directive nodes, and edit core nodes of the view: change their attributes or content, or replace them with core nodes, as a transform that numbers headings or turns inline footnotes into text does. It does not change the authored tree, source record or the tree the Carve writer reads.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-054:
# C2-X-054

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A document transform keeps core nodes it does not replace in their order and may claim a directive only once. The first registered transform to claim a directive owns it; a later claim fails that transform. Inserted extension nodes require their ordinary declaration, valid slots and core fallback. The normal tree limits and profile restrictions apply to the resulting view, and every URL it writes passes C2-H-159 to C2-H-161.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-055:
# C2-X-055

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The host checks ids in the transformed view in document order after each transform. An inserted or replacement node with an authored id already used by a preceding node fails that transform; the first node keeps its id. A duplicate authored id that the view held before the transform ran, which C2-A-039 reports, fails no transform: only the nodes a transform inserted, replaced or edited are checked. Generated ids, including heading and extension control ids, are allocated again over the final view by their ordinary rules, avoiding every authored id and earlier generated id. References in that view resolve against the final ids before HTML is written. A failed document transform leaves its input view intact and reports a diagnostic naming the extension, as in C2-X-050. The checks of C2-X-054 and of this clause are observable only in their result: a view that fails one fails that transform as this clause says, and a view that passes all of them is rendered. An engine may check only the nodes a transform inserted, replaced or edited, since every node it kept passed the same checks before it ran; the result is the one a check of the whole view gives. A render with document transforms therefore resolves twice: once before the first transform, and once over the final view for the generated ids and references of this clause.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-039:
# C2-X-039

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The core provides optional `carve.tabs` and `carve.tab` extensions at version `1`. The `tabs` div matcher produces `carve.tabs`; the nested `tab` div produces `carve.tab` only inside its `tabs` slot. A `tab` div elsewhere stays a core div.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-040:
# C2-X-040

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The `tabs` matcher claims a div only when its body has one or more `tab` divs and no other blocks, and each `tab` div has a nonempty quoted title.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-041:
# C2-X-041

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

`carve.tabs` has one slot, `tabs`, whose ordered items are `block_extension` nodes named `carve.tab` and nothing else. Each `carve.tab` has an optional `title` slot of inline nodes and a `body` slot of blocks. The transform puts the quoted title in `title` as inline content and the div body in `body`. Their declarations list `slots` as [`tabs`] and [`title`, `body`], respectively.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-042:
# C2-X-042

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The transform gives each `carve.tab` a core fallback with its title as a `strong` paragraph, when present, followed by its body blocks. The `carve.tabs` fallback concatenates those sequences in tab order.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-043:
# C2-X-043

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The tabs renderer writes one radio input, one linked label and one panel per item of `tabs` in order, with the input of the selected tab (C2-X-056) checked. That is its output in its default host option `mode`, `css` (C2-X-056). In `aria` mode it writes the WAI-ARIA tab pattern inside the same wrapper `div` instead: per item in order one `button` element with, in this order, `type="button"`, `role="tab"`, its `id`, `aria-selected` (`true` for the selected tab and `false` for the others) and `aria-controls` with the id of its panel, plus `tabindex="-1"` on every button but the selected tab's, holding the content the label would hold; then per item in order one panel, a `div` with, in this order, `class="tab-panel"`, `role="tabpanel"`, its `id` and `aria-labelledby` with the id of its button, plus `hidden` on every panel but the selected tab's. The renderer writes no script in either mode; a host that selects `aria` ships the script that switches the panels. Its build-time renderer, which a host registers for static mode (C2-X-052), writes no input, no `label` element, no generated id and no script: inside the same wrapper `div` it writes, per item in order, a `<section class="tabs-panel">` holding an `<h3 class="tabs-label">` with the content the label would hold, followed by the panel content. The selection does not change static output. Nor does the host option `mode`: the build-time renderer writes no button either. No output of the renderer has a line break between the elements it writes.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-044:
# C2-X-044

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The tabs renderer renders each label from the tab's `title` slot and each panel from its `body` slot. It escapes text and attributes through the host renderer.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-045:
# C2-X-045

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The tabs transform keeps the nested `tab` divs as div source in the outer `source.body`, in the canonical spelling of C2-X-026. A Pandoc bridge carries this structure as nested Divs with the classes `tabs` and `tab`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-046:
# C2-X-046

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A reader that knows `carve.tabs` (C2-X-038) refuses a `carve.tab` outside `carve.tabs.slots.tabs`, an item of that slot that is not `carve.tab`, or a tab without its `body` slot. The path of the refusal is the node it names: the `carve.tab`, the item of the slot, or the tab.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-047:
# C2-X-047

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The tabs renderer groups the controls under the `tabsGroup` label (C2-H-125) and names each panel with the plain text of its title, or, when the title is absent, `Tab`, one space and its position counted from 1, as `Tab 1`. The wrapper is `<div class="tabs">` with `role="group"` and an `aria-label` with that group label before authored attributes are applied. It writes the authored id, `tabs` followed by the authored classes, and the other authored attributes in the order of C2-H-009. In `aria` mode the wrapper takes `role="tablist"` instead, and a panel takes its name from its button through `aria-labelledby` and carries no `aria-label`; a button without a title holds the `Tab 1` text. An authored `role` of the `carve.tabs` node takes the place of the generated role, and an authored `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` the place of the generated name, in every mode: the wrapper writes the authored ones of these three attributes after its class, in their authored order, then the generated role and name that no authored attribute replaced. Without a stylesheet every panel of the `css` mode stays visible.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-048:
# C2-X-048

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The tabs renderer gives each radio input a unique document-scoped id and links its label to that id. The groups are counted in document order from 1: group N has the input name `tabs-N`, and its inputs the ids `tabs-N-0`, `tabs-N-1` and so on, counted from 0. In `aria` mode each button takes the id its input would take, and the panel of button `tabs-N-K` the id `tabs-N-K-panel`. Where any authored id or any generated heading id is one of the ids of a group, that group takes the next N whose ids no authored id or generated heading id takes, and later groups count on from it. The ids of a group are the ids it writes in its mode. A code group uses a separate counter from 1: its Kth tab, counted from 1, has the id `codegroup-N-tab-K`. The collision rule above applies separately to the ids of each tabs or code-group scheme.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-056:
# C2-X-056

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A tab's nonempty quoted title is its only label source (C2-X-040); a bracket label, a `label` attribute or a first heading does not supply a tab title. A tab whose attributes hold the key `selected`, with any value, is marked. The first marked tab is the selected tab, and with no mark the first tab is, so exactly one tab is selected; a later mark is ignored without a diagnostic. The standard tabs renderer takes the host option `mode`, `css` or `aria`, with `css` the default, as the code-group extension does; creating the renderer with another value fails. The option is a setting of the renderer, not the render option `mode` of C2-H-122, and it changes only the interactive output (C2-X-043). The group label of C2-X-047 applies in every mode, and the panel names in `css` mode only: in `aria` mode the button names its panel, and in static mode the heading of each section names it. A per-instance host class does not change the standard tabs contract.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-057:
# C2-X-057

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A registered `wiki` inline matcher claims `:wiki[Page]` as an inline extension with the parsed content as its target and core-text fallback. In `:wiki[Page|Display]` the content before the first `|` is the target and the content after it the display text, which is the fallback: `:wiki[Main Page|home]` falls back to `home`. Without a `|` the content is both. Its renderer may turn that target into a link only through the host URL helper and C2-H-159. A heading reference uses the existing core `</#id>` or `[Label](#id)` forms, and a bare URL or email uses an angle autolink; none gets a new delimiter from an extension (C2-X-013).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-058:
# C2-X-058

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A registered `cite` inline matcher claims `:cite[key]` as an inline extension with the key as its core-text fallback. A locator is an attribute, for example `:cite[doe]{locator="p. 4"}`, not punctuation inside the key. `:cite[a; b]` names several keys in one citation, separated by `;` and the spaces around it, and each key is resolved on its own. A named `bibliography` or `references` directive may hold definitions as core definition-list entries, with each term the citation key and its description the definition. A document transform may claim that directive and resolve the citations from it (C2-X-053); the claimed directive renders every entry in source order, including entries no citation uses. Without that extension, the inline form and directive retain their core fallback.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-059: # C2-X-059 Document: `carve://spec/extensions` The standard `imgFence` matchers claim code fences whose language is `img` or `image` and whose body is SVG source, producing `carve.imgFence.img` or `carve.imgFence.image`, respectively. Its fallback is that core code block without its attributes (C2-X-024). Its trusted sanitizer removes unsafe elements with their descendants and unsafe attributes, then accepts only a single well-formed SVG root it can reduce to a bounded image without scripts, event attributes, active or external references, or foreign content. If it cannot, the renderer writes the fallback and reports its failure under C2-X-050. It writes the standard SVG namespace on the root and percent-encodes the accepted SVG as UTF-8 in a `data:image/svg+xml` URL for the `src` of one ``; the encoded URL may be no longer than the existing 8 MiB extension payload bound (C2-X-030). Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-060: # C2-X-060 Document: `carve://spec/extensions` Only the `imgFence` sanitizer's own result, passed directly to that `` sink with its provenance intact, receives the URL-policy exception of C2-H-159. A source URL, an authored `data:` attribute, a copied sanitizer string or a value passed to another sink has no exception. The host applies the profile and its other attribute filters to the image and does not pass an unsafe sanitizer result through as HTML. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-061:
# C2-X-061

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A diagram extension of the fenced renderers, as `carve.fencedRender.mermaid`, and `carve.mathBlock` claim a code block by its language (C2-X-010), and their fallback is that core code block without its attributes (C2-X-024). A diagram extension has a build-time renderer (C2-X-052) only where the host gives it a build function, and the engine makes no network call. In `static` mode without one, C2-X-035 writes the fallback, the plain code block `<pre><code class="language-mermaid">`, and no `<pre class="mermaid">` source element as in 0.1.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-062:
# C2-X-062

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The renderer of `carve.mathBlock` writes `role="math"` on the element that holds the math, as core display math does (C2-H-072, C2-H-077).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-063:
# C2-X-063

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The `code-group` div matcher of `carve.codeGroup` claims a div only when its body holds one or more code blocks and no other blocks; a body with another block stays a core div, as a `tabs` body does (C2-X-040), so no block is lost. The label of a panel is the bracket label of its code block, or, where it has none, its quoted title, or else its language.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-064:
# C2-X-064

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The spoiler is one extension with two node names, because a definition has one matcher form: `carve.spoiler`, which the `spoiler` inline matcher makes of `:spoiler[...]`, and `carve.spoilerBlock`, which the `spoiler` div matcher makes of `::: spoiler`. A host registers both together.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-065:
# C2-X-065

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

`carve.details`, which the `details` div matcher makes, and `carve.spoilerBlock` take the fallback of a tab (C2-X-042): the quoted title as a `strong` paragraph, when present, followed by the body blocks. The core div with its class is not their fallback.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-066:
# C2-X-066

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A span key an extension adds for rendering and lint, as `samp`, `var`, `cite` and `dfn`, is an ordinary attribute for C2-A-035: only `abbr`, `time` and `kbd` are semantic keys of the core, so an added key merges with its other spellings by the general rule, and the duplicate checks treat it as any other key.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-067:
# C2-X-067

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

The `glossary` transform writes its definition lists inside the core `<div class="glossary">` wrapper of the directive, which carries the directive's attributes; it does not put those attributes on a list.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-068:
# C2-X-068

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

In `author-date` mode the author and year of a reference entry come from a span around its key in the description term, `:: [doe]{author="Doe" year="2020"}`, since a term takes no attributes in source, or from data the host gives the extension.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-069:
# C2-X-069

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A document transform does not see the render option `labels`, so the `index` extension takes the label of its back-links as its own option `backrefLabel`; its default is the default of the label `indexBackref`, `Back to`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-X-049:
# C2-X-049

Document: `carve://spec/extensions`

A writer with a source record that does not parse and transform back to an equal extension node writes the fallback and reports `structure-unspellable`. The test needs the extension's matcher, so it is the test of a writer that has the extension registered; a writer without it follows C2-X-023. A `write` call reads the option `extensions` for this test.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/extensions.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-001:
# C2-H-001

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The renderer returns an HTML fragment: no document wrapper, and no line ending after the last block.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-002:
# C2-H-002

Document: `carve://spec/html`

In text content `&`, `<` and `>` are written as `&`, `<` and `>`, and a no-break space (U+00A0) is written as ` `. No other entity is produced.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-003:
# C2-H-003

Document: `carve://spec/html`

An attribute value stands in double quotes, and `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'` in it are written as `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and `'`. A no-break space in a value stays the character.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-004:
# C2-H-004 Document: `carve://spec/html` A void element is written without a trailing slash: `
`, ``, `
`, ``. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-005:
# C2-H-005

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Each block element starts on its own line. A list, a quote, a table, a div, a figure, a section and the footnote section indent their child blocks by two spaces per level. Inline content stays on the line of its block, and a line break inside it is written as a line break with no indent.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-008:
# C2-H-008 Document: `carve://spec/html` A container whose body renders nothing keeps one empty line between its tags. This holds for a quote, a div, an admonition, a line block, a hard-break block and a figure group, and a body that holds only comments is such a body. The line is empty, with no indent. A table with no rows is not such a container: it is written as `` and `
` on two lines. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-009:
# C2-H-009

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The attributes of an element are written in one fixed order: the structural attributes of C2-H-010, then `id`, then `class`, then the language and the direction, then the keys in the order written, then the generated attributes that are not structural (`role`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby` and a generated `style`), then the render annotation of C2-H-016. A generated `style` merged with an authored `style` stands at the place of the authored key, and the `style` of an `align` key at the place of the first of the two keys (C2-H-015, C2-H-032, C2-H-057). The language is written as the `lang` attribute (C2-A-037) and the direction as the `dir` attribute (C2-A-031). Where C2-H-015 or C2-H-057 merge an authored `style` with generated declarations, the value is the authored value without its trailing spaces and `;`, then `; ` when that value is not empty, then the generated declarations.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-010:
# C2-H-010 Document: `carve://spec/html` A structural attribute is one the element derives from its own marker, destination or resolution: `type`, `start` and `data-delim` on `
    `; `data-task-state` on `
  1. `; `href` and `title` on ``; `src`, `alt` and `title` on ``; `role` on a footnote reference; `title` on `` and `datetime` on `` (C2-H-075); `rowspan`, `colspan` and `scope` on a cell; and, with `roundtrip` on, the carriers of C2-H-112. They are written in the order this clause names them. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-012:
# C2-H-012

Document: `carve://spec/html`

All classes of an element form one `class` value, joined by one space. A base class that the element's kind requires stands first: `task-list`, `math inline` or `math display`, `admonition` and the admonition kind, the name of a div's opener, `carve-figure-group`, `carve-figure-panel`. The classes the author wrote follow in the order written. A class the marker generates stands last: `line-block`. The class `hardbreaks` is a class of the tree and stands where `attrs.classes` has it (C2-A-068). A class that occurs more than once is written once, at its first place; the tree keeps every occurrence.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-013:
# C2-H-013

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Attribute names compare without regard to ASCII letter case. The keys `abbr`, `time` and `kbd` that make an element (C2-H-075) are no attribute names in this sense: they match in lower case only, and a key in another case is an ordinary attribute. A structural attribute replaces an authored key of the same name, except where a clause says the authored key wins (C2-H-048, C2-H-075), and an authored key replaces every other generated attribute of the same name, except a `style`, which is merged (C2-H-015, C2-H-032, C2-H-057). No element carries one name twice. A `lang` key beside the language part of an attribute block, as in `{lang=de :en}`, is such a case: the language part decides, and the key is not written. A `dir` key beside the `dir` field of a supplied or imported tree is the same case: the field decides.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-014:
# C2-H-014

Document: `carve://spec/html`

An attribute whose value is the empty string is written as `name=""`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-015:
# C2-H-015 Document: `carve://spec/html` An authored `align` key whose value is `left`, `right` or `center` once ASCII whitespace at its ends is removed and its ASCII letters are folded to lower case, on an element `

`, `

` or `

` to `

`, is written as `style="text-align: VALUE;"` with that folded value: on a paragraph, a heading, a div, a line block, a hard-break block and a directive that writes a `
`. An authored `style` on the same element keeps its value and takes the declaration after it. On every other element `align` stays an ordinary attribute. As in 0.1. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-016: # C2-H-016 Document: `carve://spec/html` With `sourceLines` on, each block element carries `data-source-line`, the number of the source line it starts on, counted from 1, as its last attribute. The generated value replaces an authored key of that name, as a structural attribute does (C2-H-013). Block elements here are the element of each block node, the `
text.carve://rules/C2-H-017:
# C2-H-017

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Attribute names, attribute values and destinations pass the filter of C2-H-128 before they are written. The filter removes attributes and blanks destinations. It never removes an element.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-018:
# C2-H-018 Document: `carve://spec/html` A paragraph is `

` around its inline content, except where a tightness rule writes it bare (C2-H-034, C2-H-040). A paragraph that carries attributes or a `lang` is never written bare, in an item and in a description alike: the `

` is what carries them. A block image is no such paragraph: its `` carries them (C2-H-020). Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-019:
# C2-H-019 Document: `carve://spec/html` A paragraph that holds one or more comments and nothing else but the breaks between them renders nothing: no element and no empty line (C2-B-140). A paragraph of breaks alone holds no comment and is written with `

`. A paragraph whose content, after the breaks that C2-H-069 does not write, holds only comments renders nothing as well, and so does a paragraph whose content writes nothing once the profile has degraded it (C2-H-165). Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-020:
# C2-H-020 Document: `carve://spec/html` A paragraph promoted to a block image (C2-B-157, C2-A-136) is written without its `

`: the bare `` on its own line. The attributes and the `lang` of the paragraph, which its attribute line gives, are written on the ``, merged before the image's own as if they were the first of its glued blocks (C2-I-039): the classes of the paragraph come first, and for an id or another key the image's value wins. So `{.c}` above `![a](y.png)` gives ``, as in 0.1. Where the image is an unresolved reference, C2-H-085 writes it as text, and text needs a block around it: the paragraph then keeps its `

`. That `

` carries the attributes and the `lang` of the paragraph. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-021:
# C2-H-021

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A heading is `<h1>` to `<h6>` by its level. HTML has no element for a level above 6, which only a supplied tree can hold (C2-A-071): such a heading is written as `<div role="heading" aria-level="N">` with its true level, so the level is not lost. It takes its attributes and its id like any heading, and it nests sections by its level (C2-H-026).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-022:
# C2-H-022

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Unless `headingIds` is `off`, every heading has an id: the id the author wrote, or a generated one. A generated id is the slug of the heading's plain text, computed as in 0.1 (CARVE-P2-004) and stated in C2-H-143 to C2-H-148. With `keep-case` the case is kept and a run of spaces becomes one hyphen. `lower` also folds the slug to lower case. `ascii` also transliterates it to ASCII and keeps its case, as 0.1 `asciiHeadingIds` did, and `ascii-strict` also drops what the transliteration leaves outside ASCII, as 0.1 `asciiHeadingIds: 'strict'` did; `ascii-lower` and `ascii-strict-lower` also fold the result to lower case, as each of the two with 0.1 `lowercaseHeadingIds` did.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-024:
# C2-H-024

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Generated ids are unique in the document: heading ids by this clause, the ids of notes and their marks by C2-H-202. Authored ids are reserved first, in document order. Generated ids follow in document order, and a slug that is already taken gets the suffix `-2`, then `-3`, and so on. An authored id is written as the author wrote it, also where two nodes carry the same one: the renderer does not change it, each later one is reported (C2-A-039), and a reference to that id resolves to the first node that carries it.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-026:
# C2-H-026

Document: `carve://spec/html`

With `sections` on, each top-level heading opens a `<section>` that holds the heading and every following top-level block up to the next heading of the same or a lower level number. Sections nest by level, and a level that is skipped makes no section of its own.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-027:
# C2-H-027

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The id of a heading that opens a section is written on the `<section>`. Every other attribute of that heading stays on the heading element.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-143:
# C2-H-143

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The plain text of a heading is the text its inline nodes give, in order. `text`, `code`, `literal_inline` and `math` give their value, and `non_breaking_space` gives a no-break space. `soft_break` and `hard_break` give one space. `smart_punctuation` gives the glyph it is written as. `image` gives its alt text, `autolink` its visible text, `abbreviation` the term as written, `mention` an at-sign and its target, `tag` a `#` and its name, and `caption_number` its number, or nothing while it has none. A `ruby` gives, for each pair, the base, `(`, the annotation and `)`. Every other node with inline children gives the text of its children: emphasis, strong, the braced forms, a span, a link and an inline extension. An inline extension named `index` gives nothing. `footnote_ref`, `inline_footnote`, `xref`, `symbol`, `raw_inline`, `critic_comment`, `comment` and `citation_group` give nothing, so a comment never moves an id. Which nodes give text is fixed by the node type, before any reference or symbol is resolved.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-144:
# C2-H-144

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The plain text is normalized to NFC, so a precomposed and a decomposed character give the same id. Then the characters of the list `removed` in `data/heading-slug.json`, bidirectional controls and invisible characters, are removed.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-145:
# C2-H-145

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Each glyph of the list `reversed` in `data/heading-slug.json` is replaced by its ASCII source, whether smart typography wrote it or the author typed it: `’` becomes `'` and `→` becomes `-->`. Every other character stays.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-146:
# C2-H-146

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Each maximal run of characters that are not an ASCII letter, an ASCII digit or a character at or above U+0080 is replaced by one hyphen. Leading and trailing hyphens are then removed. ASCII letters keep their case, and every character at or above U+0080 is kept as it is: letters of any script, symbols, punctuation outside ASCII, and the no-break space.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-147:
# C2-H-147

Document: `carve://spec/html`

With `lower`, each character of the result of C2-H-146 is then mapped to lower case on its own, by the Unicode lowercase mapping of that character with no context, so `Σ` becomes `σ` also at the end of a word and `İ` becomes `i` followed by U+0307. With `ascii`, the result is transliterated to ASCII by the table `transliteration` of `data/heading-slug.json`: each letter of its `folds` is replaced by its ASCII spelling, so `ß` becomes `ss`, then the text is decomposed canonically, the combining marks U+0300 to U+036F are removed and the rest is composed canonically again, so `é` becomes `e` and a Hangul syllable stays one character. A character the table cannot map is kept as it is, and C2-H-146 is applied again; ASCII letters keep their case, as in 0.1. `ascii-strict` works the same, except that each character at or above U+0080 that the transliteration leaves is then treated as a character that is not an ASCII letter or digit, so C2-H-146 makes a run of them one hyphen: `Café 日本語` gives `Cafe` where `ascii` gives `Cafe-日本語`. `ascii-lower` and `ascii-strict-lower` are `ascii` and `ascii-strict` with the result then lowered as with `lower`. Every engine uses that table, so these four values give one id in every engine; an ASCII heading keeps its slug, `Hello-World` under `ascii` and `hello-world` under `ascii-lower`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md

A duplicate slug then takes its suffix (C2-H-024), so the suffix follows the prefix: two headings `1` give `s-1` and `s-1-2`.

# C2-H-155

An admonition carries an accessible name. With a title, the title paragraph takes a generated id (C2-H-156) and the `<aside>` carries `aria-labelledby` with that id. text.carve://rules/C2-H-156:
# C2-H-156

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The generated ids are `adm-1`, `adm-2` and so on. They count the titled admonitions and the titled `footnotes` directive that places the footnote section, in document order, and then those inside footnote bodies, in the order of the footnote numbers. An unused footnote definition counts none. Every authored id and every generated heading id is reserved first. An `adm-N` that is taken gets the suffix `-2`, then `-3`, until it is free.

# C2-H-169

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The blocks inside the directive that places the footnote section are written before the section, in their order. The attributes of the directive are not written, and the section is named with `aria-labelledby` also when the directive carries an authored `aria-label`: the attributes of this directive are not written, so the exception of C2-H-155 for an authored name does not apply to it.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-158:
# C2-H-158

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The first top-level `footnotes` directive (C2-A-066) places the footnote section at its own place (C2-H-093); a later one places nothing. Its title and its label are the first children of the `<section>`, before `<hr>`. A titled one carries `aria-labelledby` and a generated id as in C2-H-155, in place of the `aria-label` of C2-H-089. The other five directives, `toc`, `glossary`, `index`, `bibliography` and `references`, place nothing in the core: each is written as `<div class="KIND">` that holds its title, its label and its blocks as a plain div does. What a directive places beyond this is left to a later extension, such as a table of contents for `toc`. A `footnotes` directive that places nothing is written as `<div class="footnotes">` in the same way.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md

# C2-H-051

# C2-H-134

Document: `carve://spec/html`

text.carve://rules/C2-H-206:
# C2-H-206

Document: `carve://spec/html`

`codeBlockRenderer` is a host function that writes code blocks, for a host that highlights them. The renderer calls it once for each `code_block` it writes, in the order of the output, wherever the block stands: in a container, in a caption figure, in a code group, in the fallback of an extension node and in the children of an expanded include. It is called in both modes and under every profile, but not for a code block outside the profile, which is written in its degraded form (C2-H-165). It is not called for any other node: not for a raw block, also where `rawHtml` off writes it as a code block (C2-H-050), not for a code span, a math node or an extension node that a renderer writes. It takes two arguments: the node, which it reads and does not change, with the language in `syntax`, the text in `value` and, where the tree has them, `title`, `groupLabel` and `attrs`; and the default HTML, the `<pre>` element that C2-H-047 and C2-H-048 give for the block, with its attributes, the carriers of `roundtrip` and the line of `sourceLines`. For a code block with a caption it is called for the block inside the `<figure>` (C2-H-062), so the node has no `caption`, `attrs`, `lang` or `dir` and the default HTML none of their attributes; the figure and its caption are written as without the function.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-207:
# C2-H-207

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The function returns HTML as text, or nothing. Text is written in place of the default HTML, after the same indentation and otherwise as it is: it is trusted host HTML, which the URL filter (C2-H-161), the character replacement (C2-H-176) and the profile do not touch, and the host answers for its safety and, in static mode, for its being self-contained (C2-H-122). Nothing writes the default HTML. A value that is neither text nor nothing is refused with an option error that names `codeBlockRenderer`, and the render returns no output. An error the function throws is the host's own and leaves the call unchanged; it is no refusal of C2-T-006. The tree does not change, and no entry of the record reports a replaced block. Without the option every code block is written as C2-H-047 says.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-055:
# C2-H-055

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A table is `<table>` with `<thead>`, one `<tbody>` for each body and `<tfoot>` for its groups. Each group tag stands on its own line and each row is one line: `<tr>`, its cells, `</tr>`. An empty group is not written.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-056:
# C2-H-056

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A header cell is `<th>` and a data cell is `<td>`. Explicit `table_cell.scope` writes `scope` with its value; otherwise a head header uses `scope="col"` and another header uses `scope="row"`. In a body with `rowHeadColumns` N, a cell that starts in one of the first N columns is written as a header cell. `headerIds` writes a space-separated `headers` attribute in its listed order, and each id names a header cell.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-057:
# C2-H-057

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A cell with a resolved alignment (C2-B-213) carries `style="text-align: VALUE;"`. A resolved vertical alignment adds `vertical-align: VALUE;` after it, one space apart, and stands alone where the cell has no horizontal alignment: `style="vertical-align: top;"`. A cell with no alignment on either axis carries no `style`. An authored `style` keeps its value and takes the declarations after it.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-058:
# C2-H-058

Document: `carve://spec/html`

`rowspan` and `colspan` are written only from the counts of the cell and only for a count above 1, so an authored key of either name on a cell is never written: the span marks alone shape the grid, as in 0.1. A cell that a span covers is not written.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-061:
# C2-H-061

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The caption of a table is `<caption>`, the first child of `<table>`. The attributes of the table stay on `<table>`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-152:
# C2-H-152

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A table with at least one column that has a `width` writes `<colgroup>` after its caption and before its first group, with one `<col>` per column. A column with a width carries `style="width: P%;"`, where P is the width times 100 written as a decimal number without trailing zeros, so `0.305` gives `30.5%` and `0.25` gives `25%`. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-153:
# C2-H-153

Document: `carve://spec/html`

`aligns`, `valigns`, `widths`, `header-rows`, `footer-rows`, `body-rows`, `body-header-rows` and `body-header-cols` on a table are never written as HTML attributes, whether the table consumed the key or kept it in `attrs` (C2-B-227). `header-cols` on a pipe table or a delimited table is written as an ordinary attribute (C2-B-214).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-200:
# C2-H-200 Document: `carve://spec/html` A cell whose children are not one `cell_paragraph` holds the blocks of an imported or supplied tree (C2-A-091), and each `paragraph` among them is written with `

`. A cell of one paragraph stays on the line of its row: `

c

`. Any other such cell is written as a list item with more blocks is (C2-H-007): a first paragraph on the line of the cell tag, every other block on its own line one level deeper than the row, and the closing cell tag on its own line at the indent of the row, after which the row goes on. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-062:
# C2-H-062

An image paragraph, a code block, a quote or a math block that carries a caption (C2-A-082) is written as `<figure>` around the block and then `<figcaption>` with the caption. With `sourceLines` on it carries the line the block starts on, and the element of the block inside it the line of the block's own opening markup, after its attribute lines.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-063: # C2-H-063 Document: `carve://spec/html` The `attrs`, `lang` and `dir` of such a block are written on its `

# C2-H-064

A figure group is `<figure class="carve-figure-group">`. Each panel in it (C2-A-084) is `<figure class="carve-figure-panel">` in place of the `<figure>` of C2-H-062, and the caption of the group is the last child of the group. A table panel is wrapped too: the panel figure holds the `<table>`, which keeps its caption as `<caption>` (C2-H-061) and has no `<figcaption>`.

text.carve://rules/C2-H-065: # C2-H-065 Document: `carve://spec/html` A caption holds blocks (C2-A-081). A caption with one paragraph, which is every parsed caption, writes that paragraph bare inside `
text.carve://rules/C2-H-066:
# C2-H-066

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The caption number mark `#` in a caption is replaced by the number of the caption in its sequence. The sequences, the label word that selects one, and the numbering of equations are as in 0.1. C2-B-207, C2-B-208 and C2-H-149 to C2-H-151 state them. A panel caption takes no number. The number mark of a caption that takes no number, such as the caption of a panel, is written as the character `#`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-067:
# C2-H-067

Document: `carve://spec/html`

With `roundtrip` off the number is plain text. With it on, the number is wrapped in `<span data-carve-caption-number>`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-068:
# C2-H-068

Document: `carve://spec/html`

`caption.short` is not written to HTML (C2-A-175).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-149:
# C2-H-149

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Each sequence key (C2-B-208) has its own count, from 1, in the order of C2-H-170. Each caption with a mark takes the next number of the sequence of its key. The label words are not a closed list: `Figure`, `Table`, `Listing` and `Equation` have no special meaning, the block under the caption does not select the sequence, and `Fig.`, `figure` and `Figure` count apart. The number is written in place of the mark as a decimal number, and the rest of the caption is written as it stands. A caption without a mark is written as it stands and takes no number.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-150:
# C2-H-150

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The captions and numbered equations of footnote bodies take their numbers after those of the document body, in the order of the footnote numbers. One in an unused footnote definition takes none.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-170:
# C2-H-170

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Captions and numbered equations of one key are counted in document order, a node before the nodes inside it, the document body first and then the footnote bodies (C2-H-150): the caption of a table takes its number before an equation in a cell of that table.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-151: # C2-H-151 Document: `carve://spec/html` In a supplied tree, a display `math` node that carries `numberPrefix` takes the next number of the sequence whose key is its `numberPrefix`, counted together with the captions of that key. The number is written after the math element as ` PREFIX N`. Inline math takes no number. A display math node inside a block or a `figure_group` whose caption has a mark takes no number of its own: the nearest such caption around it owns the number. `numberPrefix` has no source spelling, so a parsed tree holds no numbered equation, and `^ Equation #` numbers a caption. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-069:
# C2-H-069

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A comment renders nothing in every form: line, block and braced. The whitespace around a braced comment stays as written. A *comment line* of a paragraph or another leaf, a line that holds nothing but comments of any form and spaces, takes one of the two line breaks around it with it: the break behind it is not written, or the break before it when the content ends with the comment. The test is made in each list of inline children on its own, also in the children of an inline node such as a strong span: a line of that list is what stands between two of its breaks, and the end of the list counts as the end of the content. The tree keeps both breaks.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-070:
# C2-H-070

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Frontmatter renders nothing.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-071:
# C2-H-071

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A link definition and an abbreviation definition render nothing, except that with `roundtrip` on a run of abbreviation definitions writes a template (C2-H-178). A footnote definition renders only through the footnote section (C2-H-089).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-133:
# C2-H-133 Document: `carve://spec/html` An include directive that was not expanded is an `include` node (C2-A-181). It renders as a paragraph that holds the directive as text, written bare or with `

` as a `paragraph` node at its place would be (C2-H-006, C2-H-007, C2-H-034, C2-H-040): `{{`, a space, the path as C2-H-171 writes it, the section, the options in the order of C2-W-058 and the entries of `invalid` as the tree holds them, each after one space, a space and `}}`. An unexpanded include that has a caption is never written bare: its paragraph and the paragraph of the caption (C2-N-074) each get `

` on lines of their own. It is reported with the code `include-unresolved`. An include is unexpanded when no resolver was given or when its expansion failed (C2-N-061); an expanded include writes its children and nothing else (C2-N-075). Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-171:
# C2-H-171

Document: `carve://spec/html`

When an unexpanded include is written, a path that holds a space, a tab, `#`, `@`, `}`, `"` or `“` stands in double quotes, with a backslash before each `"` and `\` in it, as the writer writes it (C2-B-202, C2-W-058), so the text reads back as the same directive. An option value that holds a space, a tab, `@` or `}` stands in double quotes, and every other value stands bare. The value is the one the tree holds. An invalid option is written as the source spelled it (C2-A-181), so `@cols:"a,,b"`, which is no list of names (C2-B-205), stays `@cols:"a,,b"`. A `cols` list of names is written as its names joined by commas in one pair of double quotes; the tree keeps no quotes (C2-A-181). The writer does the same (C2-W-058). A value that starts with a double or a single quote is written in double quotes too, since bare it would read as the start of a quoted value (C2-B-204).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-072:
# C2-H-072

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The inline nodes map to elements as follows.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-073:
# C2-H-073

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A replacement is a `delete` followed by an `insert` (C2-A-097) and renders as `<del>` directly followed by `<ins>`, with no wrapper.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-074:
# C2-H-074

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Emphasis and strong nest in the tree order: `<strong><em>` or `<em><strong>`, as written (C2-A-096).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-075: # C2-H-075 Document: `carve://spec/html` A span with one of the keys `abbr`, `time` or `kbd` is written as the element of that name in place of ``. A value of `abbr` becomes `title` and a value of `time` becomes `datetime`, each only when it is not empty, so `[x]{time}` and `[x]{time=""}` are `x`; a value of `kbd` is dropped. Several keys nest in the fixed order `abbr`, `time`, `kbd` from inside out, and the remaining attributes go on the outermost element. An authored `title` or `datetime` wins over the derived one. The three keys match in lower case only: a key in another case, `KBD` or `Abbr`, is an ordinary attribute, so `[x]{KBD}` is `x` (C2-H-013). As in 0.1 (CARVE-P10-003 to CARVE-P10-007). Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-076:
# C2-H-076

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The names `samp`, `var`, `cite` and `dfn` are not core. Without their extension, `[x]{samp}` is a span with the attribute `samp=""`. An unqualified inline extension with no renderer is `<span class="ext-NAME">` around its content. The core never turns an extension name into an element name. In 0.2.0 an extension may give qualified `inline_extension` and `block_extension` nodes. A matching trusted renderer writes its returned HTML string unchanged under C2-X-034. An unknown optional extension renders through its fallback, inside an element that carries the node's attributes where it has any (C2-X-035), and is reported with the code `extension-fallback-rendered`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-077:
# C2-H-077 Document: `carve://spec/html` A math block is a paragraph that holds nothing but one display math span. The fact is set when the paragraph closes (C2-B-158, C2-B-198) and is the mark `role: "math"` (C2-A-184), as for a block image. It is written as `

` around the display form of C2-H-072, and it takes a caption (C2-H-062). Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-078:
# C2-H-078

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A smart-punctuation node is written as its glyph. With `smartTypography` off it is written as its `source` (C2-A-098).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-142:
# C2-H-142

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Three shapes reach the renderer only in a supplied tree (C2-A-175). `small_caps` is `<span class="smallcaps">` around its content. `ruby` is `<ruby>` that holds, for each pair, the base, then `<rp>(</rp>`, `<rt>` around the annotation and `<rp>)</rp>`. A `section` node is `<section>` around its blocks, indented like every container.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-079:
# C2-H-079

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A link is `<a href="URL">` around its content, with `title` when it has one. An autolink is a link whose content is its body as written. The destination of an email autolink is `mailto:` followed by the address, and its content is the address.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-080: # C2-H-080 Document: `carve://spec/html` An image is ``, with `title` when it has a tooltip. `alt` is always written, empty for a decorative image. A supplied image without `src` writes `src=""`. A `longDescription` writes its blocks as visible HTML after the block that contains the image. This keeps block elements outside a paragraph and needs no generated id or reference. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-081:
# C2-H-081

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A direct link, a reference link, or an autolink inside link text is unwrapped: its content is written and its anchor is not (C2-A-111). A resolved cross-reference inside link text writes its generated plain text without an anchor. A mention or tag with a `social` URL inside link text writes its inert span instead of an anchor. These rules apply at every depth of the link text. An unresolved reference or cross-reference writes its ordinary text. Raw HTML, trusted symbol values, and extension renderer output remain verbatim; the core does not inspect anchors supplied by those payloads. A core citation group writes text and makes no anchor.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-082:
# C2-H-082

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A destination that `urlPolicy` denies is written as the empty string, and the element stays: `<a href="">`. The denial is reported as the render loss `destination-denied`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-083:
# C2-H-083

Document: `carve://spec/html`

A link reference resolves against the link definitions, then against the headings (C2-I-081, C2-I-084). A reference that a heading resolves is `<a href="#ID">` with the id of that heading. The first matching heading in document order wins.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-085:
# C2-H-085

Document: `carve://spec/html`

An unresolved full or collapsed reference renders its brackets and label as literal text: `[`, rendered children, `]`, then `[key]` for `refForm: "full"` or `[]` for `refForm: "collapsed"`. An image adds `!` and uses its `alt` as text. No source form is rebuilt for the children. A footnote reference or inline footnote among them keeps its ordinary meaning. A shortcut of parsed source has a matching definition and never reaches this rule (C2-I-072); an unresolved shortcut of a supplied tree (C2-A-213) renders `[`, its rendered children and `]`, with no label after them. The attribute blocks glued to the reference follow its text as one brace block in the fixed order (C2-I-085, C2-H-139), for a render of source and of a supplied tree alike.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-086:
# C2-H-086

Document: `carve://spec/html`

An unresolved footnote reference renders as the text `[^key]`, and an unresolved cross-reference as the text `</#key>`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-139:
# C2-H-139

Document: `carve://spec/html`

An attribute block that is attached to an unresolved reference is written after it as text, as one brace block in the fixed order: id, classes, language, keys. A key with an empty value is written as its name alone. A value that holds whitespace, `"`, `'`, a backslash, `|` or `}` stands in double quotes, with a backslash before each `"` and each backslash in it; every other value stands bare.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-141:
# C2-H-141

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The attributes of a link definition are merged into every link and image that resolves through it. The classes of the definition come first and the classes of the reference follow. An id and a key of the reference win over those of the definition. The keys of the definition that the reference does not carry come first, in the definition's order, then the keys of the reference in its order: a definition `{j=2 k=1}` and a reference `{m=4 j=3}` give `k="1" m="4" j="3"`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-087:
# C2-H-087

Document: `carve://spec/html`

Footnotes are numbered from 1 in the order of their first reference in the document. A labeled footnote and an inline footnote share the one sequence. A later reference to the same label reuses its number. References in the body of the document are numbered first, in document order; references that stand inside a note are numbered after them, note by note in the order of the notes' numbers.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-088: # C2-H-088 Document: `carve://spec/html` A footnote reference or inline footnote writes its note mark as `N`. The second and later references to one note have the ids `fnrefN-2`, `fnrefN-3`, and so on, each suffixed when taken (C2-H-202). An id the author wrote on a reference replaces the generated one, and the backlink of the note points to it. When a note mark occurs anywhere in the text of a direct or reference link, including inside an inline descendant, nothing is written at its place. The marks are written directly after the closing `` of the outermost rendered link in source order. The footnote and inline footnote nodes stay at their places in the tree, and the backlinks point to the moved marks. An image's alternative text and every other plain text rendering are unchanged. A cross-reference has generated plain text and no inline children that can hold a note mark. A heading's generated id is on its heading or section element, not on an enclosing anchor, so a link inside a heading follows this rule as elsewhere. Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-089:
# C2-H-089

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The footnotes are written in one section: `<section role="doc-endnotes" aria-label="LABEL">`, then `<hr>`, then `<ol>` with one `<li id="fnN">` per note in number order, its id suffixed when taken (C2-H-202). LABEL is the `endnotes` string of `labels`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-202:
# C2-H-202

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The ids of C2-H-088 and C2-H-089 take part in the uniqueness of C2-H-024. They are allocated after every other generated id (C2-H-024, C2-H-025, C2-H-156, C2-H-158), reference by reference in the order of C2-H-087: a reference that introduces note N allocates `fnN` and then its own id, and a later reference to note N allocates its own id. An id that is already taken gets the suffix `-2`, then `-3`, until it is free, so a taken `fnref1-2` becomes `fnref1-2-2`. The `href` of the reference and the backlinks of the note use the final id. An id the author wrote on a reference is reserved first like every authored id and is kept. 0.1 left these ids out, so an authored id or a heading slug could duplicate them.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-090:
# C2-H-090

Document: `carve://spec/html`

The body of an inline footnote is one paragraph.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/html.md
text.carve://rules/C2-H-091:
# C2-H-091 Document: `carve://spec/html` The backlinks are appended to the last block of the note that renders something when that block is written as `

`, and otherwise stand in a paragraph of their own. A note with one reference has one backlink, `↩`, where LABEL is the `footnoteBacklink` label (C2-H-125).
