The text `x(/u)(/u)/` is written `x(\/u)(\/u)/`: bare, the third and fourth slash pair, so the third is escaped; then the first and fourth pair, so the first is escaped. An engine may find the same form with fewer parses, as long as the form is the same. For a tree from a parse the procedure keeps the tree. For a supplied tree it may not: the writer compares the parse of its finished form with the tree and reports each node that did not read back as a loss (C2-W-011, C2-W-124).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-125:
# C2-W-125

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

The procedure of C2-W-088 can end while a node of the tree has not formed, because a character that opens nothing in the bare text keeps it from forming or ends it early. The writer then places a backslash for that node, takes out the backslashes the procedure had placed for the same stretch, and runs the procedure again from there. These are the only cases. One: a bare opening brace that reads on into a later construct of the tree gets the backslash, `x *\{*` for a strong `{`; of several braces it is the one glued before the construct, or else the last one inside the construct before its own attribute block, or else the nearest before it. Two: where the right neighbor decides the direction of a smart quote of the tree, the neighbor gets it, `x/"\]` for a left double quote before `]`. Three: where a sigil stands before the bracket of a footnote reference of the tree, the sigil gets it, `x\^[^[]`. Four: where a hyphen run starts with a dash of the tree and ends in text, the first hyphen behind the dash gets it, `x--\-` for an en dash and a hyphen. Five: where a closer, a lone bracket or a sigil inside a bracket label keeps a link from forming or ends it early, its first character gets the backslash, as the `/}` inside a braced emphasis, a `[` or `]` inside an inline footnote, and the caret of link text `^a` in `[\^a](/u)`. Six: where a text character directly behind a node would lengthen that node, it gets the backslash, as a backtick behind a code span and a name character behind a mention or a tag: the text of a code span `a` followed by a backtick is written with a backslash before that backtick, and a mention `@a` followed by an underscore as `@a\_`. Seven: where the escape of a sigil opener would change the direction of a smart quote of the tree before it, the backslash goes before the bracket of that opener instead: a right single quote before the text `:n[]` is written with the backslash before `[`, not before the colon; where the opener is a run without a bracket, as a comparison sign, its second character takes the backslash, `!\=`. Where more than one case fits an input, the cases are tried in this order and the first that gives the tree is taken. Where none gives the tree alone, the writer keeps the backslash of case six when case six fits, and otherwise that of the first case that fits, and runs the procedure again from there: for the text `x{.c}` and a backtick, the code span `a` and the text of a backtick, the brace stays bare and both text backticks take a backslash. A form with these backslashes is the canonical one, and C2-W-088 does not call them defects.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-092:
# C2-W-092

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A paragraph line is tested for reading as a block opener or as an interrupter. The cases:

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-093:
# C2-W-093

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A delimiter is tested for pairing: a `/` or `*` that would open or close emphasis or strong, and a delimiter inside a braced span that would close a span opened outside it.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-094:
# C2-W-094

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A bracket is tested for forming a construct: a pair followed by a link tail, by `[label]` or `[]`, or by a brace block; `![`; `^[`; `[^`; and a bracket pair whose label would resolve as a reference.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-095:
# C2-W-095

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A sigil is tested for forming: `@` and `#` before a name after a boundary (C2-I-090), `:name:`, `:name[`, `<` before a URL, an email address or `/#`, a backtick run, `$` before a backtick run, and the runs that smart typography replaces where the tree holds text and not a smart-punctuation node.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-096:
# C2-W-096

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

An opening brace is tested for forming an attribute block, a braced comment, an editorial comment or a braced opener (C2-I-043).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-097:
# C2-W-097

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A backslash in text is written as two when the next character is ASCII punctuation or a space, or when it ends the line (C2-I-010 to C2-I-012). In the alt text of an image a backslash is written as two when the next character is ASCII punctuation or when it ends the alt text, and a bracket that has no partner in the alt text takes a backslash (C2-I-074). A `[` directly followed by `^` opens a footnote label (C2-I-087) and would end the image text early, so the writer escapes the `]` directly after `[^`, and where a later `]` of the alt text has no partner it escapes the `]` that closes the `[^` pair instead, so that the `[` takes the later one: `[^]]` is written `![[^\]]]()` and `[^}]{#]` is written `![[^}\]\{#]]()`. A code span and a braced comment in the alt text are read raw: their brackets take part in no pairing, and the opening run of one that has no closer in the alt text takes a backslash.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-098:
# C2-W-098

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

In a table cell every pipe is written with a backslash, in text, a destination, a title, a label and a quoted attribute value alike, except a pipe between a backtick run and its closing run, as in a code span, which needs none (C2-B-169, C2-B-224). A value of a row attribute that holds a pipe is written in quotes (C2-W-050) with the pipe bare, since a pipe in a quoted value there does not close the row (C2-B-166).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-099:
# C2-W-099

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A text line that holds only underscores, or one hyphen, is written as it is and needs no escape: it is not a thematic break (C2-B-159). A text run of two or more hyphens that would read as dashes is written with every second hyphen escaped, starting with the second, on any line, as in `-\-` and `-\--` (C2-I-111, C2-W-095): that leaves no two bare hyphens side by side and adds no escape that is not needed (C2-W-088). The escape also keeps three hyphens on line 1 from opening frontmatter (C2-B-161). Where the first block of the document would read as another tree on line 1 and reads as itself below a blank line, as a paragraph that holds only an em dash node with the source `---` does (C2-B-161), the output starts with one blank line. Formatting that output again gives the same bytes.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-100:
# C2-W-100

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

`carve fmt` writes the canonical form of each file, and with `--normalize` the normalized one (C2-W-127). With `--check` it changes nothing and exits with status 1 when a file would change and 0 when none would. For each file that would change, in the order of the files, it writes three lines on standard output, the product of the command (C2-T-014): the path, a colon and the number of the first line that differs, as `a.crv:2`; then `- ` and that line of the file; then `+ ` and the line `fmt` writes there. Where one side has no such line, its line is the prefix alone, `-` or `+`. Lines are compared with their line endings, so a file that differs only in a line ending, a CRLF or a missing final line feed, names the first line whose ending differs, and both of its lines are written without their endings: `a` with no final line feed gives `a.crv:1`, `- a` and `+ a`. With `--diff` it prints a unified diff under the same exit codes. The path of standard input is `<stdin>`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-101:
# C2-W-101

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A command line fails with status 2 for an unknown option or a bad option value, for an input file that is missing or unreadable, for AST JSON that is not valid, and for an HTML input the importer refuses (C2-M-006). The first line on stderr starts with `carve[CATEGORY]:`, where CATEGORY is `usage`, `input-unreadable`, `ast-json-invalid` or `import-input-invalid` for these failures; the table of C2-T-040 holds every category with its status.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-102:
# C2-W-102

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

The writer is also reachable from AST JSON with no source and no sidecar. It then writes the defaults of C2-W-083.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-103:
# C2-W-103

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A parse, a render, a write and a lint run report into one diagnostics record (C2-A-172). Every entry has a code, a severity, a position, a message and a channel (C2-A-173). The position is a byte range in the source, a path into the tree, or both: a finding of the writer on a supplied tree has the path alone.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-104:
# C2-W-104

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

The channel is `parse`, `render-loss` or `lint`. A code belongs to one channel. The writer's codes `structure-unspellable` and `field-unspellable` are in the render-loss channel, and so are the codes of the HTML importer (C2-M-080).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-105:
# C2-W-105

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

The severity is one of `hint`, `warning` and `error`, in lower case. The 0.1 engine source writes the first with a capital, `Hint`. The default is `warning`: a rule has that severity unless the catalog names another.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-106:
# C2-W-106

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

Every code is an entry of one catalog, `data/lint-rules.json`. This covers the specified parse, HTML render, write, import and lint operations; export-only loss codes of the renderers of C2-T-003 are engine codes outside that catalog. A catalog code is a contract: it is not renamed and not reused. A single plain message applies to every finding of its code. A row may express that same message as one variant whose `when` is `every finding of this code`; it applies to every finding. When a row has several messages, every variant states a `when` condition, and at least one condition must match every finding; if conditions overlap, the first matching variant in `messages` applies. The `reports` text of a row states what the code reports and the clauses it rests on; for a rule kept from 0.1 it is the trigger of the 0.1 engine with the row's `change`, stated on the 0.2 tokens and tree.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-107:
# C2-W-107

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

Lint is computed by a lint call from the parsed document: its tokens, tree and source ranges assigned by the parse. A render call does not run lint or return lint-channel entries; `unresolved-reference-link` belongs to a lint call, even when C2-H-085 writes the same unresolved reference as text. A source shape counts only where the parse reads it as the construct a catalog row names. A mark that C2-I-010 reads as an escaped character is not the start or end of a source shape that any catalog row reports. Where a rule reports a shape because it stays text, the shape counts only where the parse reads it as text of a paragraph, heading, cell, term, caption or line of a line block. Lint does not search the body of a comment block, a line or braced comment, a code span or block, raw content, an attribute key or value, a link destination or title, frontmatter, math content, or the marks of a braced opener or closer that formed or that C2-I-060 leaves as text, unless the row expressly names that place. The `reports` text cannot extend a trigger beyond a clause it cites: where they give different results for an input, the clause decides and the row must agree.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-108:
# C2-W-108

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

Lint never changes the tree and never changes the output of `fmt`.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-109:
# C2-W-109

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

The option `rules` turns single rules on and off, and `platforms` selects the platform rules. A rule can be suppressed in the source by the control comments of 0.1 (C2-B-215, C2-B-216). A rule that is off by default is turned on by its id. There is no named group of rules.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-110:
# C2-W-110

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A rule whose id starts with `deprecated-` reports a spelling that 0.2 removed and that now reads as something else. These rules are on by default through 0.2.x.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-111:
# C2-W-111

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

Each `deprecated-` rule states its trigger on the 0.2 tokens and tree. The 0.2 engine holds no 0.1 parsing code for them.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-113:
# C2-W-113

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

A finding that a syntax chapter calls a diagnostic or a warning is reported by the parser, in the parse channel. A finding that a chapter calls lint, and every other rule of this catalog, is reported in the lint channel. A code keeps its one channel in every tool.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-137:
# C2-W-137

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

`comment-splits-table-row` reports a comment between a table row and its continuation row (C2-B-175), as a comment-only line or as the trailing comment of the row, at the comment. The comment belongs to the row's group after the whole row (C2-A-086), so it does not stay where it was written, and where it ends the last group the writer keeps it there only with an empty continuation row behind it (C2-W-135). The message suggests moving the comment above the row or below its last continuation row. The rule is a hint and changes neither the tree nor `fmt` (C2-W-108).

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-138:
# C2-W-138

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

The range of an entry is the source span of the construct that the catalog row of its code names, in `reports` or `channel_reports`, unless that row states a `range` or names a range in `reports`, or the clause of the rule names another place, as C2-W-137 and C2-M-081 do. A stated catalog range takes precedence over the general extents below. Where that construct is a part of a node, such as an attribute, an option, a destination, a delimiter or a quote, the range is that part and not the node. Where the row states no range, an attribute range is its whole key and value as written, without the enclosing braces; a block opener range is the opening mark only, without indentation or following content. An entry of a run on source carries that range, in the render-loss channel too, and its path, where it has one, names the node that holds the construct. An entry on a supplied tree has the path alone (C2-W-103); where its construct is a field, the path names the field, as `/children/1/href`. A finding about a whole document starts where the document starts.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://rules/C2-W-143:
# C2-W-143

Document: `carve://spec/writer`

For lint, a line is blank for the rules inside its containers when it holds only spaces and tabs after the prefixes of those containers (C2-B-027). Every rule that tests for a blank line tests this. A line `>` inside a quote is blank for the rules inside the quote, although the parse does not read it as a blank line that ends the quote (C2-B-009, C2-B-032). A mark that is no container prefix is not blank: `>>` at column 1 is text (C2-B-031). The term *blank line* keeps its meaning for the parse.

Source: https://github.com/markup-carve/carve/blob/109597c5d6d37d4ea8f256fc854842816f1364df/spec/0.2/writer.md
text.carve://spec/README:
# Carve 0.2 specification

For existing documents and integrations, see [Upgrading from Carve 0.1](UPGRADING.md) and its [machine-readable upgrade map](data/upgrade-map.json).

This tree holds the specification of Carve 0.2, written fresh from the 0.2 rule set instead of edited from the 0.1 text.
It is a freeze candidate on the `next2` branch and is not released: [`STATUS.md`](STATUS.md) names the candidate and says what is frozen, what is provisional and what is still open. The reference engine is `carve-js` on the same branch name.
Documents: Syntax blocks (`syntax-blocks.md`, which includes tables), Syntax inline, HTML rendering, AST 2.0, extensions (`extensions.md`), the source-layout sidecar, Writer and fmt, and Includes (`includes.md`, prefix `C2-N-`), which defines include expansion.
The HTML import mapping (`import-html.md`, prefix `C2-M-`) defines how HTML without carriers becomes a tree.
Tooling (`tooling.md`, prefix `C2-T-`) defines the library calls and the command line every engine offers, with its flags, exit codes and reports.
Clause ids in this tree use a new prefix per document, starting with `C2-B-` for the block chapter, so that no 0.1 id is reused with a new meaning.
Every example of the ten documents is also an entry of the [conformance corpus](conformance/README.md), with the clause cases and the refused trees that engines test against; an example marked "unverified" has hand-written expected output.

Two edits on the same span produce `upgrade-conflict`; the lower entry ID wins. The tool reads only 0.1 source. **Run it once per 0.1 file. It is not idempotent.** Running it on a native 0.2 source, including the output of a first run, is outside its contract; a second run can change already upgraded list text. If HTML still differs and no U row maps the cause, the blocking `upgrade-mismatch` record has status `no mapped row` and the range of the differing 0.1 source. The file is not written. A mapped difference that cannot be verified retains its mapped row id and also blocks writing. ### Repository checklist 1. Make a copy or branch and inventory every `.crv` file, including generated and included documents. 2. Run `--check`, then `--json` for each file. Record all `report`, `upgrade-conflict`, and `upgrade-mismatch` entries. 3. Run `--write` once on the 0.1 files. Review every `SILENT` row above, especially list shape, punctuation, references, raw HTML, and host options. 4. Render representative pages with both engines. Compare selectors, generated ids, links, and page scripts. Review differences that the tool's normalized comparison hides, including attribute order and the `task` class. 5. Decide how the application will handle includes, lint, extensions, importers, and non-HTML output before switching its runtime. 6. Keep the upgraded source and the tool's JSON report together in review. # Carve 0.2: the AST, contract 2.0

Status: part of the freeze candidate of Carve 0.2 on `next2`, frozen with the rest of the core (`STATUS.md` names the candidate).

This document defines the tree a Carve 0.2 parser returns and its JSON form, which one implementation writes and another reads. It is ported from the contract 2.0 draft on the `next-ast2` branch (PART 12 of the 0.1 grammar, clauses CARVE-P12-nnn) and brought in line with the 0.2 syntax. Spelling that the draft kept in the tree lives in the source-layout sidecar, which has its own document (`source-layout.md`).

Conventions:

- A clause is a paragraph that starts with an id of the form `C2-A-nnn`. The prefix is new in 0.2. No 0.1 clause id is reused.
- `C2-B-nnn` and `C2-I-nnn` name clauses of the block and inline chapters, `C2-L-nnn` clauses of the source-layout document.
- The machine-readable form of this contract is `spec/0.2/data/ast-schema.json`. The schema and this document define the same 2.0 contract.
- JSON examples are complete, valid JSON. They leave out `pos` unless the example is about positions.
- A clause that starts with the word "Exception" is a carve-out from a more general clause.
- A *producer* writes a tree, a *reader* ingests one, a *writer* turns a tree into Carve source or another format.
- A *container* is a node that holds blocks: a quote, a list item, a description, a footnote, a div and its named kinds. A list, a description list and a table are not containers; they hold only their own member nodes.
- A *definition* is one of the four top-level definition nodes: a link, footnote, abbreviation or citation definition. The node type `definition_list` is the type of what the prose calls a description list.
- A *comment* is a `comment` node of any of its three forms. An *editorial comment* is a `critic_comment`.
- The *reference form* is the field `refForm` of a link or image written as a reference. The *display form* is the field `display` of an `xref`. The fields have separate names and meanings.
- Where a rule differs from the contract 2.0 draft on `next-ast2`, the section "Migration" says what a draft tree held. The clauses state the rule alone.

## Tree and sidecars

**C2-A-001** The tree holds meaning. A fact is a tree field only when it changes rendered output or a later resolution.

**C2-A-002** Spelling that changes neither is not in the tree. It is recorded in the source-layout sidecar (`source-layout.md`).

**C2-A-003** Source layout, node identity, annotation ranges and provenance are sidecars: each is returned only when the caller asks, validates against its own schema, addresses nodes by RFC 6901 pointers into the tree it came with, and is never placed inside the tree.

**C2-A-004** Two documents that differ only in sidecar content are the same document.

**C2-A-005** Diagnostics are not tree content either: they are one record beside the tree (C2-A-172).

**C2-A-006** The shape defined here is the interchange contract. An implementation whose internal tree differs maps it on output and does not export its internal shape.

**C2-A-007** Node type names and field names are spec surface. An implementation does not invent a synonym and does not publish a field this contract does not name.

## Root, envelope and versions

**C2-A-008** The root is a `document` node with block `children` and `astVersion` in the form `2.MINOR`, where MINOR is a non-negative decimal integer without a leading zero; a 2.0 producer writes `"2.0"`.

**C2-A-009** The root may carry `srcByteLength`, `extensions`, `stages`, `resources` and the common node fields (C2-A-027). No other root field is allowed.

**C2-A-010** `srcByteLength` is the measured number of source bytes, with zero for empty source and absence for unmeasured source. A reader with the source refuses a mismatched value; a reader without the source keeps it as supplied.

**C2-A-011** Document content does not hang off the root: frontmatter and definitions are nodes in `children`.

```json
{
  "type": "document",
  "astVersion": "2.0",
  "srcByteLength": 5,
  "children": [
    { "type": "paragraph", "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "Hello" }] }
  ]
}
```

**C2-A-012** At a storage or process boundary the tree travels inside an envelope with `astVersion` and `document`, and optionally `vocabulary` and `extensions`. An in-memory handoff and `carve ast` without `--envelope` use the bare tree. `vocabulary` is an object. An envelope field other than `astVersion`, `document`, `vocabulary` and `extensions` is refused, as an unknown field of a node is (C2-A-028).

**C2-A-013** The envelope and its `document` carry equal `astVersion` strings, and a reader refuses a pair that differs. The envelope does not change the tree.

**C2-A-217** `encodeTree` writes the JSON text of the JSON Canonicalization Scheme (RFC 8785): no whitespace, the members of every object in ascending order of their names compared as UTF-16 code units, and each string and number in the one spelling that scheme gives. So one tree has one encoding in every engine, and its `treeFingerprint` (C2-T-046) agrees across engines. A reader does not depend on that order: `decodeTree` reads the members of an object in any order (C2-A-188).

```json
{
  "astVersion": "2.0",
  "extensions": [{ "name": "org.example.notes", "version": "1", "required": false, "slots": [] }],
  "document": { "type": "document", "astVersion": "2.0", "children": [] }
}
```

**C2-A-014** `astVersion` is `major.minor` and versions this contract, not the language. A leading zero is refused. Until the 0.2.0 release, contract 2.0 may still change; the rules of this section on what a version may change apply from that release on.

**C2-A-015** A major version may remove, rename or reinterpret a field or a node type. Every major version ships a migration function from the previous major version (C2-A-176).

**C2-A-016** A minor version adds only three things: optional declared extensions, extension nodes with a fallback, and namespaced `data`. It adds no core field and no core node type. A new construct therefore enters as an extension node with a fallback, and is promoted to a core node at the next major version.

**C2-A-017** An extension declaration has a qualified `name`, a boolean `required`, a nonempty `version` and `slots`, an ordered list of distinct slot names. The names in one list of declarations are distinct, and a reader refuses a list that holds one name twice. A reader matches the version as an exact string under C2-X-003. If both the root and envelope declare one name, their version, required flag and ordered slots agree.

**C2-A-018** A reader refuses a higher major version, an unknown required extension, an unknown core field, an unknown core node type and an extension node without a valid fallback.

**C2-A-019** A reader accepts every minor version of major 2 that it can read under the additions allowed by C2-A-016.

## Node grammar

**C2-A-021** Every node is a JSON object with a `type` that holds its node type name.

**C2-A-022** `children` is the primary content slot of every node that holds other nodes.

**C2-A-023** `value` is the literal payload of a node that holds text: `text`, `code`, `code_block`, `math`, `raw_block`, `raw_inline`, `literal_inline`, `comment`, `critic_comment` and `frontmatter`.

**C2-A-024** Named child slots are `caption`, `short`, `prefix`, `locator.children`, `suffix`, `pairs`, `base`, `annotation`, `title`, `longDescription`, `columns`, `fallback`, extension `slots`, and the node-bearing metadata keys of C2-A-030 and C2-A-212. Each slot has its content kind and walk order in `spec/0.2/data/node-slots.json` and, for extensions, the tree declaration.

**C2-A-025** A walker visits the slots in `spec/0.2/data/node-slots.json` order, including typed metadata. It visits extension slots in the order of the root or envelope declaration, without a registry. It visits recursive metadata value slots as described by `data/node-slots.json`. It never searches opaque `data` or extension `props` for nodes. Resolution visits `title`, then `children`, then `caption` in source order (C2-L-011), and skips the caption of an expanded include (C2-N-074). Caption and equation numbers are assigned when their owner is visited (C2-H-170), and footnote numbers and ids follow the same order (C2-H-087), so a footnote reference in the title of a div is numbered before one in its children; for all three the document body is visited before the footnote bodies, in the order of the footnote numbers (C2-H-087, C2-H-150).

**C2-A-026** `spec/0.2/data/node-slots.json` is generated from `spec/0.2/data/ast-schema.json` and `data/extensions.json`. It names every node-bearing child slot and its walk order.

**C2-A-027** Every typed node may carry the common fields `attrs`, `data`, `pos`, `segments`, `metadata`, `dir` and `lang`, as far as its schema definition allows.

**C2-A-028** Nodes are closed: a reader refuses a field the schema does not name on a node type (C2-A-167). Unknown fields inside `task`, `marker`, a payload alternative or a manifest entry are refused as well.

**C2-A-029** Every `data` key has the qualified grammar of C2-A-123, matches a declaration on the root or envelope, and holds opaque JSON. A reader preserves unknown optional data and refuses a node anywhere inside it.

**C2-A-030** `metadata` is a closed object with optional `title` and `subtitle` inline lists, `authors` as strings, `date` as a string, and `bibliography` as the typed object of C2-A-121. Root metadata also admits `abstract` as blocks, `keywords` as strings, `fields` as named metadata values, and `headers` and `footers`. Each header or footer is a closed object with `placement` set to `default`, `first` or `even` and a `children` slot of blocks. A walker visits every declared metadata slot. Extension `props` is opaque JSON. A reader refuses a node inside `metadata` outside a declared slot or inside `props`.

**C2-A-031** `dir` is `ltr`, `rtl` or `auto`. `dir` and `lang` are inherited from the nearest ancestor that carries them.

### Attributes

**C2-A-032** `attrs` holds the attribute blocks attached to a node: an optional single `id`, an ordered `classes` list and `keyValues`, an ordered list of pairs. Each pair is a list of two strings, the key and its value, and the pairs stand in written order. A bare key has the empty string as its value.

**C2-A-033** The tree records no order between the kinds of parts. The written order is fixed: the id, then the classes as written, then the language, then the keys as written (C2-B-098).

**C2-A-034** A key named `id` or `class`, in any ASCII letter case, is not a member of `keyValues`: it folds into `id` or `classes` when the block is parsed, and of several ids the last one written wins (C2-B-104).

**C2-A-035** Glued attribute blocks and consecutive attribute lines are merged before the tree is built: classes add up, and a later key replaces an earlier key of the same name (C2-B-093, C2-I-039). Names are the same when they agree without regard to ASCII letter case, within one block as across merged blocks. On a span, the lowercase semantic keys `abbr`, `time` and `kbd` are distinct from spellings of those names in another case; those other spellings are ordinary keys and merge with each other by the general case-insensitive rule (C2-H-013, C2-H-075). On every other node, all spellings of each name merge by the general rule. A key occurs once in `keyValues`, at the place and in the spelling where it was first written, with the value written last. A reader refuses a supplied `keyValues` that holds two keys of one name, or a key that is no key by C2-I-030.

**C2-A-036** A reader never looks for nodes inside `keyValues`: `{type=widget}` is an ordinary attribute.

**C2-A-037** The language part of an attribute block sets the node field `lang` and is not a key: `{:en}` is the shorthand for `lang: "en"` on the node. A writer puts it after the classes.

**C2-A-038** `attrs.id` holds only an id the author wrote. A generated heading id is not stored there (C2-A-134).

**C2-A-039** `attrs.id` is an anchor in the document. For a duplicate id the first node in document order wins, and the producer reports each later one with the rule `duplicate-id`, whatever the node type. An id in the view of an extension node that resolution does not visit (C2-X-032) is no anchor and is not compared.

```json
{
  "type": "span",
  "attrs": { "id": "a", "classes": ["x", "y"], "keyValues": [["data-n", "1"], ["hidden", ""]] },
  "lang": "en",
  "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "t" }]
}
```

## Text and literal payload

**C2-A-040** A node list holds no two adjacent `text` nodes. Adjacent runs are joined in the tree that `parse` returns, not in the encoder.

**C2-A-041** A backslash escape is not a node. The escaped character is part of the surrounding `text` value, and a writer computes the escapes it needs.

**C2-A-042** An escaped space is a `non_breaking_space` node with no value. One node stands for one space.

**C2-A-043** Every string field holds literal Unicode. No private-use character has a special meaning, and a temporary marker of a parser or writer is never published.

**C2-A-044** A reader replaces every U+0000 in an ingested string with U+FFFD before it uses the value.

**C2-A-045** `code_block.value` holds every payload character, the final line break included. A closed fence with one line `a` has the value `"a\n"`, and a closed fence with no line has `""`. Container prefixes and fence delimiters are not payload.

**C2-A-046** The value of a parsed fence ends with a line break after its last line, also where the fence is unclosed and the source ends on that line without one: the end of the source counts as a line ending. A producer adds nothing else.

**C2-A-047** A built or imported code block may hold `"a"` with no final break, which is a different value from `"a\n"`. A reader does not append a break.

**C2-A-048** `raw_block.value` follows the same rules as `code_block.value`.

**C2-A-049** `frontmatter` is the first child when present, of the document or of an include whose selection takes the frontmatter of its file (C2-N-021). It carries `format`, which is the word on its opener or `"yaml"` when there is none, and `value`, the text between the delimiters as written, which ends with a line break after its last line also where the block is unclosed and the source ends there without one (C2-A-046). A producer does not publish parsed keys in its place.
