Each stands at its place in source order among the other blocks; no definition is moved or collected. A reader refuses one inside a container.

## Blocks

### Lists and tasks

**C2-A-053** A `list` carries `children` of `list_item` nodes, one `marker` object and `spacing`.

**C2-A-054** A bullet marker is `{"kind": "bullet", "char": c}` where `c` is `-` or `*`.

**C2-A-056** An ordered marker has `kind: "ordered"`, `style` (`1`, `a`, `A`, `i` or `I`) and `delimiter` (`.` or `)`), and may carry `start`, an integer from 0 to 999999999 (C2-B-219); a reader refuses another value. Whether the author wrote numbers or the bare dot is spelling and is not in the marker.

**C2-A-058** `marker.start` is omitted when it is 1, and a reader refuses `start: 1` in a supplied tree instead of normalizing it. A default has one encoding everywhere: a reader refuses `mode: "normal"` on a citation (C2-A-120), an autolink `text` equal to its `href` (C2-A-216), and an empty `attrs`, `classes` or `keyValues`, and an empty `props`, `slots`, `payload` or `resourceIds` of an extension node (C2-X-037). An ordered marker always carries `style` and `delimiter` (C2-A-056).

**C2-A-059** `list.spacing` is `tight` or `loose` and is set when the list closes (C2-B-062). No list attribute overrides it.

**C2-A-060** A task item carries `task`, a closed object with only `mark`. `mark` is one of the eight characters space, `x`, `_`, `-`, `/`, `!`, `>` and `?`; a parsed `X` becomes `x`.

**C2-A-061** A consumer derives task status from `mark` using `data/task-states.json`; `status` is never stored in the 2.0 tree. This replaces the earlier draft pair of `mark` and `status`.

```json
{
  "type": "list",
  "marker": { "kind": "ordered", "style": "1", "delimiter": ".", "start": 2 },
  "spacing": "tight",
  "children": [
    {
      "type": "list_item",
      "children": [{ "type": "paragraph", "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "a" }] }]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Description lists

**C2-A-062** A `definition_list` holds `definition_term`, `definition_description` and source `comment` nodes in document order. A term holds inlines and a description holds blocks.

**C2-A-063** The grouping of terms and descriptions is not published. A run of terms belongs to the descriptions that follow it.

**C2-A-064** A `definition_list` has no `spacing` field. A renderer reads the blocks of each description (C2-B-073, C2-B-077).

### Quotes, divs and their sigil forms

**C2-A-065** A quote is a `block_quote` with block `children`, whether it was written with `>` lines or as a quote fence. Which of the two the author wrote is not in the tree.

**C2-A-066** The name of a div opener decides its node type as C2-B-127 and `data/div-names.json` say: an admonition name gives an `admonition` and a directive name a `directive`, each with the name as its `kind`, a figure group a `figure_group`, and every other name, or none, a `div`, with its classes in the order of C2-B-128.

**C2-A-067** A `directive` always carries `children` and may carry a `title` and `tocTarget` (`headings`, `figures`, `tables` or `listings`).

**C2-A-068** A hard-break block is not a node type and not a field. It is a `div` with the class `hardbreaks` in which every line end is a `hard_break` node. The opener form adds the class after the classes the author wrote, so it comes last in `attrs.classes`; the class form has it where it was written. The two forms give the same tree when `hardbreaks` is the last class. Which form the author wrote is in the sidecar.

**C2-A-069** A line block is a `line_block` whose `children` are `line` nodes, one per line of its body in order, and the `comment` of each comment block in it at its place (C2-B-123). A `line` holds inline `children`. An empty line of the body is a `line` with no children, and it ends a stanza. A line that holds only a braced comment is a `line` that holds the comment.

```json
{
  "type": "div",
  "attrs": { "classes": ["hardbreaks"] },
  "children": [
    {
      "type": "paragraph",
      "children": [
        { "type": "text", "value": "a" },
        { "type": "hard_break" },
        { "type": "text", "value": "b" }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

### Headings, thematic breaks and code

**C2-A-070** A `heading` carries `level` and inline `children`, which hold a `soft_break` or a `hard_break` where the heading continues on a further line (C2-B-154). The marker character is not recorded in the tree, and the formatter writes `=`.

**C2-A-071** `heading.level` is an integer of at least 1, and a reader refuses a smaller value. Carve source gives 1 to 6, and an imported tree may hold more (C2-H-021).

**C2-A-072** A `thematic_break` has no fields of its own: 0.2 has one spelling, the star run.

**C2-A-073** A `code_block` carries `value` and may carry `syntax`, the language word, and `title`, a list of inlines. A parsed `title` is one `text` node that holds the quoted value read as in C2-I-033; it is not inline-parsed, so `"src/*a*"` gives the text `src/*a*`. The fence character and the fence length are not in the tree.

### Comments

**C2-A-074** A `comment` carries `value` and `form`, which is `block` for a `%%%` block, `line` for a `%%` comment and `braced` for `{% %}`. `form` is meaning: a line comment and a comment block read differently when the source is parsed again. `value` of a line comment is its text without the one space that follows `%%`, when there is one, and without spaces and tabs at its end, also where the comment ends at the pipe of a cell (C2-B-169, C2-B-223); `value` of a braced comment is its text without the one space after `{%` and the one space before `%}`, when there are such spaces; `value` of a block comment is its body, with a line break between two lines and none after the last.

The comment of a comment-only line belongs to the open leaf, if any, or else to the innermost open container (C2-B-138).

### Definitions

**C2-A-077** A `link_reference_definition` carries a folded `key` (C2-A-104), `namespace: "link"`, `href` and optional `tooltip`. A parsed tree never holds an empty `href`; a supplied one is unspellable and the Carve writer reports it.

**C2-A-078** A `footnote` carries `key`, `namespace: "footnote"` and block `children`.

**C2-A-079** An `abbreviation_def` carries `key`, `namespace: "abbr"` and `expansion`.

**C2-A-080** Definitions are nodes with a position, so document order decides which of two definitions wins: the first one (C2-B-085).

### Figures and captions

**C2-A-081** A caption is a `caption` node with block `children` and an optional inline `short`. A producer does not derive `short` from the full caption.

**C2-A-082** In 0.2 a caption attaches to an image, a table, a code block, a quote, a math block or a figure group (C2-B-147). Each of them carries its caption in its own `caption` slot: the `paragraph` of a block image or a math block, the `code_block`, the `block_quote`, the `table` and the `figure_group`. The parser makes no wrapper. A reader refuses a `caption` on a paragraph whose `role` is neither `image` nor `math`. The comment of a comment-only line between a block and its caption (C2-B-137) is placed by C2-B-138: below a block image or a math block it is a child of that paragraph, which is still open, and below a quote a child of the quote's open leaf or of the quote. For a figure group it is the last child of the group, and for a table the last child of the table. Below a code block, which holds no children, it is the sibling after the block (C2-A-145).

**C2-A-084** A `figure_group` carries block `children` in source order and an optional `caption`, the caption of the group. Its panels are the tables among its children, and the image paragraphs, code blocks, quotes and math blocks among them that carry a caption; there is no separate panel list.

```json
{
  "type": "figure_group",
  "children": [],
  "caption": {
    "type": "caption",
    "children": [{ "type": "paragraph", "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "Two views" }] }]
  }
}
```

### Tables

**C2-A-086** A `table` carries `children` that are `table_head`, `table_body` and `table_foot` nodes, and after them the comment of a comment-only line that stands below the last row and not before a continuation of that row, with or without a caption below it (C2-A-082). The groups stand in this order: at most one `table_head`, then the `table_body` nodes, then at most one `table_foot`, and a reader refuses another order or count. Each group holds `table_row` nodes and each row holds `table_cell` nodes. There is no flat row list and no count object. The comment of a comment-only line between two rows (C2-B-137) is a `comment` node among the rows of its group, at its place in source order. It belongs to the group of the row above it, so a comment between the last head row and the first body row is the last child of the head. A `table_head` and a `table_foot` admit a `comment` among their rows as a `table_body` does. The trailing line comment of a row (C2-B-167) is a `comment` node at the place that a comment-only line directly below that row would take: among the rows of the row's group, directly after the row, or, after the last row of the table, as the comment after the groups. The row then ends at its closing pipe or its row attribute, and the comment spans from the first space before its `%%` to the line ending (C2-A-151). For `| 1 | 2 | %% note`, a line feed and `| 3 | 4 |`, the body holds the first row, the comment `note` and the second row, and the first row spans offsets 0 to 9. A comment between a row and its continuation row (C2-B-175), as a comment-only line or as the trailing comment of the row, belongs to the row's group, directly after the row, because the continuation is part of that row (C2-B-184); a continued row has no `pos` (C2-A-158), so the comment overlaps no sibling. For `| a |`, `%% x` and `+ b |` on three lines, the body holds the row `a b` and then the comment `x`, and the table holds no comment after its groups.

**C2-A-088** The partition of a table into head, body and foot is held by its groups alone: the `table_head`, `table_body` and `table_foot` nodes and the rows each holds. No node carries a count of head rows. `rowHeadColumns` of a `table_body` is the number of its leading columns whose cells are row headers (C2-B-230). A `header-rows` attribute that set the partition is spelling, recorded in the layout sidecar (C2-L-057), so a pipe table and a delimited table with the same cells in the same groups are equal trees (C2-L-023).

**C2-A-089** A table has `columns` of `table_column` nodes. Each column keeps authored `align` beside result `resolvedAlign` and authored `valign` beside result `resolvedValign`; it may also hold `width` (C2-B-211 to C2-B-213). `resolvedAlign` is the horizontal mark of the last header cell in the head that starts in that column and carries one (C2-B-182, C2-B-213), or else the authored `align` from the `aligns` attribute, and `resolvedValign` is the vertical mark of the last such cell that carries one, or else the authored `valign` from the `valigns` attribute. A cell mark overrides the resolved column alignment for that cell.

**C2-A-091** `table_cell.children` is always a list of blocks. A cell written in a pipe table holds one `cell_paragraph` with inline `children`, which renders without a paragraph element. An imported cell may hold other blocks. A reader refuses a cell with no children that carries no `span`, and a `cell_paragraph` that is not the only child of its cell; a span mark cell has no children (C2-A-092).

**C2-A-092** A cell carries `header` and may carry authored `span`, resolved `colspan` and `rowspan`, `align`, `valign`, `scope` and `headerIds`. Each present count is an integer of at least 1, and a reader refuses a smaller value. `valign` is one of `top`, `middle`, `bottom` and `baseline`, and a reader refuses another value. `scope` is one of `row`, `col`, `rowgroup` and `colgroup`; `headerIds` is an ordered list of `attrs.id` values of header cells, and a reader refuses a missing or nonheader target. A parse of Carve source produces neither accessibility field. A span mark that joins nothing leaves an ordinary cell that holds the mark as text (C2-B-173); a valid mark cell stays empty and spans the text between its pipes (C2-A-158), with `header` false since its prefix is not kept (C2-B-174), while the covering cell carries the count.

**C2-A-093** A supplied count that contradicts an authored `span` mark is refused; a parser derives counts from marks according to C2-B-172 to C2-B-174. A `rowspan` that reaches past the last row of its cell's group, head, body or foot, is refused too, since no span crosses a group (C2-B-174). The mark decides the effective span, and counts without a mark describe an imported span. Column `align` is authored and `resolvedAlign` is derived under C2-A-089 and C2-B-213.

**C2-A-094** A continuation row leaves no node and no field. Each fragment is read as inline content by itself, and the cell holds the nodes of its fragments in order with one space of ordinary text between two fragments (C2-B-184). Where the row broke is spelling and is in the sidecar.

**C2-A-095** A table has no field for the widths of a separator row, since 0.2 has no such row; no field for the kind of source content of a cell, since `cell_paragraph` says it; no field for whether it was written as a pipe table or a delimited table, which is spelling; and no field for whether the source spelled a column, which its `align` and `width` say (C2-B-211, C2-B-212).

```json
{
  "type": "table",
  "columns": [{ "type": "table_column", "align": "right" }],
  "children": [
    {
      "type": "table_body",
      "children": [
        {
          "type": "table_row",
          "children": [
            {
              "type": "table_cell",
              "header": false,
              "children": [
                { "type": "cell_paragraph", "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "1" }] }
              ]
            }
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Inline nodes

**C2-A-096** `emphasis` and `strong` nest in the order written. There is no combined token and no field for one.

**C2-A-097** A replacement is a `delete` node directly followed by an `insert` node (C2-I-062). There is no `critic_substitution` node.

```json
{
  "type": "paragraph",
  "children": [
    { "type": "delete", "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "old" }] },
    { "type": "insert", "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "new" }] }
  ]
}
```

**C2-A-098** A `smart_punctuation` node carries `kind`, `source`, the characters as typed, and `glyph`, the glyph that `data/smart-punctuation.json` gives its kind; a reader refuses another glyph, and a `source` other than the one the table gives the kind. `source` stays in the tree, because a renderer with `smartTypography` off prints it. The `kind` of a smart punctuation node is one of the kinds of `data/smart-punctuation.json`; a reader refuses any other value.

**C2-A-099** A line break inside a leaf is a `soft_break` or a `hard_break`. Neither has a value.

**C2-A-100** An `inline_footnote` holds its content in `children` and may carry `number` as a resolution result.

**C2-A-101** A `mention` carries `kind`, `target` and an optional visible `label`. Parsing `@name` gives the `kind` `user`, the name as `target` and no `label`; another kind and a label come from an extension or a supplied tree. A `tag` and a `symbol` carry `name`.

**C2-A-102** A `math` node carries `value` and `display`. A display equation may carry `numberPrefix`, and result `number` only together with it: a reader refuses `number` without `numberPrefix`, and either field on inline math.

### References

**C2-A-103** A reference use and a definition carry `key` and `namespace` together. The namespaces are `link`, `footnote`, `citation`, `abbr` and `heading`. A direct link or image carries neither.

**C2-A-104** `key` is the folded label: every run of spaces, tabs and line breaks becomes one space, the ends are trimmed, and case is kept (C2-I-079). Uses and definitions fold the same way, so two keys match when they are equal strings.

**C2-A-105** A reference `link` or `image` carries `refForm`, `full`, `collapsed` or `shortcut`, exactly when it carries `key`. This field records reference spelling separately from cross-reference display. The verbatim text is in the sidecar.

**C2-A-106** The tree is pre-resolve. A resolution result is added beside the authored construct and never replaces it.

**C2-A-107** On a reference use an absent `href` or `src` means unresolved, and the empty string means a destination that is empty. There is no `resolved` field.

**C2-A-108** An unresolved full or collapsed reference remains a `link` or `image` with its `children` or `alt`, `key`, `refForm` and `attrs`; it never becomes text. HTML renders its brackets and label as literal text. A shortcut forms only for a defined key and is therefore never unresolved when parsed from source.

**C2-A-109** A link reference is looked up in the link definitions first and then in the headings (C2-I-081, C2-I-083, C2-I-084). The heading lookup applies to link references only, not to images and not to footnotes. It compares plain text that the tree alone gives, so it needs no source. Its result is an `href` on the link, like any other resolution.

**C2-A-110** A trailing attribute block on a reference is ordinary `attrs`, resolved or not. The reference node keeps only its own authored attributes. The merge with the attributes of its link definition (C2-I-082) is a resolution result: it is not written into `attrs` and takes no part in equality.

```json
{
  "type": "link",
  "key": "getting started",
  "namespace": "link",
  "refForm": "collapsed",
  "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "getting started" }]
}
```

**C2-A-111** A link or an autolink inside link text stays a node in the tree. A renderer unwraps it.

**C2-A-112** `href`, `src` and every other destination hold what the author wrote. A producer does not blank or rewrite a destination on the way into the tree.

**C2-A-113** A consumer that puts a destination into a URL sink applies the URL policy itself. The tree may hold `javascript:alert(1)`.

**C2-A-114** A link or image may carry `targetKind` (`url`, `wiki`, `doc` or `xref`) for a target that is not a URL.

**C2-A-115** An `image` may carry `alt`, `decorative`, `tooltip`, `resourceId` and `longDescription`, a list of blocks. `decorative: true` requires `alt` to be absent, and an absent `alt` requires `decorative: true`; a reader refuses either contradictory pair. A parse of Carve source produces no `longDescription` or `decorative` field. A resolved reference takes its tooltip from its definition.

**C2-A-116** An `xref` carries `key`, `namespace`, and optional `display` (`number`, `page`, `title` or `full`); resolution may add `href`. The `display` field records cross-reference display separately from reference spelling. A Carve writer reports `display` as unspellable (C2-I-096). A parsed `xref` always carries the namespace `heading`, read as the namespace of the document's ids, which numbered captions share (C2-H-095): the parse does not know whether the key names a heading or a caption.

**C2-A-117** A `footnote_ref` carries `key` and `namespace: "footnote"`, and `number` once resolved. An `abbreviation` carries `key` and `namespace: "abbr"`, and may carry `expansion`.

### Citations

**C2-A-118** A `citation_group` carries `children` of `citation` nodes and `raw`. A `citation` occurs nowhere else.

**C2-A-119** `citation_group.raw` is the bracket text as written. It stays in the tree, because it is what renders when a key has no entry. Core has no citation spelling (C2-I-101): where no extension handles citations, HTML writes `raw` as text and a `citation_definition` writes nothing, and a Carve writer writes `raw` and reports `structure-unspellable` for a `citation_definition`.

**C2-A-120** A citation item has optional `mode` from the closed set `normal`, `author-in-text` and `suppress-author`, matching the three Pandoc citation modes; absence means `normal`, which is never written (C2-A-058). A group has no mode, and an item has no separate author-suppression flag. A locator is one object with optional string `label` and required inline `children`; the earlier `locatorLabel` and `locatorValue` fields are refused.

**C2-A-121** A `citation_definition` carries `key`, `namespace: "citation"`, inline `children` and optional typed `metadata.bibliography`, not bibliographic attributes. Bibliography may hold `title` and `containerTitle` as inline lists, `authors` as a list of strings, and `issued`, `doi` and `url` as strings; other keys are refused. This replaces the earlier draft use of `attrs` for bibliography facts.

## Extension nodes, foreign data and resources

**C2-A-122** `block_extension` and `inline_extension` carry `name`, a nonempty `version` that a qualified name requires, opaque JSON `props`, `children`, optional named `slots`, a fallback that a qualified name requires, optional `payload`, and optional `source` under C2-X-024. Each payload alternative has exactly nonempty string `format` and non-null JSON `value`; unknown fields are refused. The `children` of a qualified extension node are content for its renderer, as a slot is (C2-X-032); without the renderer only the fallback and the source record are read (C2-X-027, C2-X-028, C2-X-035). The 8 MiB limit of C2-A-132 counts a string value in UTF-8 bytes and another value in UTF-8 JSON bytes. This replaces the earlier version and source-field shape.

**C2-A-123** A qualified name has the grammar `namespace.name`, with each segment matching `[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_-]*` and one or more dot-separated namespace segments. A qualified extension node is declared by the full name on the root or envelope and carries a same-role fallback, whether it is inline or block. This closes the earlier draft dot-only test.

**C2-A-124** A name without a dot is the name of an inline extension written in Carve source when no declared matcher claims it. `:kbd[Ctrl]` gives `"name": "kbd"`, needs no declaration, and its `children` are its fallback. Such a node carries `name`, `children` and the common fields, and a reader refuses any other field on it. A matcher may transform that core node to a qualified extension under C2-X-006.

**C2-A-125** A `block_extension` has a qualified name and a mandatory fallback. A 0.2.0 transform may produce one from a core div or code block under C2-X-008 to C2-X-011. This replaces the earlier phase 6 deferral and the prohibition on produced block extensions.

**C2-A-128** Reading a tree never runs anything in `payload`, `props` or `data`. An application enables active content only through a separate capability outside this contract.

```json
{
  "type": "inline_extension",
  "name": "kbd",
  "children": [{ "type": "text", "value": "Ctrl" }]
}
```

**C2-A-129** A foreign construct with a core equivalent maps to core nodes. One without may be carried in declared `data` or in an extension with a fallback. A writer that cannot carry it reports the loss with its JSON path.

**C2-A-130** The contract promises semantic interchange. It does not promise an editable round trip for a foreign format, and it does not promise that source spelling survives in the tree.

**C2-A-131** `document.resources` is a manifest of closed entries with `id`, `mediaType`, `digest` in `sha256:` plus 64 lowercase hex digits, and optional `href` and `size`. `size` is a non-negative integer of bytes. A missing or duplicate referenced id is refused; unknown entry fields are refused rather than kept. This closes the earlier draft open entry shape.

**C2-A-132** A reader bounds a decoded extension payload to 8 MiB per node, metadata value nesting to 64 levels, resource references to 4096 per tree and fallback nesting to 32 unqualified inline extension nodes, and refuses an excess.

## Resolution results

**C2-A-133** Resolution results remain in the tree beside authored fields. `spec/0.2/data/ast-results.json` is the complete per-type list of result fields, including generated ids, resolved destinations, numbers, alignment, derived span counts and root `stages`.

**C2-A-134** A generated heading id is a resolution result. It is published in the heading field `generatedId` and never in `attrs.id`.

**C2-A-135** The root `stages` list names the resolution stages that ran: `includeExpansion` (C2-N-006), `referenceResolution` and `tableAlignment`. A producer names a stage only when its results are complete. A renderer runs reference resolution and table alignment on every tree it is given and overwrites every result field of `data/ast-results.json` except the fields of `include`: it never reads such a field from the tree, and `stages` lets it skip no stage. The fields of an expanded include are kept (C2-N-075).

**C2-A-136** A block image is a `paragraph` containing one `image` and any following comment-only lines, with `role: "image"`. A parser sets the role on close (C2-B-157, C2-B-191), and an ordinary paragraph omits it. A wrapped reference label that covers two lines remains ordinary (C2-B-197). The `role` is a tree fact used by equality.

## Positions

**C2-A-138** Every node of a tree that a parser built from source carries `pos`, except the root and the node types of C2-A-158. A parser builds positions unless the caller asks for a tree without them; a tree built that way omits `pos` on every node and is otherwise the same. Rendering from source needs no positions and builds none, unless `sourceLines` is on.

**C2-A-139** A node that has no position omits `pos`. `pos` is never `null`, and a producer never invents a range.

**C2-A-140** `pos` has six required integers: `startLine`, `endLine`, `startColumn`, `endColumn`, `startOffset` and `endOffset`.

**C2-A-141** Lines and columns start at 1, offsets start at 0, and a reader refuses a smaller value. Columns count Unicode code points, offsets count original UTF-8 bytes, and ends are exclusive.

**C2-A-142** `pos.file`, when present, is a string id of the included input whose coordinates are measured. Absence means the top-level input; positions in different files are never compared. In an expanded tree the id is the `file` of the include whose children hold the node (C2-N-019).

```json
{
  "type": "text",
  "value": "é!",
  "pos": {
    "startLine": 1, "endLine": 1,
    "startColumn": 3, "endColumn": 5,
    "startOffset": 2, "endOffset": 5
  }
}
```

The invariants below are written so that a test can check each one on any tree and its source.

**C2-A-143** For every `pos`, `startOffset` is not greater than `endOffset`, and line and column are the line and column of the offset in the source.

**C2-A-144** A child lies inside its parent: its `startOffset` is not before the parent's and its `endOffset` is not after it. A node without `pos` is skipped, and its children are compared with the nearest ancestor that has one.

**C2-A-145** Siblings are ordered and disjoint: for two nodes `a` before `b` in one node list, `a.endOffset` is not greater than `b.startOffset`. Nodes without `pos` are skipped. Two cases are exempt: the comment of a comment-only line that stands between an attribute line and the block that takes it (C2-B-137) lies inside the span of that block (C2-A-148) and is its sibling before it, and the comment of a comment-only line between a code block and its caption lies inside the span of the code block (C2-A-154) and is its sibling after it (C2-A-082).

**Exception C2-A-146** Two breaks that meet at one line ending share it, against C2-A-145.

**C2-A-148** A span starts at the markup that opens the construct: the quote mark, the heading marker, the list marker, the colon run of a div, the opening bracket of a link, the backtick run of a fence. Leading indent on the opening line is outside the span, of a container as of a leaf: in ` > a` the quote starts at its mark, offset 1. A block that took attribute lines (C2-B-091) starts at the first of them.

**Exception C2-A-149** A table cell does not start at its opening markup, against C2-A-148: it spans the text between its pipes.

**C2-A-150** No span starts at a line ending, except the span of a `soft_break` or a `hard_break`.

**C2-A-151** A span ends directly after the last source character the construct owns. A closing delimiter and an attached attribute block are inside; a following line ending, a blank line and an attribute line that attached to nothing are outside. The spaces and tabs at the end of a line always have an owner. At the end of a block's last line they belong to the block, which ends at the line ending, an include and a heading as every other block; the padding of a cell belongs to the cell (C2-A-149). Inside a content they belong to the node that drops them (C2-I-002), on the last line of the content as on the others: to a line comment at the end of the line, which starts at the first space or tab before its `%%` and ends at the line ending, and otherwise to the break that follows them (C2-A-153). A node that holds text ends after its last kept character. For `a %% x`, two spaces, a line feed and `b`, the paragraph spans offsets 0 to 10, the comment 1 to 8 and the soft break 8 to 9; for `{{ a.crv }}` and two spaces, the include spans 0 to 13.

**C2-A-152** A break owns its line ending, so its end is column 1 of the next line. A hard break also spans its backslash. A hard break at the end of the content with no line ending after it, as at the end of a table cell (C2-I-102), spans its backslash only.

**C2-A-153** A break that a parser makes from a plain line ending, with no backslash in the source, has a span: the spaces and tabs that C2-I-002 drops before the line ending and no line comment owns (C2-A-151), and the line ending itself. It starts directly after the last kept character of its line, so for `a`, two spaces, a line feed and `b` the soft break spans offsets 1 to 4. A hard break spans the same and its backslash (C2-A-152). It is not among the nodes that omit `pos`.

**C2-A-154** A container, a list, a description list and a table end after their closer when they have one, and otherwise after their last child that has a position. Each starts at its opening markup and ends at its closing markup also when its first or last child has no position. A block that carries a caption, a figure group and a table included, ends where its caption ends, and the caption spans from its caret to the end of its last line (C2-A-151).

**C2-A-155** A container with no positioned child spans its own opening markup and is not zero-width.

**C2-A-156** A node whose value is not one contiguous slice of the source omits `pos`. A span over the first piece, or from the first piece to the last, is not an alternative.

**C2-A-157** Such a node may carry `segments`, a list of ranges in the shape of `pos`, one per source piece in order.

**C2-A-158** In a tree a parser built from source, a node omits `pos` only when it has no source character or when its value is not one contiguous slice of the source (C2-A-156). Nodes with no source character are `table_column`, the `cell_paragraph` of an empty cell and a `line` with no children (C2-A-069). Nodes that are not one slice are a `table_row`, a `table_cell` and a `cell_paragraph` that a continuation row joined, an inline node of such a cell that takes characters from more than one of its pieces, the delimited table cases of C2-A-215, a `text` node merged from pieces that are not adjacent in the source, and the copy of a caption that an expanded code include gives its child, with every node inside it (C2-N-073). Every other node carries `pos`. An empty cell and a cell that holds a span mark span the text between their pipes (C2-A-149), so in `| a | |` the second cell spans offsets 5 to 6. A `caption_number` spans its `#`, and the text on each side of it spans its own characters: for `![i](a.png)`, a line feed and `^ Figure #: cap`, the text `Figure ` spans offsets 14 to 21, the number 21 to 22 and the text `: cap` 22 to 27.

**C2-A-159** A node of a tree that was built or imported without Carve source has no position and omits `pos`. The types `section`, `ruby`, `ruby_pair` and `small_caps` have no source spelling and are never positioned by a parser. A block extension transformed from source takes the claimed core node's position.

**C2-A-160** A node that a producer has not placed yet is a defect, not a case of C2-A-158.

## Equality

**C2-A-161** Two trees are equal when their node types, fields, node-list order, `attrs`, typed `metadata` and opaque `data` agree after text coalescing (C2-A-040), except the fields listed in `spec/0.2/data/ast-results.json` and source geometry in C2-A-162.

**C2-A-162** Equality skips `pos`, `segments`, `srcByteLength`, and exactly the resolution fields listed in `spec/0.2/data/ast-results.json`; a span count is skipped only when derived from an authored mark. `paragraph.role` is compared (C2-A-136).

**C2-A-165** `parse(x)`, encoded to JSON and decoded, equals `parse(x)` in every field, positions included. An encoder that drops a field is not conformant.

## Reading a tree

**C2-A-167** Where this document says a reader refuses, it fails with a typed, documented error that names what was wrong and the path of the node. It does not truncate, repair, drop or crash, and it does not surface the error of a JSON library.

**C2-A-168** A reader refuses a root that lacks `type`, `children` or `astVersion`, and a root whose `type` is not `document`.

**C2-A-170** A reader validates a tree against `spec/0.2/data/ast-schema.json` at decode and refuses a failure. The files under `resources/` describe the 0.1 contract.

**C2-A-171** A reader accepts every tree its own parser can produce at the two nesting limits, 200 blocks (C2-B-190) and 200 inline levels in each inline content (C2-I-118), and refuses deeper input. The levels are counted within each file: the children of an expanded include start again at level 0 (C2-N-015), so one chain of includes may hold the top-level document and 16 included files (C2-N-064), each as deep as the limits allow. It derives its bound from the limits by the worst cost per level of its own encoding.

## Diagnostics

**C2-A-172** A parse, a render, a write and a lint run report into one diagnostics record that sits beside the tree. Nothing in the tree marks a node as diagnosed.

**C2-A-173** Every entry of the record has a code, a severity, a position, a message and a channel (C2-W-103). The channel is `parse`, `render-loss` or `lint`, and a code belongs to one channel (C2-W-104). The position is an optional range in UTF-8 bytes and an optional RFC 6901 path into the tree, so a finding on a tree with no source has the path alone. An entry of the HTML importer is positioned in the bytes of its HTML input and may also carry `foreignType`, the name of the HTML node it is about (C2-M-081).

**C2-A-174** The record replaces the separate callbacks, warning lists and render-loss settings of 0.1. Two 0.1 loss settings stay as options of the render: the allow list `allowLosses` and the cap `maxLosses` (C2-H-204, C2-H-205).

## Shapes that Carve source cannot spell

**C2-A-175** An interchange-only shape is a node, a field or a wrapper that only a format bridge or another consumer supplies. A parser never produces one, JSON encoding and decoding keep it, and a Carve writer does not invent syntax for it and reports what it could not write.

| Shape | Carve writer | HTML |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `caption.short` | omits the field | renders the full caption once |
| `table_cell.scope` and `headerIds` | reports each field | writes `scope` and `headers` attributes |
| `image.longDescription` | reports the field | renders its blocks after the image |
| `image.decorative` | reports the field | writes empty `alt` |
| `xref.display` | reports the field | uses the default core text |
| blocks in `table_cell.children` | reports the loss | renders the blocks in the cell |
| `small_caps` | writes the children | `span` with class `smallcaps` |
| `section` | writes the children | `section` element |
| `ruby` | writes each base with its annotation in parentheses | `ruby` element |
| an extension node with an unknown name | writes the fallback | renders the fallback |

## Migration

**C2-A-176** Trees of other contract versions are upgraded by a migration function, not by the reader: a 2.0 reader refuses a tree that holds `escaped_text`, `critic_substitution`, `cell_wrap` or `figure` (C2-A-018).

**C2-A-177** A 2.0 producer writes `"2.0"`. The `next-ast2` draft never shipped. A migration function recognizes its tree or an earlier 0.2 draft tree by the retired node types and fields in the table below, not by `astVersion`, which a draft tree may hold as `"2.0"`.

**C2-A-178** For a tree written by `next-ast2` or an earlier 0.2 draft the migration function applies the matching rows:

| Draft shape | Becomes |
| --- | --- |
| `critic_substitution` with `old` and `new` | a `delete` holding `old`, directly followed by an `insert` holding `new` |
| `escaped_text` | `text` with the same `value`, then coalesced with its neighbors |
| `cell_wrap` | a `text` node holding one space, then coalesced |
| `cellWraps` on `code`, `math` and `raw_inline` | dropped |
| `rawRef` | dropped; 0.1 references become `collapsed` when `rawRef` ends in `[]` and `full` otherwise; 0.1 has no `shortcut` form; `key` is folded |
| `key` on definitions and footnote references | folded |
| `attrs.order` and the `keyValues` object | `keyValues` becomes a list of pairs, in the order `attrs.order` gives or else in member order; `order` is dropped; a key named `id` or `class` folds in |
| an `image` in a list of blocks | a `paragraph` with `role: "image"` that holds the image |
| a `line_block` with block children | `line` children, split at the breaks of each paragraph, with an empty `line` between stanzas; `lines` is dropped |
| a heading id in `attrs.id` | kept as an authored id: the draft tree does not say which ids were generated |
| `marker.bare`, `block_quote.fenced`, `table.sourceFormat` | dropped from the tree; written to a source-layout sidecar when the caller asks for one and supplies the original source, and otherwise dropped |
| `definition_list.spacing` | dropped |
| the former image promotion stage | dropped; `role: "image"` stays as the tree has it |
| the task status `cancelled`, in a draft tree or a 1.2 tree | removed; status derives from the mark |
| the former reference spelling field on links and images | `refForm`; the name identifies reference spelling rather than xref display. |
| the former cross-reference display field | `display`; the name identifies generated display text rather than reference spelling. |
| the former string tooltip field on link reference definitions | `tooltip`; all link target strings use one name, while visible titles stay inline lists. |
| the former image and math promotion flags on paragraphs | `role: "image"` and `role: "math"`; one field makes the two exclusive. |
| the former camel-case ruby pair node type | `ruby_pair`; the type follows snake_case and carries common node fields. |
| the former citation author-suppression flag | `citation.mode: "suppress-author"`; one field determines the mode. |
| `citation_group.mode` | removed; every item carries its own mode. |
| `citation.locatorLabel` and `citation.locatorValue` | `locator` object with label and inline children; its parts cannot disagree. |
| the former stored task state | removed; the state derives from `task.mark`. |
| `include.options` string pairs | decoded typed option object; source quoting is written to a source-layout sidecar as `optionSpelling` when the caller asks for one and supplies the original source, and otherwise dropped. |
| `thematic_break.marker`, `table.separatorWidths`, `table_row.continuationLines`, `table_cell.sourceContent`, `strong.boldItalic` | dropped |
| `table_body.headRows` | dropped; the groups hold the partition, and the count is written to a source-layout sidecar as `headerRows` when the caller asks for one and supplies the original source, and otherwise dropped |
| a definition inside a container | not produced by the draft, which moves it to the document; no change |
| a named `admonition` whose `kind` is not one of the eight admonition names | a `div` with the name as its first class |
| a `figure` that holds one image paragraph, code block, quote or math paragraph, and comments after it | that block, which takes the `caption` and the `attrs` of the figure; the comments go where C2-A-082 places them; `kind` is dropped |
| any other `figure` | a `figure_group` with the same children, `caption` and `attrs`; `kind` is dropped |

**C2-A-179** A 1.2 tree is first upgraded to the draft shape by the upgrade the draft defines (flat rows to table groups, `items` and `rows` to `children`, `ref` to `key`, `checked` and `taskState` to `task`, and so on; a 1.2 unordered list with no stored bullet character takes `marker: {kind: "bullet", char: "-"}`, and `checked: true` becomes `task: {mark: "x"}` while `checked: false` becomes `task: {mark: " "}`) and then migrated as above.

**C2-A-180** The migration is lossy for spelling by design and reports nothing for it.

## Further clauses

These clauses were added after other documents began to cite this one. They stand here so that no earlier id moves, and they go to their sections at the next renumbering.

**C2-A-181** An `include` has `path`, optional `section`, an optional decoded `options` object and optional `invalid`. `options` holds the valid options only (C2-B-205): `lines` and `rows` are range strings, `region` is an identifier string, `cols` is either a range string or a list of name strings, `shift` is an integer of at most nine digits or `"auto"`, and `code` is a syntax string or `true` when no value was written. A reader refuses a value outside the shape of its key, a range whose first number is greater than its second included. No quoting or escapes remain in these values; source spelling belongs to the layout record (C2-L-055). The option names and order come from `data/include-options.json`. `invalid` is the list of the invalid options (C2-B-206) in source order, each as written from its `@` to the end of its value, quotes and escapes included, so `@shift:x` and `@cols:"a,,b"` are kept as they stand. Expansion adds `file` and `children`, both resolution results (C2-N-017). A caption below a code include is its `caption` (C2-N-073), and a reader refuses a `caption` on an include whose `options` hold no `code`, and its own `attrs` act only through the child of a code include (C2-N-072). This replaces the earlier draft list of string pairs.

**C2-A-182** An `include` node has a position like any other block: it starts at its opening braces and ends after its closing braces and the spaces and tabs behind them on its line (C2-A-151). For `{{ a.crv }}` and two spaces the include spans offsets 0 to 13; indented by two spaces, with two spaces behind it, it spans 2 to 15.

**C2-A-183** A captioned block carries its own `attrs`, `lang` and `dir`, as every block does: the attribute line above it applies to it (C2-B-091).

**C2-A-184** A math block is a `paragraph` containing one display `math` node and any following comment-only lines, with `role: "math"`. A parser sets the role when it closes as one display math line (C2-B-158, C2-B-198); an ordinary paragraph omits it. A captioned math block is that paragraph with a `caption`. A reader refuses `role` on a paragraph of another shape: with `image` the children are one `image`, with `math` one display `math`, each with only soft breaks and comments beside it (C2-A-136).

The five facts that C2-B-191 sets when a block closes are tree fields, compared by equality (C2-A-161).

**C2-A-187** The bracket label of a div, an admonition, a directive and a code block is the string `groupLabel`, the text between the brackets as written, with no inline parsing: in `::: tip [Tab *x*]` it is `Tab *x*`. In 0.1 the label was inline content.

**C2-A-186** A parsed item, description, term or heading is never empty: one with nothing else holds a comment node (C2-B-136, C2-B-145). A parsed div, admonition, line block, hard-break block or quote may have no children: a quote mark alone on its line is an empty quote (C2-B-031), as is a quote fence with no body (C2-W-032, C2-W-082). A tree that was not parsed from source may hold an item, description, term or heading with no children.

```json
{
  "type": "include",
  "path": "parts/intro.crv",
  "section": "setup",
  "options": {"lines": "1-5"}
}
```

**C2-A-188** A valid tree passes the schema and the reader checks, which are every refusal of this document that the schema does not express. Among them are nesting depth, position ordering and source agreement when source is available, manifest and header-cell id references, the order of the two numbers of an include range (C2-A-181), the order of table groups (C2-A-086), the children of a table cell (C2-A-091), keys that occur once in `keyValues` (C2-A-035), an autolink `text` that differs from its `href` (C2-A-058), the glyph and the source of a smart punctuation node (C2-A-098), names that occur once in a list of extension declarations (C2-A-017), declared `data` keys, envelope version agreement, extension slot names against the declaration, extension fallback depth, metadata field count, annotation ids against a supplied range sidecar, frontmatter that is not the first child (C2-A-049), a span count against its mark (C2-A-093), an extension node inside a qualified fallback (C2-X-022), a qualified extension node without its declaration (C2-A-123) or with another version than its declaration (C2-X-018), and an unknown required extension (C2-A-018). A schema pass alone does not establish validity.

**C2-A-189** A reader refuses a node-shaped object inside opaque `data` or `props`, even when it is nested in a list or object. A node-shaped object is an object whose `type` is the name of a core node type; the rest of the object is not validated. The core walker ignores that data.

**C2-A-216** An `autolink` carries `text` only where its visible text differs from `href`, which is the email form: `<a@b.org>` gives `href` `mailto:a@b.org` and `text` `a@b.org`, and `<https://x.org>` gives `href` alone.

## Standard data namespaces

**C2-A-190** `carve.source`, `carve.style` and `carve.annotation` are optional declared data namespaces with the value schemas in `data/`.

**C2-A-191** Parsing Carve source produces none of these namespaces.

**C2-A-192** The core HTML renderer ignores all three namespaces. It writes nothing for root metadata `headers`, `footers`, `abstract`, `keywords` or `fields` and reports no notice.

**C2-A-193** A Carve source writer ignores all three namespaces and reports no loss for them, because data is not content. It cannot spell root metadata `headers`, `footers`, `abstract` or `keywords` and reports each under C2-W-011 as `field-unspellable` at the path of that field, as `/metadata/keywords`. It handles `fields` under the frontmatter rule of C2-W-011.

**C2-A-194** Equality compares all three data values under C2-A-161.

**C2-A-195** `carve.source` may stand on any node and records the foreign format, a locator with a part, element path or id, and the importer name and version.

**C2-A-196** `carve.source` replaces the 1.x provenance sidecar's source-id graph and byte offsets with a local foreign locator; multi-source lineage and byte spans remain in a separate provenance sidecar.

```json
{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Hello"}],"data":{"carve.source":{"format":"docx","locator":{"part":"word/document.xml","path":"/document/body/p[1]"},"importer":{"name":"pandoc-carve","version":"2.0"}}}}
```

**C2-A-197** `carve.style` may stand on any node with a named style and direct alignment, indentation, spacing before, spacing after, page break before, keep with next, language or direction; on the root it may also hold named styles, page size and margins. It holds scalar facts and named styles. It holds no nodes.

**C2-A-198** Style lengths are non-negative points, alignment is `start`, `center`, `end` or `justify`, and direction is `ltr` or `rtl` where no common `dir` field already holds it.

**C2-A-199** An importer stores only style facts it can read and a target writer may ignore facts it cannot express.

```json
{"type":"document","astVersion":"2.0","children":[],"extensions":[{"name":"carve.style","version":"1","required":false,"slots":[]}],"data":{"carve.style":{"namedStyles":{"Body":{"alignment":"start","spacingAfterPt":6}},"page":{"widthPt":595.28,"heightPt":841.89,"marginsPt":{"top":72,"right":72,"bottom":72,"left":72}}}},"metadata":{"headers":[{"placement":"default","children":[{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Report"}]}]}],"footers":[]}}
```

**C2-A-200** Font families, font sizes, colors, borders, floats, columns, section breaks and arbitrary CSS remain outside `carve.style` because no small shared round-trip vocabulary covers them.

**C2-A-201** Font emphasis already expressed by inline nodes stays in those nodes and never enters `carve.style`.

**C2-A-202** `carve.annotation` may stand on any node and holds a list of ids of entries in the annotation-range sidecar.

**C2-A-203** A tree-only reader checks the shape of each `carve.annotation` value and refuses duplicate ids in a value or across the tree. With the annotation-range sidecar, a reader also checks that each id identifies one range whose start or end path is that node or a descendant.

**C2-A-204** A block-boundary anchor uses the containing block's path and offset zero for its start or the block's annotation-text length for its end; a boundary between two blocks uses the end of the preceding block, or the start of the following block when there is no preceding block.

**C2-A-205** A range of the annotation-range sidecar keeps its start and end paths and byte offsets through a tree round trip, while rebinding after edits remains outside this contract.

```json
{"type":"paragraph","children":[{"type":"text","value":"Draft"}],"data":{"carve.annotation":{"ids":["comment-7","revision-2"]}}}
```

**C2-A-206** The three namespace schemas validate only their own values. A tree-only reader checks declaration, namespace placement, duplicate annotation ids and root metadata child slots.

**C2-A-207** Annotation text is the node's `value` or `alt` string, or `smart_punctuation.source`, followed by the projections of child slots in `data/node-slots.json` order, with no inserted separator; a soft or hard break contributes one LF and a nonbreaking space contributes one U+00A0, and offsets count the UTF-8 bytes of that text, as the layout sidecar does (C2-L-012), and a reader refuses an offset that falls inside the bytes of one character.

**C2-A-208** Source format, locator parts, importer name and version, style names and language, and annotation ids are nonempty strings; style page break and keep flags are booleans.

**C2-A-209** Named styles and page occur only in root `carve.style`. Headers and footers occur only in root `metadata`. Direct language or direction occurs only when the node has no corresponding common field.

**Exception C2-A-210** A qualified extension node may carry the canonical source form of C2-X-024 in the tree, even though it changes neither rendering nor resolution; a bare-tree writer needs it to reproduce the claimed source form.

**C2-A-211** The only block boundary in an empty document uses the root path with offset zero.

**C2-A-212** A metadata value is an object with exactly `kind` and `value`. `kind` is `string`, `boolean`, `number`, `inlines`, `blocks`, `list` or `map`. The value has that type. `inlines` and `blocks` are child lists; `list` holds ordered metadata values; `map` holds named metadata values. A walker reaches child lists at every depth. It visits root `fields` and nested `map` entries in Unicode code point name order, and `list` entries in array order. Resolution, the URL policy and rendering profiles apply to their nodes. A reader refuses more than 64 nested metadata values or more than 256 named entries across root `metadata.fields` and nested metadata maps in one document (data/limits.json).

**C2-A-213** A supplied `link` or `image` with `refForm` equal to `shortcut` and a key with no definition is valid. Resolution leaves it unresolved, and rendering writes the unresolved reference as text.

**C2-A-214** The annotation-range sidecar is a JSON object with a `ranges` list. Each range has a nonempty string `id`, a `start` object and an `end` object. Each endpoint has an RFC 6901 `path` into the tree and a nonnegative integer `offset` measured in UTF-8 bytes of the annotation text of that node (C2-A-207). The schema is `data/annotation-ranges.schema.json`.

**C2-A-215** A table group made from a delimited table may omit `pos`. Its rows, cells, cell paragraphs and decoded text nodes omit `pos`; the table itself carries the position of its source fence. A pipe table group carries `pos`. These are the delimited table cases of C2-A-158, including the group and decoded text nodes.

## The tree gate

The fixtures of `spec/0.2/trees/` are the gate of this document. Each tree of a Carve example of the block, inline, HTML and writer chapters, the expanded tree of each example of the Includes document, the imported tree of each example of the HTML import document, and each supplied tree that holds a node type or a field no example tree holds, passes `data/ast-schema.json`; each tree that has its source passes the position invariants C2-A-139 to C2-A-159 against it, an expanded tree against the source of the file that each `pos` names (C2-A-142). Every node type and every field of the schema occurs in at least one of them. Each of them passes the reader checks of C2-A-188 that the gate states (`scripts/lib/spec2-reader.mjs`). Each refused tree names the clause that refuses it and whether the schema refuses it or only a reader check beyond the schema, and a tree refused by a reader check breaks one of those checks. `npm run spec2:data` checks all of this, and no fixture is waived. An engine meets the gate when its parse of each example equals the fixture under C2-A-161 with every `pos` equal too, an include example parsed with a resolver that serves the example's files under their names, and its reader accepts every positive tree and refuses every refused one.

text.carve://spec/extensions:
# Carve 0.2: extensions

Status: provisional, not frozen with the core of Carve 0.2 on `next2`. The interfaces of this document may change in a 0.2.x release together with the extension catalog, because that work holds the open interface point O12 and may revisit two rulings of 17 November, the element around an attributed fallback (O15, C2-X-035) and the unresolved fallback after a renderer fails (O17, C2-X-050); see `STATUS.md`, "What is not frozen". The standard extensions are not frozen either.

This document defines the extension interface for Carve 0.2.0.

## Registration and matching

**C2-X-001** An extension is a versioned behavior identified by a qualified name under C2-A-123.

**C2-X-002** A producer declares each qualified extension it uses on the root or envelope with a name, a version, a required or optional flag and an ordered `slots` list of distinct names.

**C2-X-003** A reader refuses a required extension whose name or version it does not implement.

**C2-X-004** A reader preserves an unknown optional extension and uses its core fallback.

**C2-X-005** The matcher claims only an existing core node after core source parsing has finished.

**C2-X-006** An inline matcher claims `:name[content]{attributes}` under C2-I-094 by its source name.

**C2-X-007** The inline matcher receives the source name, parsed inline children and parsed attributes.

**C2-X-008** A block div matcher claims a `div` by the name after its opener run under C2-B-119.

**C2-X-009** The div matcher receives that name, the quoted title, the bracket label, parsed attributes and parsed body blocks.

**C2-X-010** A block fence matcher claims a `code_block` by the language on its opener.

**C2-X-011** The fence matcher receives that language, the title, the bracket label, parsed attributes and the code text value.

**C2-X-012** A name without a declared and enabled matcher stays the core node that the parser built: an inline source extension, a div with its first class, or a code block.

**C2-X-013** An extension adds no sigil, line shape or delimiter in 0.2.0.

**C2-X-014** Two enabled matchers cannot claim one core node; registration of such a pair fails before parsing.

## Transformation and carriage

**C2-X-015** A transform maps one claimed core node to one extension node of the same inline or block role. It may place further extension nodes that it produces inside the slots of that node, as the tabs transform places each `carve.tab` (C2-X-039).

**C2-X-016** A transform leaves every core node outside its claimed node unchanged.

**C2-X-017** A transform reads only the claimed node and its descendants.

**C2-X-018** The extension node carries the declared qualified name and version, with the same version as its declaration.

**C2-X-019** `props` is a JSON object whose keys and value types are defined by the extension's registered schema.

**C2-X-020** `slots` is an object of named child lists. The registered extension schema fixes each slot's content kind. The root or envelope declaration names the slots in order, including slots absent from a node. A slot name is a lowercase identifier and has no number suffix that encodes position. Repeated children form an ordered list in one slot. A walker visits slots in declaration order without a registry. A validator refuses a slot the declaration does not name.

**C2-X-021** `payload` is an optional list of alternatives with a nonempty format and a non-null JSON value under C2-A-122.

**C2-X-022** `fallback` is mandatory for every qualified extension node. It is core content of the node's own role, block or inline: it contains no extension node and validates as core content.

**C2-X-023** A reader without the extension resolves, renders and writes the fallback as core content, except where the Carve writer has a source form under C2-X-027. A writer without the extension writes that source form only when the written text parses back to one core node of that form and name whose canonical content is `body`, and otherwise writes the fallback and reports `structure-unspellable`. The source form it writes reports no loss: it reads back as that core node, which a reader with the extension claims again, and it is an exception to the equality of C2-W-002.

**C2-X-024** A source transform carries a `source` record with `form`, `name`, canonical `body` text, and any quoted title or bracket label, plus the core node's attributes on the extension node. The class a div takes from its name (C2-B-119) is no attribute of the extension node: `{#t .k}` above `:::: tabs` gives the attributes `id` `t` and the class `k`. Where the fallback is the claimed core node, it is that node without these attributes, which the extension node holds, so the fallback HTML of C2-X-035 writes each of them once.

**C2-X-025** `source.form` is `inline`, `div` or `fence`, and `source.name` is the claimed source name. A reader refuses a `source.name` that no matcher of its form can claim: for `div` a name that makes no plain div (C2-B-127), for `fence` a language that opens no `code_block`, for `inline` a name that is no inline extension name (C2-I-094).

**C2-X-026** `source.body` is the canonical Carve spelling of the claimed node's content, without its opener, closer or attached outer attributes.

**C2-X-027** A Carve writer with a source record writes the canonical `:name[body]`, colon-run div or fenced code block form under C2-W-039 and C2-W-040 and writes the extension node's attributes in the core attribute form.

**C2-X-028** A Carve writer without a source record writes the fallback and reports `structure-unspellable` at the extension node.

**C2-X-029** A transform gives the same node for the same claimed core node, extension version and configuration.

**C2-X-030** A reader refuses more than 32 nested unqualified inline extension nodes along `children` used as fallback under C2-A-124, or more than 8 MiB of decoded payload on one extension node under C2-A-132. The nesting bound counts only that path, the `children` of unqualified inline extension nodes: a qualified fallback holds no extension node (C2-X-022), so it nests none.

**C2-X-031** A reader refuses a `source.body` longer than 8 MiB in UTF-8 bytes and a qualified extension nesting depth greater than 32 through slots or children.

## Resolution, rendering and equality

**C2-X-032** Resolution visits one view of an extension node: its `children` and named slots when a renderer is registered in the selected mode's channel (C2-X-033, C2-X-052) for its name and version or for an extension node whose slots hold it, and the profile admits the node (C2-H-163), and its fallback otherwise. So a node the profile degrades is resolved in its fallback, which its degraded form writes (C2-H-165). Validation and the limits visit all of them. Resolution does not execute or inspect props, payload or source text.

**C2-X-033** A host registers a renderer by qualified name and version. The renderer receives the node, resolved child lists, fallback, rendering profile, URL policy, render `mode` (C2-H-122) and host helpers for escaped text, attributes, child lists and generated ids. Its `host.attributes(node, { block?, bare?, style? })` returns the attributes for an element, each with a leading space, in core writer order: `block: true` appends a generated `data-source-line` last when `host.sourceLines` is on and the node has a position; `bare: true` omits the node's authored id, classes and key-value attributes, so a synthesized row or row group can take only that generated line. With `style`, the helper merges the generated style declarations with an authored `style` into one attribute, at the authored key's position and with the value order of C2-H-009; without an authored `style` it writes the generated attribute in the order of C2-H-009. The host also exposes `sourceLines`, the effective boolean render option, and `blockDepth`, the current block indent in two-space units (C2-H-042).

**C2-X-034** An extension renderer is trusted host code. It returns an HTML string, which the host writes unchanged. The renderer uses the host helpers of C2-X-033 to apply escaping, the URL policy and the profile to its output. A host that renders untrusted documents registers only renderers it trusts. A structured output interface is left to a later version.

**C2-X-050** A host transform or renderer exception does not escape the engine. When a transform throws, the engine retains the claimed core node and reports a diagnostic that names the extension. When a renderer throws or returns a value that is not a string, the engine renders the extension fallback and reports a diagnostic that names the extension. That fallback is written unresolved, since resolution visited the slots (C2-X-032): its references, footnote references and cross-references render as unresolved text (C2-H-085, C2-H-086) and its headings carry no generated id, and the diagnostic says that the fallback was written unresolved. The size of a renderer's HTML string is the host's responsibility.

**C2-X-051** If the engine cannot prepare a claim's canonical source record because the writer reports a loss (C2-W-134) or refuses a repair (C2-W-133), the engine retains the core node and reports `extension-transform-failed` naming the extension. Parsing and rendering continue with that core node.

**C2-X-035** With no matching renderer, the HTML renderer writes the fallback and reports `extension-fallback-rendered`. Where the HTML renderer writes the fallback of an extension node that carries attributes (an `id`, a class or a pair, C2-A-032), here or after a renderer fails (C2-X-050), it writes the fallback inside a `<div>` for a block extension and a `<span>` for an inline extension, and that element carries the attributes by the rules of every element (C2-H-010 to C2-H-014). A node without attributes adds no element.

**C2-X-036** Every profile restriction and URL policy check applies inside slots and fallback.

**C2-X-037** Equality compares an extension node's name, version, props, children, slots, fallback, payload, resource ids and source record under C2-A-161.

**C2-X-038** A reader validates extension props and slot content kinds against its registered extension schema when it knows the extension. It validates slot names against the tree declaration even without a registry.

**C2-X-052** In `interactive` mode a registered interactive renderer handles the node. In `static` mode an explicitly registered build-time renderer handles it; registration for interactive mode alone does not select that channel. A build-time renderer returns self-contained HTML and receives the same host inputs and helpers as C2-X-033. With no renderer in the selected channel, C2-X-035 writes the fallback. Both channels obey C2-X-034 and C2-X-036.

**C2-X-053** A host may register ordered document transforms. After includes and ordinary resolution, before HTML rendering, each receives a copy of the resolved render view and returns a view; registration order is execution order, and a later transform sees the earlier result. A transform may inspect the whole document, replace or insert nodes declared by its extension, claim existing directive nodes, and edit core nodes of the view: change their attributes or content, or replace them with core nodes, as a transform that numbers headings or turns inline footnotes into text does. It does not change the authored tree, source record or the tree the Carve writer reads.

**C2-X-054** A document transform keeps core nodes it does not replace in their order and may claim a directive only once. The first registered transform to claim a directive owns it; a later claim fails that transform. Inserted extension nodes require their ordinary declaration, valid slots and core fallback. The normal tree limits and profile restrictions apply to the resulting view, and every URL it writes passes C2-H-159 to C2-H-161.

**C2-X-055** The host checks ids in the transformed view in document order after each transform. An inserted or replacement node with an authored id already used by a preceding node fails that transform; the first node keeps its id. A duplicate authored id that the view held before the transform ran, which C2-A-039 reports, fails no transform: only the nodes a transform inserted, replaced or edited are checked. Generated ids, including heading and extension control ids, are allocated again over the final view by their ordinary rules, avoiding every authored id and earlier generated id. References in that view resolve against the final ids before HTML is written. A failed document transform leaves its input view intact and reports a diagnostic naming the extension, as in C2-X-050. The checks of C2-X-054 and of this clause are observable only in their result: a view that fails one fails that transform as this clause says, and a view that passes all of them is rendered. An engine may check only the nodes a transform inserted, replaced or edited, since every node it kept passed the same checks before it ran; the result is the one a check of the whole view gives. A render with document transforms therefore resolves twice: once before the first transform, and once over the final view for the generated ids and references of this clause.

## Standard extension: tabs

The standard extensions are a catalog that follows the core: this section is not part of the freeze candidate, and the clauses of the sections before and after it are, with the provisional status of the head of this document.

**C2-X-039** The core provides optional `carve.tabs` and `carve.tab` extensions at version `1`. The `tabs` div matcher produces `carve.tabs`; the nested `tab` div produces `carve.tab` only inside its `tabs` slot. A `tab` div elsewhere stays a core div.

**C2-X-040** The `tabs` matcher claims a div only when its body has one or more `tab` divs and no other blocks, and each `tab` div has a nonempty quoted title.

**C2-X-041** `carve.tabs` has one slot, `tabs`, whose ordered items are `block_extension` nodes named `carve.tab` and nothing else. Each `carve.tab` has an optional `title` slot of inline nodes and a `body` slot of blocks. The transform puts the quoted title in `title` as inline content and the div body in `body`. Their declarations list `slots` as [`tabs`] and [`title`, `body`], respectively.

**C2-X-042** The transform gives each `carve.tab` a core fallback with its title as a `strong` paragraph, when present, followed by its body blocks. The `carve.tabs` fallback concatenates those sequences in tab order.

**C2-X-043** The tabs renderer writes one radio input, one linked label and one panel per item of `tabs` in order, with the input of the selected tab (C2-X-056) checked. That is its output in its default host option `mode`, `css` (C2-X-056). In `aria` mode it writes the WAI-ARIA tab pattern inside the same wrapper `div` instead: per item in order one `button` element with, in this order, `type="button"`, `role="tab"`, its `id`, `aria-selected` (`true` for the selected tab and `false` for the others) and `aria-controls` with the id of its panel, plus `tabindex="-1"` on every button but the selected tab's, holding the content the label would hold; then per item in order one panel, a `div` with, in this order, `class="tab-panel"`, `role="tabpanel"`, its `id` and `aria-labelledby` with the id of its button, plus `hidden` on every panel but the selected tab's. The renderer writes no script in either mode; a host that selects `aria` ships the script that switches the panels. Its build-time renderer, which a host registers for static mode (C2-X-052), writes no input, no `label` element, no generated id and no script: inside the same wrapper `div` it writes, per item in order, a `<section class="tabs-panel">` holding an `<h3 class="tabs-label">` with the content the label would hold, followed by the panel content. The selection does not change static output. Nor does the host option `mode`: the build-time renderer writes no button either. No output of the renderer has a line break between the elements it writes.

**C2-X-044** The tabs renderer renders each label from the tab's `title` slot and each panel from its `body` slot. It escapes text and attributes through the host renderer.

**C2-X-045** The tabs transform keeps the nested `tab` divs as div source in the outer `source.body`, in the canonical spelling of C2-X-026. A Pandoc bridge carries this structure as nested Divs with the classes `tabs` and `tab`.

**C2-X-046** A reader that knows `carve.tabs` (C2-X-038) refuses a `carve.tab` outside `carve.tabs.slots.tabs`, an item of that slot that is not `carve.tab`, or a tab without its `body` slot. The path of the refusal is the node it names: the `carve.tab`, the item of the slot, or the tab.

**C2-X-047** The tabs renderer groups the controls under the `tabsGroup` label (C2-H-125) and names each panel with the plain text of its title, or, when the title is absent, `Tab`, one space and its position counted from 1, as `Tab 1`. The wrapper is `<div class="tabs">` with `role="group"` and an `aria-label` with that group label before authored attributes are applied. It writes the authored id, `tabs` followed by the authored classes, and the other authored attributes in the order of C2-H-009. In `aria` mode the wrapper takes `role="tablist"` instead, and a panel takes its name from its button through `aria-labelledby` and carries no `aria-label`; a button without a title holds the `Tab 1` text. An authored `role` of the `carve.tabs` node takes the place of the generated role, and an authored `aria-label` or `aria-labelledby` the place of the generated name, in every mode: the wrapper writes the authored ones of these three attributes after its class, in their authored order, then the generated role and name that no authored attribute replaced. Without a stylesheet every panel of the `css` mode stays visible.

**C2-X-048** The tabs renderer gives each radio input a unique document-scoped id and links its label to that id. The groups are counted in document order from 1: group N has the input name `tabs-N`, and its inputs the ids `tabs-N-0`, `tabs-N-1` and so on, counted from 0. In `aria` mode each button takes the id its input would take, and the panel of button `tabs-N-K` the id `tabs-N-K-panel`. Where any authored id or any generated heading id is one of the ids of a group, that group takes the next N whose ids no authored id or generated heading id takes, and later groups count on from it. The ids of a group are the ids it writes in its mode. A code group uses a separate counter from 1: its Kth tab, counted from 1, has the id `codegroup-N-tab-K`. The collision rule above applies separately to the ids of each tabs or code-group scheme.

**C2-X-056** A tab's nonempty quoted title is its only label source (C2-X-040); a bracket label, a `label` attribute or a first heading does not supply a tab title. A tab whose attributes hold the key `selected`, with any value, is marked. The first marked tab is the selected tab, and with no mark the first tab is, so exactly one tab is selected; a later mark is ignored without a diagnostic. The standard tabs renderer takes the host option `mode`, `css` or `aria`, with `css` the default, as the code-group extension does; creating the renderer with another value fails. The option is a setting of the renderer, not the render option `mode` of C2-H-122, and it changes only the interactive output (C2-X-043). The group label of C2-X-047 applies in every mode, and the panel names in `css` mode only: in `aria` mode the button names its panel, and in static mode the heading of each section names it. A per-instance host class does not change the standard tabs contract.
