## Standard extension source forms

**C2-X-057** A registered `wiki` inline matcher claims `:wiki[Page]` as an inline extension with the parsed content as its target and core-text fallback. In `:wiki[Page|Display]` the content before the first `|` is the target and the content after it the display text, which is the fallback: `:wiki[Main Page|home]` falls back to `home`. Without a `|` the content is both. Its renderer may turn that target into a link only through the host URL helper and C2-H-159. A heading reference uses the existing core `</#id>` or `[Label](#id)` forms, and a bare URL or email uses an angle autolink; none gets a new delimiter from an extension (C2-X-013).

**C2-X-058** A registered `cite` inline matcher claims `:cite[key]` as an inline extension with the key as its core-text fallback. A locator is an attribute, for example `:cite[doe]{locator="p. 4"}`, not punctuation inside the key. `:cite[a; b]` names several keys in one citation, separated by `;` and the spaces around it, and each key is resolved on its own. A named `bibliography` or `references` directive may hold definitions as core definition-list entries, with each term the citation key and its description the definition. A document transform may claim that directive and resolve the citations from it (C2-X-053); the claimed directive renders every entry in source order, including entries no citation uses. Without that extension, the inline form and directive retain their core fallback.

**C2-X-059** The standard `imgFence` matchers claim code fences whose language is `img` or `image` and whose body is SVG source, producing `carve.imgFence.img` or `carve.imgFence.image`, respectively. Its fallback is that core code block without its attributes (C2-X-024). Its trusted sanitizer removes unsafe elements with their descendants and unsafe attributes, then accepts only a single well-formed SVG root it can reduce to a bounded image without scripts, event attributes, active or external references, or foreign content. If it cannot, the renderer writes the fallback and reports its failure under C2-X-050. It writes the standard SVG namespace on the root and percent-encodes the accepted SVG as UTF-8 in a `data:image/svg+xml` URL for the `src` of one `<img>`; the encoded URL may be no longer than the existing 8 MiB extension payload bound (C2-X-030).

**C2-X-060** Only the `imgFence` sanitizer's own result, passed directly to that `<img>` sink with its provenance intact, receives the URL-policy exception of C2-H-159. A source URL, an authored `data:` attribute, a copied sanitizer string or a value passed to another sink has no exception. The host applies the profile and its other attribute filters to the image and does not pass an unsafe sanitizer result through as HTML.

## Standard extensions of the 0.1 catalog

These extensions follow the catalog status of the tabs section. Each claims a core node by the matcher its row of `data/extensions.json` names, and with no renderer in the selected channel C2-X-035 writes its fallback.

**C2-X-061** A diagram extension of the fenced renderers, as `carve.fencedRender.mermaid`, and `carve.mathBlock` claim a code block by its language (C2-X-010), and their fallback is that core code block without its attributes (C2-X-024). A diagram extension has a build-time renderer (C2-X-052) only where the host gives it a build function, and the engine makes no network call. In `static` mode without one, C2-X-035 writes the fallback, the plain code block `<pre><code class="language-mermaid">`, and no `<pre class="mermaid">` source element as in 0.1.

**C2-X-062** The renderer of `carve.mathBlock` writes `role="math"` on the element that holds the math, as core display math does (C2-H-072, C2-H-077).

**C2-X-063** The `code-group` div matcher of `carve.codeGroup` claims a div only when its body holds one or more code blocks and no other blocks; a body with another block stays a core div, as a `tabs` body does (C2-X-040), so no block is lost. The label of a panel is the bracket label of its code block, or, where it has none, its quoted title, or else its language.

**C2-X-064** The spoiler is one extension with two node names, because a definition has one matcher form: `carve.spoiler`, which the `spoiler` inline matcher makes of `:spoiler[...]`, and `carve.spoilerBlock`, which the `spoiler` div matcher makes of `::: spoiler`. A host registers both together.

**C2-X-065** `carve.details`, which the `details` div matcher makes, and `carve.spoilerBlock` take the fallback of a tab (C2-X-042): the quoted title as a `strong` paragraph, when present, followed by the body blocks. The core div with its class is not their fallback.

**C2-X-066** A span key an extension adds for rendering and lint, as `samp`, `var`, `cite` and `dfn`, is an ordinary attribute for C2-A-035: only `abbr`, `time` and `kbd` are semantic keys of the core, so an added key merges with its other spellings by the general rule, and the duplicate checks treat it as any other key.

**C2-X-067** The `glossary` transform writes its definition lists inside the core `<div class="glossary">` wrapper of the directive, which carries the directive's attributes; it does not put those attributes on a list.

**C2-X-068** In `author-date` mode the author and year of a reference entry come from a span around its key in the description term, `:: [doe]{author="Doe" year="2020"}`, since a term takes no attributes in source, or from data the host gives the extension.

**C2-X-069** A document transform does not see the render option `labels`, so the `index` extension takes the label of its back-links as its own option `backrefLabel`; its default is the default of the label `indexBackref`, `Back to`.

## Writing consistency

**C2-X-049** A writer with a source record that does not parse and transform back to an equal extension node writes the fallback and reports `structure-unspellable`. The test needs the extension's matcher, so it is the test of a writer that has the extension registered; a writer without it follows C2-X-023. A `write` call reads the option `extensions` for this test.

# Carve 0.2: importing HTML Status: part of the freeze candidate of Carve 0.2 on `next2`, frozen with the rest of the core (`STATUS.md` names the candidate); the examples are verified against the reference importer (`import/` of `carve-js`). This document defines how an HTML importer turns HTML into a 0.2 tree. `html.md` defines how a tree becomes HTML and, in its section "Import", how the carriers of a render with `roundtrip` are read back (C2-H-182 to C2-H-199). This document covers everything else: HTML from any other tool, Carve HTML rendered without `roundtrip`, and every element and attribute that carries no carrier. The mapping is the one the reference importer follows. No carrier is added: a fact that HTML cannot hold is a loss, and the importer reports it. Conventions: - A clause is a paragraph that starts with an id of the form `C2-M-nnn`. `C2-A-nnn`, `C2-B-nnn`, `C2-H-nnn`, `C2-I-nnn`, `C2-L-nnn` and `C2-W-nnn` name clauses of the AST document, the block and inline chapters, the HTML document, the sidecar document and the writer document. - A clause that starts with the word "Exception" is a carve-out from a more general clause. Exceptions are counted at the end. - `data/import-html.json` holds the rows the clauses read: `attributes`, `elements`, `conventions`, `codes` and `losses`, and the tables of this document are rows of it too. Where a row and its clause disagree, the clause wins. - Each example is a `compare` container that holds the HTML input, the children of the imported document as JSON without positions and provenance, and the Carve source the canonical writer gives for that tree. A line below an example that starts with `Reported:` names codes the import reports; it need not name every one. - "Report X" means: add an entry with the code X to the diagnostics record (C2-M-080). ## Scope and input **C2-M-001** The importer takes a string of HTML and returns a 0.2 document tree, its canonical Carve source and a diagnostics record. The `lang` of ``, or else of ``, is the `lang` of the document node, and the same holds for a `dir` read as the attribute row `dir` reads it (C2-M-052). # Carve 0.2: includes Status: part of the freeze candidate of Carve 0.2 on `next2`, frozen with the rest of the core (`STATUS.md` names the candidate). This document defines how an include directive is expanded: which file a directive reads, how that file becomes part of the tree, what its options select, how references cross a file boundary, what fails and how a failure is reported. The shape of the directive is defined by the block chapter (C2-B-156, C2-B-201 to C2-B-206) and its node by the AST document (C2-A-181, C2-A-182). It replaces section 19 of the 0.1 specification (rules I1 to I16 of CARVE-P6-001) and applies the 0.2 rulings on includes. Conventions: - A clause is a paragraph that starts with an id of the form `C2-N-nnn`. `C2-A-nnn`, `C2-B-nnn`, `C2-H-nnn`, `C2-I-nnn`, `C2-L-nnn` and `C2-W-nnn` name clauses of the AST document, the block and inline chapters, the HTML document, the sidecar document and the writer document. `I1` to `I16` name the rules of the 0.1 include section. - A clause that starts with the word "Exception" is a carve-out from a more general clause. Exceptions are counted at the end. - An example names the files a resolver serves, each in a fenced block below a line `File`, then a `compare` container with the entry document and the expected HTML, and where the tree matters the tree in JSON. The resolver of an example serves exactly those files under the names shown and returns each name as its id. Every example is *unverified*: the fixture trees come from the reference engine, and the HTML is written by hand and not machine-checked. - JSON examples leave out `pos` unless the example is about positions, and leave out the nodes the example is not about. - The tables that decide a rule are data files: `data/includes.json` lists the failure causes and the option combinations, `data/include-options.json` the options, and `data/limits.json` the two limits. ## Scope and defaults **C2-N-001** Expansion is part of 0.2.0. Every engine that offers the `includes` option (C2-H-137) expands include directives as this document states, and an engine that does not offer the option refuses it (C2-H-137). **C2-N-002** Only an `include` node is expanded, and only a block line makes one (C2-B-156). There is no inline include: `{{ ... }}` inside inline content is text, each of its braces read on its own (inline chapter, braced forms), so a directive in a sentence, in a heading, in a table cell or on a lazy line of a paragraph (C2-B-024) stays text and is never passed to a resolver. Example 1 (unverified) File `part.crv`: ```carve Never read. ``` ::: compare ```carve See {{ part.crv }} here. Text {{ part.crv }} ``` ```html

See {{ part.crv }} here.

Text {{ part.crv }}

``` ::: **C2-N-003** The `includes` option holds a resolver (C2-N-007) and the two limits (C2-N-064, C2-N-065). A library call that gives no resolver expands nothing: every include stays unexpanded and is reported with `include-no-resolver` (C2-N-061). **C2-N-004** A command-line tool expands includes by default when it reads its entry document from a file and writes any target other than Carve source. It uses the resolver of C2-N-012 with the containment root set to the directory of the entry file, as a canonical path with every symbolic link resolved. The tool offers a way to turn expansion off and a way to name another root. With the entry read from standard input there is no entry file and so no default root: the tool expands nothing unless the caller names a root. A tool that expands nothing, with expansion turned off or with standard input and no root, has no resolver, and each include is reported with `include-no-resolver` (C2-N-003). With a named root, an include of standard input resolves against that root. **C2-N-005** A processor whose output is Carve source does not expand, whether or not a resolver is given: `carve fmt`, a render to the Carve target and every other pipeline whose product is Carve source return the directive as the author wrote it. `carve flatten`, whose product is the expanded tree, is the one command that expands (C2-T-047). Such a processor reports no `include-no-resolver` (C2-N-003), since it expands nothing by its own rule. (I15, carried over) **C2-N-006** Expansion runs after the top-level document is parsed and before resolution (C2-A-135), as part of the parse that the `includes` option configures. A tree in which expansion ran lists `includeExpansion` in the root `stages` (C2-A-135). Expansion runs whenever the parse has a resolver, also when the document holds no include. ## The resolver **C2-N-007** A resolver is a function of the host. It receives the decoded path of the directive (C2-B-202), the section name when there is one, the decoded valid options (C2-A-181), and the id of the including file, which is absent when the directive stands in a top-level document that has no id. It returns either the text of the target and an id for it, or one error cause: `not_found`, `outside_root`, `unreadable` or `non_text`. **C2-N-008** The resolver returns the whole target. It may read the section and the options, for example to decide access, but it does not select: the processor applies every selection, transform and mode to the text the resolver returned. **C2-N-009** An id is a string that names one target. Two spellings of a path that reach the same target give the same id, so `a/b.crv` and `a/./b.crv` are one id. The cycle check (C2-N-066), `pos.file` (C2-N-019) and the include node's `file` (C2-N-017) all use this id. **C2-N-010** A path is resolved relative to the including file, never relative to the root or to the working directory of a process. The one exception: with the entry read from standard input and a named root (C2-N-004), the path base of the entry document is that root, so its includes resolve against the root. **C2-N-011** Content is text when it is well-formed UTF-8 and holds no U+0000. A resolver reports any other content as `non_text` and does not replace a byte: the replacement rule for the top-level input does not apply to an included file. A leading U+FEFF of a returned text is not content. The file holds U+0000, so it is no text: the include stays unexpanded (C2-N-011). Example 41 (unverified) File `bad.crv` holds the three bytes `61 00 62`: `a`, U+0000 and `b`. ::: compare ```carve {{ bad.crv }} ``` ```html

{{ bad.crv }}

``` ::: Reported: `include-non-text`, `include-unresolved`. **C2-N-012** The resolver of a command-line tool reads files. It resolves the path against the directory of the including file, takes the canonical form of the result with every symbolic link resolved, and returns `outside_root` unless that form lies inside the canonical root. A `..` segment is allowed when the canonical result stays inside the root, and an absolute path is allowed only when it canonicalizes inside the root. The resolver takes the switch `allowAbsolute`, on by default: on, an absolute path is tested against the root as every other path is; off, an absolute path gives `outside_root` before anything is read, as the 0.1 option of that name did by default. The command line keeps it on. A path that starts with a URI scheme, letters and `:` before any `/`, gives `outside_root`: the resolver fetches nothing remote. **C2-N-013** The containment test comes before any test of existence. For a target that does not exist, the resolver canonicalizes the longest prefix that exists and appends the rest normalized; a result outside the root is `outside_root` whether or not the target exists, so the cause never reveals the existence of a file outside the root. Inside the root, a missing target is `not_found` and a file that cannot be read is `unreadable`. The file the resolver reads is the file it tested: no change of the file system between the test and the read, such as a symbolic link turned to a directory outside the root, makes it read a file outside the root, so a resolver that tests a path and then opens that path again does not meet this clause. A resolver meets it by testing what it opened: it opens the file, then compares the identity of the open handle, its device and file number, with that of the canonical path it tested inside the root, or it opens each segment of the path from a handle of the root without following a link out of it. A host whose platform offers neither does not give the resolver of C2-N-012 a file system that untrusted documents or other processes can change during the expansion: it serves the files from a store that does not change between the test and the read, such as a snapshot or a set of files read into memory before the expansion, or from a directory that the platform confines, such as a preopened directory of WASI. **C2-N-014** One expansion has one root. A nested include resolves its path against its own including file (C2-N-010) and is still tested against the root of the top-level document; the root is not re-based per file. A configured root is an absolute path, and a root that is not absolute is refused: expansion then stays off, as with no resolver. Given the files `book/main.crv`, `book/chapters/one.crv` and `book/shared/glossary.crv` and the root `book/`, the directive `{{ ../shared/glossary.crv }}` in `chapters/one.crv` reads the glossary, and `{{ ../../etc/passwd }}` gives `outside_root`. ## Expansion **C2-N-015** An included file is parsed as a document of its own, with the parse options of the top-level document. It has its own contents and its own depth counts: the block limit (C2-B-190) and the inline limit (C2-I-118) count within that file. A construct that is open at the end of the file, a fence, a list, a div, a quote or a comment block, ends there, as at the end of any document. Nothing of the including file is read by that parse, and nothing in the included file captures a line of the including file. Example 2 (unverified) File `child.crv`: ````carve ```js let x = 1; ```` ::: compare ```carve Before. {{ child.crv }} After. ``` ```html

let x = 1;

Reported: `unclosed-code-fence`. **C2-N-016** The blocks of that document, after selection (C2-N-027 to C2-N-052), become the `children` of the include node. The include node stays where the directive stood. There is no splice of source text, so a directive cannot complete or interrupt a construct of the including file. The root of the expanded tree declares each extension that the parse of an included file declared, a name once (C2-A-017, C2-X-002); that parse has the extensions of the top-level document (C2-N-015), so the declarations agree. **C2-N-017** An include node carries `file`, the id the resolver returned, whenever the resolver returned a text for it, and `children` exactly when it was expanded. An unexpanded include has no `children`; an include of an empty file, or of a selection that holds no block, has an empty `children` list. A node that has `children` also has `file`. Both fields are resolution results (C2-A-133): tree equality skips them. **C2-N-018** Expansion is recursive: the includes in an included file are expanded the same way, each relative to its own including file. Directives are expanded in tree order, a node before the nodes inside it, so the resolver is called and the size cap is charged (C2-N-065) in that order. server.listen(3000)
``` ::: ```json { "type": "include", "path": "src/server.js", "options": {"region": "start", "code": "js"}, "attrs": {"classes": ["diff"], "keyValues": [["title", "server.js"]]}, "file": "src/server.js", "children": [ { "type": "code_block", "syntax": "js", "value": "const server = http.createServer(handler)\nserver.listen(3000)\n", "attrs": {"classes": ["diff"], "keyValues": [["title", "server.js"]]} } ] } ``` **C2-N-043** The payload holds one line per selected line, each ended by one line feed, as an authored fence's content is: a CRLF becomes a line feed, a lone CR stays as content of its line (C2-B-010), a last line without a line ending gains one, a selected blank last line keeps its line feed, and an empty selection gives the value `""`. A leading U+FEFF of the file is not payload; a U+FEFF that opens a later line is. A lone CR ends no line, in the file as in an authored fence, so the one selected line keeps it (C2-B-010, C2-N-034). Example 32 (unverified) File `a.txt` holds the three bytes `61 0D 62`: `a`, a CR and `b`, with no line ending. ```carve {{ a.txt @code @lines:1-1 }} ``` ```json { "type": "include", "path": "a.txt", "options": {"code": true, "lines": "1-1"}, "file": "a.txt", "children": [{"type": "code_block", "value": "a\rb\n"}] } ``` **C2-N-044** The child's `pos` is in the included file. It starts at column 1 of the first selected line, after a leading U+FEFF on line 1, and ends directly after the last character of the last selected line, without its line ending. An empty selection has a zero-width span at the start of the file, after a leading U+FEFF, or at column 1 of the closing marker line of an empty region. A table made from the payload (C2-N-045) has the same span, and its cells keep their positions in the file. **C2-N-045** With the `table` flag in the include's attributes and the language `csv` or `tsv`, the child is the delimited table such a fence gives (C2-B-180), with bad quoting reported as on an authored fence (C2-B-181). `rows` selects records and `cols` projects columns (C2-N-046, C2-N-047). Example 16 (unverified) File `data/plans.csv`: ```csv Plan,Seats,Price Starter,1,"$0" Team,10,"$49, billed yearly" ``` ::: compare ```carve {table} {{ data/plans.csv @code:csv }} ``` ```html
PlanSeatsPrice
Starter1$0
Team10$49, billed yearly
``` ::: **C2-N-046** `rows` counts the parsed records of the whole file from 1, header records included, after the leading U+FEFF is removed. A quoted field that holds line breaks is one record. A whole physical line that is a well-formed marker of C2-N-039 is no record under any selection or none: it is no row, no cell, and does not count toward `rows` or `header-rows`. A marker is recognized only outside a quoted field, here and for `region`: inside a quoted field the line is data of that field. The first `header-rows` records of the file, one by default, form the head, and the last `footer-rows` records of the file, none by default, form the foot. Both are written under any selection, and a selection chooses only body records, so a head or foot record inside the range is not repeated. A `lines` selection chooses, whole, the records of the whole file whose first line lies in the range, also one that ends past the range, so a quoted field is never cut. The two counts are taken on the records of the whole file as C2-B-221 takes them on the rows of a table: the head takes its records first, and a `footer-rows` count larger than the records below the head takes them all. A `rows` range that starts past the last record leaves the include unexpanded with `include-rows-out-of-range`, and an end past the last record is clipped. (I1d, carried over) Example 34 (unverified) File `a.csv`: ```csv Name "first #region keep mid #endregion keep last" ``` ::: compare ```carve {table} {{ a.csv @code:csv }} ``` ```html
Name
first #region keep mid #endregion keep last
``` ::: The two marker lines stand inside a quoted field, so they are data of the cell. Example 37 (unverified) File `t.csv`: ```csv H a b F ``` ::: compare ```carve {table footer-rows=1} {{ t.csv @rows:2-4 @code:csv }} ``` ```html
H
a
b
F
``` ::: Record 4 is the foot of the file, so the range puts only `a` and `b` in the body, and `F` is written once, in the foot. **C2-N-047** `cols` with a list of names takes the columns whose head names match exactly, in the order given, so it may reorder them. The names are matched against the head of the whole file (C2-N-046) under any selection: a `lines` or `region` selection chooses records and never makes a new head. A requested name that the first head record lacks or holds twice leaves the include unexpanded with `include-cols-invalid`, and a name requested twice with `include-cols-duplicate`; an empty or a repeated head name that no request names is not tested. `cols` with a range selects columns by number and is valid only with `header-rows=0`; on another table, or past the last column, it gives `include-cols-invalid`. `cols` combines with any one selection or none. (I1d, carried over) Example 36 (unverified) File `a.csv`: ```csv Name,Price A,1 B,2 ``` ::: compare ```carve {table} {{ a.csv @lines:2-2 @cols:"Price" @code:csv }} ``` ```html
Price
1
``` ::: Line 2 selects the record `A,1`; the head is still the first record of the file, so `Price` names its second column. ### Shift **C2-N-048** `shift` with a number N adds N to the level of every heading among the children of the include, at every depth, headings of nested includes included. A level that would fall below 1 or rise above 6 is set to 1 or 6, the heading is kept, and `include-heading-clamp` reports it. A shift changes no text and no id: an authored id stays, and a generated id is computed from the unchanged text (C2-N-057), so a cross-reference into a shifted heading still resolves. Section numbering counts the new levels. (I8, carried over) Example 17 (unverified) File `child.crv`: ```carve = A ====== B ``` ::: compare ```carve {{ child.crv @shift:1 }} ``` ```html

A

B
``` ::: **C2-N-049** `shift:auto` computes N as (C + 1) - T. C is the level of the nearest heading before the include in document order that stands in the include's own block container or in a container around it, where an expanded include counts as no container; a heading inside a sibling container that closed before the include does not count, and with no such heading C is 0. T is the lowest heading level among the children after selection and after the includes inside them are expanded. With no heading among the children, `auto` changes nothing and reports nothing. (I8, carried over) **C2-N-050** Shifts are applied once the tree is expanded, include by include in tree order, an include before the includes inside it. Each include reads the levels as the shifts before it left them, so a nested `auto` places its headings relative to the assembled document and is not shifted twice. Example 18 (unverified) File `child.crv`: ```carve {{ grand.crv @shift:auto }} ``` File `grand.crv`: ```carve = GrandTop ``` ::: compare ```carve = One {{ child.crv @shift:1 }} ``` ```html

One

GrandTop

``` ::: `child.crv` shifts `GrandTop` to level 2. The nested `auto` then finds C = 1 and T = 2, so N = 0. **C2-N-051** `shift` on a code include has no effect and reports nothing, since its child holds no heading. **C2-N-052** The children of an include hold no node of the including file, and an include's selection, transform and mode act only on its own children. ## References across files **C2-N-053** The file of a node is the file whose parse produced it: the top-level document, or the included file of the nearest expanded include around the node. The including file of an include is the file of the include node. **C2-N-054** A link reference is looked up in the link definitions of its own file first, which for a selection are those of the whole file (C2-N-020, C2-N-031), then in those of the including file, then in those of each file further out, up to the top-level document, and only then in the headings of the whole tree (C2-A-109, C2-H-083). The first file that defines the key decides. A definition never reaches inward: a reference in an including file does not see a definition of the file it includes. Example 19 (unverified) File `child.crv`: ```carve Child [c][ref] and [up][]. [ref]: https://child.example ``` ::: compare ```carve Parent [p][ref]. [ref]: https://parent.example [up]: https://up.example {{ child.crv }} ``` ```html

Parent p.

Child c and up.

``` ::: **C2-N-055** A footnote reference and an abbreviation look up their definition the same way: their own file first, then outward to the top-level document. Two files may each define a footnote with one key; they are two notes, and each reference reaches the note of the nearest file that defines the key. (Changed from 0.1, which renamed the second label: I5.) **C2-N-056** Footnotes are numbered once, over the expanded tree, by the order of their first reference (C2-H-087), and the footnote section collects the notes of every file. Example 20 (unverified) File `c.crv`: ```carve Child sees [^p] and [^n]. [^n]: Child note. ``` ::: compare ```carve See [^n]. {{ c.crv }} [^p]: Parent note. [^n]: Parent n. ``` ```html

See 1.

Child sees 2 and 3.

  1. Parent n.↩

  2. Parent note.↩

  3. Child note.↩

``` ::: **C2-N-057** Ids run over the expanded tree by the existing rules: the authored ids of every file are reserved in document order, then generated heading ids follow in document order with the suffixes of C2-H-024. Nothing is renamed: an authored id keeps its spelling in every file, and no rename is reported. A generated id that the merged tree suffixes is a generated id like any other (C2-A-134). Example 21 (unverified) File `a.crv`: ```carve = Setup ``` ::: compare ```carve = Setup {{ a.crv }} ``` ```html

Setup

Setup

``` ::: **C2-N-058** An authored id that stands in two files is a duplicate id like one that stands twice in one file: `duplicate-id` reports the later occurrence (C2-A-039), both elements are written with it, and a cross-reference ``, a link to `#id` and a link reference that resolves to a heading reach the first occurrence in document order, also when they stand in the file that holds the later one. Example 22 (unverified) File `child.crv`: ```carve {#tip} = Child tip Back to . ``` ::: compare ```carve {#tip} = Parent tip {{ child.crv }} ``` ```html

Parent tip

Child tip

Back to Parent tip.

``` ::: `duplicate-id` reports the heading of `child.crv`. In 0.1 it was renamed to `tip-2` and the cross-reference followed it. Reported: `duplicate-id`. **C2-N-059** Caption numbers and equation numbers are counted once, over the expanded tree, in the order of C2-H-170. **C2-N-060** Within one file a second definition of a key is a duplicate (C2-B-085). A key that two files each define once is no duplicate and reports nothing. ## Failures and limits **C2-N-061** Every failure leaves the include unexpanded and reports one code, the code of its cause, at the include node in the parse channel with severity warning. The causes, their codes and the order in which they are tested are the rows of `causes` in `data/includes.json`; the first cause that applies is reported and no later one is tested. No failure removes the directive, and no failure is silent: past the cap `include_diagnostics` of `data/limits.json`, 100 entries, a failure is counted and not listed (C2-T-024). **C2-N-062** The causes that are tested before the resolver is called, `no_resolver`, `option_invalid`, `conflict`, `depth` and `size_spent`, never call it, and the node has no `file`. A cause the resolver returns leaves the node without `file`. A cause tested after the resolver returned a text, `cycle`, `size_exceeded` and every selection cause, leaves `file` on the node: the file was read. **C2-N-063** A failure in an included file is reported at the include node in that file. The range of a finding is counted in the file of the node its path names (C2-A-173, C2-N-053). An entry with `file` may also carry `includedBy`, the chain of include nodes that read that file, from the top-level document inward, each with its `file` and `range` (C2-T-020). **C2-N-064** The top-level document stands at depth 0, and a file included from a file at depth D stands at depth D + 1. A directive whose file would stand deeper than the limit `include_depth` of `data/limits.json`, 16, is not resolved and reports `include-depth`. A host may lower the limit and may not raise it. Example 23 (unverified, with the depth limit lowered to 1) File `a.crv`: ```carve {{ b.crv }} ``` File `b.crv`: ```carve Deep. ``` ::: compare ```carve {{ a.crv }} ``` ```html

{{ b.crv }}

``` ::: **C2-N-065** The size cap `include_bytes` of `data/limits.json`, 8388608, bounds the sum of the UTF-8 byte lengths of every text the resolver returns in one expansion, the same file counted each time it is read. A text that would carry the sum past the cap is refused with `include-budget` (`size_exceeded`) and does not count toward the sum, and once the sum has reached the cap every later include is refused with `include-budget` before its resolver is called (`size_spent`). A host may lower the cap and may not raise it. **C2-N-066** A cycle is an include whose returned id is the id of the top-level document or the `file` of an include around it. It is refused with `include-cycle`, so a file that includes itself, directly or through other files, is read once on that chain. Example 24 (unverified) File `a.crv`: ```carve A, then {{ b.crv }} below: {{ b.crv }} ``` File `b.crv`: ```carve {{ a.crv }} ``` ::: compare ```carve {{ a.crv }} ``` ```html

A, then {{ b.crv }} below:

{{ a.crv }}

``` ::: **C2-N-067** The two limits also bound the work: each directive is at least seven bytes of source, so the number of resolver calls is at most the length of the top-level input and of the returned texts divided by seven. There is no separate bound on resolver calls. **C2-N-068** A message names the path as the directive wrote it and the cause. It never repeats an error text or a path that the resolver produced, so an absolute path of the host does not reach the output. **C2-N-069** Included content gets the same treatment as the including document: one `urlPolicy`, one `rawHtml` setting, one `profile` and every sanitizing rule of the HTML document apply to the whole expanded tree. No option is relaxed or tightened for content because it was included. **C2-N-070** An unexpanded include renders as C2-H-133 states, the directive as text in a paragraph, and the render reports `include-unresolved` in the render-loss channel, whatever the cause. Example 25 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve {{ missing.crv #part @shift:1 }} ``` ```html

{{ missing.crv #part @shift:1 }}

``` ::: The parse reports `include-not-found`, and the render `include-unresolved`. Reported: `include-not-found`, `include-unresolved`. ## Attributes and captions **C2-N-071** The attribute line above a directive attaches to the include node (C2-B-095), and the writer writes it back (C2-N-080). With `code` it acts through the child, which carries the same attributes (C2-N-042), and the `table` flag selects the delimited table (C2-N-045). **Exception C2-N-072** An include's own `attrs` take part in nothing else: they are not written to HTML, its id is no anchor and is not counted by the duplicate-id rule (C2-A-039) or the id reservation of C2-H-024, and its `lang` and `dir` apply to no child. Only the copy in a code include's child acts. On an include without `code`, `include-attributes-unused` reports them. Example 26 (unverified) File `a.crv`: ```carve Text. ``` ::: compare ```carve {#intro .wide} {{ a.crv }} ``` ```html

Text.

``` ::: **C2-N-073** A caption line directly below a code include attaches to the include (C2-B-147). When the include is expanded, its child carries the same caption, and the child is captioned as an authored code block or table is (C2-H-062). The copy in the child has no `pos`: its characters are in the including file, and a node under the children of an include is positioned in the included file (C2-A-142). The caption of the include keeps its position. A caption below an include without `code` is text, and `unattached-caption` reports it (C2-B-149). **Exception C2-N-074** The caption of an expanded include is skipped by every resolution walk and is not written: it takes no number, makes no footnote and claims no id, and the copy in its child is numbered, resolved and written. The caption of an unexpanded include is numbered where it stands and written after the directive's paragraph as one more paragraph, as C2-H-165 writes the caption of a degraded block. Example 27 (unverified) File `data/plans.csv`: ```csv Plan,Seats Starter,1 ``` ::: compare ```carve {table} {{ data/plans.csv @code:csv }} ^ Table #: Plans ``` ```html
Table 1: Plans
PlanSeats
Starter1
``` ::: The note and the id of the caption are made once, by the copy in the child, as for an authored code block. Example 38 (unverified) File `a.txt`: ```text code ``` ::: compare ```carve {{ a.txt @code }} ^ Listing #: x^[note] [s]{#q} ``` ```html

  1. note↩

``` ::: ## Rendering **C2-N-075** An expanded include renders its children and nothing else: no element, no attribute and no `data-source-line` of its own. Every HTML rule that reads the blocks of a container or of the document reads the children of an expanded include in its place, recursively: section wrapping (C2-H-026), the one-line forms of an item and a quote (C2-H-006, C2-H-007), the bare first paragraph of a description (C2-H-040) and the placement of the footnote section (C2-H-158). Example 28 (unverified) File `a.crv`: ```carve = Chapter Body. ``` File `one.crv`: ```carve One ``` ::: compare ```carve {{ a.crv }} Parent text. - {{ one.crv }} ``` ```html

Chapter

Body.

Parent text.

  • One
``` ::: The section opened by the included heading takes the blocks of the including file that follow, as it would in one file. **C2-N-076** With `sourceLines` on, an element rendered from an included node carries the line it starts on in its own file (C2-H-016, C2-N-019). The line is not mapped into the including file. Example 29 (unverified, `sourceLines` on) File `a.crv`: ```carve Hi ``` ::: compare ```carve Top. {{ a.crv }} ``` ```html

Top.

Hi

``` ::: **C2-N-077** A profile tests an include like any block (C2-H-163). `full` and `article` accept it. Under `comment` and `minimal`, whose allow lists do not name `include`, the include is outside the profile, expanded or not, and is written in its degraded form, the source text of its directive (C2-H-165); its children are not written, and `profile-construct-degraded` reports it once. Example 30 (unverified, `profile` set to `comment`) File `a.crv`: ```carve Included text. ``` ::: compare ```carve {{ a.crv }} ``` ```html

{{ a.crv }}

``` ::: **C2-N-078** An unexpanded include is a render loss (C2-N-070), so with `strictLosses` on a render of a tree that holds one returns no output (C2-H-130). An expanded include is no loss. **C2-N-079** With `roundtrip` on, an expanded include still writes only its children, so an import of that HTML gives the included blocks in place of the directive. The render reports this as the render loss `include-expanded-roundtrip`, once for each expanded include that no expanded include holds. The abbreviation template of C2-H-178 covers the children of the document only; the definitions of an included file get no template. ## Writing and the sidecar **C2-N-080** A Carve writer writes an include as its directive (C2-W-058), with its attribute line above it and its caption below it. It never writes the children and never writes `file`, and it reports no loss for either: both are resolution results (C2-N-017). (I12, carried over) **C2-N-081** Because tree equality skips `children` and `file`, `parse(fmt(x)) == parse(x)` holds for a document with includes whether or not either side was expanded (C2-W-002). **C2-N-082** The source-layout record covers the nodes of the top-level document. The nodes in the children of an include have no entries, and the include node has its own entry like any block, `optionSpelling` included (C2-L-055). ## Dependencies **C2-N-083** The dependencies of a document are the include nodes of its tree, in tree order. Each names its path as written, its including file (C2-N-053), and whether it was read: a node with `file` was read, a node without `file` was not. With no resolver, every directive is a dependency that was not read. **C2-N-084** A host that watches files for changes watches the distinct `file` values of the tree, and for each node without `file` the place its path would name relative to its including file. A host that wants a set rather than a list removes repeats by id. Example 31 (unverified) File `a.crv`: ```carve {{ b.crv }} {{ gone.crv }} ``` File `b.crv`: ```carve B. ``` ::: compare ```carve {{ a.crv }} {{ b.crv }} ``` ```html

B.

{{ gone.crv }}

B.

``` ::: The dependencies are four include nodes in this order: `a.crv` read, `b.crv` read with the including file `a.crv`, `gone.crv` not read with the including file `a.crv`, and `b.crv` read with the including file the top-level document. ## Lint **C2-N-085** A linter expands includes when its caller gives a resolver or a root, by the rules of this document and with the same limits. Without one it reads no include target, and each include reports `include-no-resolver` as in any parse. (I16, carried over) **C2-N-086** The top-level document is linted as it is. Every Carve include that the expansion accepted is linted with every rule and with the options of the top-level document, over the source the expansion parsed: the whole file, the line range or the region. For a section the whole file is linted, and only the findings from the first line of the selected heading or block through the last line of the last selected block are kept. A rule that reads the payload of a block also runs on a code include's child. **C2-N-087** A finding in included content names its file by id, with a line and a column counted in that file, and its tree path, which leads through the includes that reached it. A finding is reported once for each distinct file, line, column and rule; where one position is reached more than once, the first reach in document order supplies the path. `shift` does not make a range distinct. Lint control comments count the lines of their own file (C2-B-216). **C2-N-088** On a delimited table include, `lines` is valid and counts physical lines, and lint adds the hint `include-lines-table-rows-hint`, which suggests `rows`. ## What 0.1 rules became | 0.1 rule | In 0.2 | | --- | --- | | I1 syntax | shape: C2-B-201 to C2-B-206; semantics: C2-N-024 to C2-N-026, C2-N-034, C2-N-035 | | I1a section | C2-N-027 to C2-N-033 | | I1b region | C2-N-037 to C2-N-041 | | I1c code | C2-N-042 to C2-N-045, C2-N-073, C2-N-074 | | I1d rows and cols | C2-N-045 to C2-N-047, C2-N-088 | | I2 block and inline | the block half is C2-N-002, C2-N-016; the inline half is dropped | | I3 resolution model | C2-N-003, C2-N-007, C2-N-008, C2-N-011 | | I4 mechanism | C2-N-015 to C2-N-019 | | I5 collisions | C2-N-053 to C2-N-060; rename dropped | | I6 limits | C2-N-064 to C2-N-067; the resolver-call bound dropped | | I7 errors | C2-N-061 to C2-N-063, C2-N-068, C2-N-069 | | I8 shift | C2-N-048 to C2-N-051 | | I9 verbatim | C2-N-002, C2-N-042 | | I9a run recognition | dropped | | I10 containment | C2-N-012 to C2-N-014 | | I11 dependencies | C2-N-083, C2-N-084 | | I12 writer | C2-N-080, C2-N-081 | | I15 Carve target | C2-N-005 | | I16 lint | C2-N-085 to C2-N-088 | I13 and I14 were unassigned in 0.1. ## Counts | Section | Clauses | Exceptions | Examples | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | Scope and defaults | 6 | 0 | 1 | | The resolver | 8 | 0 | 1 | | Expansion | 9 | 0 | 8 | | Selection, transforms and mode | 29 | 0 | 17 | | References across files | 8 | 0 | 4 | | Failures and limits | 10 | 0 | 3 | | Attributes and captions | 4 | 2 | 3 | | Rendering | 5 | 0 | 3 | | Writing and the sidecar | 3 | 0 | 0 | | Dependencies | 2 | 0 | 1 | | Lint | 4 | 0 | 0 | | **Total** | **88** | **2** | **41** | The document has 88 clauses, 2 of them marked with the word "Exception", and 41 examples, all unverified. # Carve 0.2: the source-layout sidecar

Status: part of the freeze candidate of Carve 0.2 on `next2`, frozen with the rest of the core (`STATUS.md` names the candidate).

The tree of a Carve document holds its meaning (`ast.md`). How the author spelled it is recorded in a second JSON object, the source-layout sidecar. This document defines that object: its shape, the facts it holds, and the spelling a writer uses when it has a tree and no sidecar.

The shape is ported from the sidecar of the `next-ast2` branch (CARVE-P12-032 and CARVE-P12-067, `resources/ast-source-layout-schema.json`). The version 2 schema is `spec/0.2/data/layout-schema.json`. Seven facts are new here: they were tree fields in that draft or in an earlier 0.2 draft and moved out of the tree.

Conventions: a clause is a paragraph that starts with an id of the form `C2-L-nnn`. `C2-A-nnn`, `C2-B-nnn` and `C2-I-nnn` name clauses of the AST document and of the block and inline chapters.

## What the sidecar is

The sidecar is a record beside the tree, returned only when the caller asks and never placed inside the tree (C2-A-003).

Two documents that differ only in sidecar content are the same document (C2-A-004): tree equality (C2-A-161) does not read the sidecar.

**C2-L-003** Parsing, AST JSON, CLI JSON and rendering are the same with and without a sidecar. An AST reader does not accept a sidecar as a tree.

**C2-L-004** A sidecar belongs to the one tree it was returned with. Its paths do not hold after that tree is edited.

**C2-L-005** A sidecar does not survive a write: the written source is a new input with a layout of its own.

**C2-L-006** The tree wins. A writer ignores a sidecar fact that contradicts the tree, such as a `sourceFormat` on a table that a delimited table cannot hold.

## Shape

**C2-L-007** The sidecar is an object with six required fields and no others:

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `version` | `2` |
| `encoding` | `"utf-8"`, or `"base64"` for a byte input that is not well-formed UTF-8 (C2-L-056) |
| `source` | the original input: the string, or under `"base64"` the bytes in base64 |
| `lineEndings` | `none`, `lf`, `crlf`, `cr` or `mixed` |
| `bom` | whether the input starts with U+FEFF |
| `nodes` | a list of node entries |

The draft had `version: 1`. The version changes because the closed schema gains fields.

**C2-L-008** A reader refuses a sidecar version it does not implement.

**C2-L-058** A reader also refuses a record that breaks C2-L-011, C2-L-012, C2-L-020, C2-L-027 or C2-L-056, judging a fact only on an entry whose node type defines it. The first-fragment wrap of C2-L-048 meets C2-L-020. A writer ignores an entry whose path names no node of the tree, and a fact that is not defined for the type of the node its entry names (C2-L-006).

**C2-L-009** A node entry has `path`, `startByte` and `endByte`, and may have any of the facts below. It has no other fields.

**C2-L-010** `path` is an RFC 6901 JSON Pointer into the tree. The empty string is the root, and `/children/2/children/0` is the first child of the third block. This is how every sidecar fact refers to its node.

**C2-L-011** Entries stand in document order, a node before the nodes inside it, which compares each index of a `path` as a number: `/children/2` stands before `/children/10`. The slots of one node are visited in the order `title`, `children`, `caption`, and its other slots after them in the order of `data/node-slots.json`, the named slots of an extension node in the order of its declaration (C2-X-020). The nodes in a `fallback` have no entry. No two entries have the same path.

**C2-L-012** `startByte` and `endByte` are a range in bytes of the original input, start inclusive and end exclusive: its UTF-8 bytes, or under `"base64"` the bytes as given (C2-L-056). For a node that has `pos` they equal `pos.startOffset` and `pos.endOffset` (C2-A-141): a byte-order mark and every CR are counted as they stand. A range never exceeds the byte length of the input. An offset into a node value, as in `wraps` (C2-L-020), counts the UTF-8 bytes of that value.

**C2-L-056** `encoding` is `"base64"` exactly when the input was given as bytes that are not well-formed UTF-8 (C2-B-218), and `"utf-8"` for every other input. Under `"base64"`, `source` holds those bytes in the base64 alphabet of RFC 4648, section 4, with padding, and the ranges count them as they stand, so they still equal `pos`. A string input with an unpaired surrogate is no byte input: it keeps `"utf-8"`, and its `source` holds U+FFFD in place of the surrogate, whose three bytes are the ones C2-B-218 counts. For the bytes `61 FF 62` the sidecar has `"encoding": "base64"` and `"source": "Yf9i"`, and the entry of the paragraph spans bytes 0 to 3.

**C2-L-013** A producer does not invent a range. A node whose source is not one contiguous range, such as a cell joined from continuation rows, has an entry whose range runs from the start of its first piece to the end of its last. Such a node has no `pos` (C2-A-156), so this range is not a position.

**C2-L-014** Source and ranges are the minimum. A fact other than the required facts of C2-L-047, C2-L-052, C2-L-054 and C2-L-059 is optional. An absent optional fact means unknown: a producer omits what it did not measure, and a consumer does not read an absent fact as a value.

**C2-L-015** A writer that finds no fact uses the default of the section "Defaults". That is a rule about writing, not a reading of the document: the default is never reported as what the author wrote.

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "encoding": "utf-8",
  "source": ". a\n. b\n",
  "lineEndings": "lf",
  "bom": false,
  "nodes": [
    { "path": "/children/0", "startByte": 0, "endByte": 7, "bare": true },
    { "path": "/children/0/children/0", "startByte": 0, "endByte": 3, "markerRaw": ".", "markerColumn": 0, "contentColumn": 2 },
    { "path": "/children/0/children/1", "startByte": 4, "endByte": 7, "markerRaw": ".", "markerColumn": 0, "contentColumn": 2 }
  ]
}
```

## Facts moved out of the tree

These facts hold spelling that the tree does not. The last column names the field that held it in the `next-ast2` draft.

| Fact | On the entry of | Value | Draft tree field |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bare` | an ordered `list` | `true` when the items are numbered with the bare dot | `list.marker.bare` |
| `fenced` | a `block_quote` | `true` for a quote fence, `false` for `>` lines | `block_quote.fenced` |
| `hardBreakOpener` | a `div` with the class `hardbreaks` | `true` for the hard-break opener, `false` for the class form | none; the draft had no field |
| `wraps`, `continuationLines` | a `table_cell`, a `table_row` | where continuation rows broke the cell, and how many the row has | `cell_wrap`, `cellWraps`, `table_row.continuationLines` |
| `rawRef` | a `link` or `image` that carries `key` | the reference as typed, from the opening bracket to the bracket that closes the reference (C2-L-049) | `link.rawRef`, `image.rawRef` |
| `sourceFormat` | a `table` | `pipe`, `csv` or `tsv` | `table.sourceFormat` |
| `headerRows` | a delimited `table` | the effective count of its `header-rows` attribute | `table_body.headRows` |

**C2-L-016** `bare` says whether an ordered list was numbered with the bare dot or with written numbers. A list that mixes both (C2-B-043) records the form of its first marker, and the formatter writes the whole list in that form. The tree holds only the start value (C2-A-056).

**C2-L-017** `fenced` says which of the two quote forms the author wrote. Both give the same `block_quote`.

**C2-L-018** `hardBreakOpener` says which of the two forms of a hard-break block the author wrote. Both give the same `div` (C2-A-068).

**C2-L-019** `continuationLines` on a row entry is the number of continuation rows below that row, the ones with only empty fragments included.

**C2-L-020** `wraps` on a cell entry is a list of objects, sorted by `line`. Each has `line`, the number of the continuation row counted from 1; `path`, the pointer of the text node among the children of the cell's paragraph that holds the space joining that row's fragment (C2-B-184); and `offset`, the UTF-8 byte offset behind that space in the node's value, where the fragment starts. A wrap falls between two fragments, so it never lies inside another node (C2-L-048). The one exception is the wrap of the row where the first fragment that is not empty stands, for a cell whose fragments before it are empty: no space joins that fragment, and its wrap has `path`, the pointer of the first inline node of the cell's paragraph, of any type, and `offset` 0 (C2-L-048). A continuation row whose fragment of the cell is empty adds nothing and has no wrap for that cell (C2-B-184). A wrap in a cell that spans rows also has `row`, the number of rows below the cell's own row.

**C2-L-022** `rawRef` is the only place that holds a reference label as typed. The tree holds the folded `key` and the `refForm` (C2-A-105).

**C2-L-023** `sourceFormat` says how a table was written. The tree is the same for a pipe table and a delimited table with the same cells in the same groups (C2-A-088): blocks Examples 267 and 268 give equal trees.

**C2-L-057** `headerRows` on the entry of a delimited table is the effective count of a valid `header-rows` attribute the source gave (C2-B-209, C2-B-221), 0 included. A table without the attribute, and a pipe table, on which the attribute has no effect (C2-B-186), have no such fact. The groups of the tree hold the partition; the fact records only that the count was written. A `headerRows` that differs from the number of head rows of the tree contradicts the tree, and the writer ignores it (C2-L-006).

```json
{
  "version": 2,
  "encoding": "utf-8",
  "source": "| a |\n+ b |\n",
  "lineEndings": "lf",
  "bom": false,
  "nodes": [
    { "path": "/children/0", "startByte": 0, "endByte": 11, "sourceFormat": "pipe" },
    { "path": "/children/0/children/0/children/0", "startByte": 0, "endByte": 11, "continuationLines": 1 },
    {
      "path": "/children/0/children/0/children/0/children/0",
      "startByte": 1,
      "endByte": 10,
      "wraps": [
        { "line": 1, "path": "/children/0/children/0/children/0/children/0/children/0/children/0", "offset": 2 }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

In this example the cell's text value is `a b`, and the fragment of the first continuation row starts at byte 2.

## Measured facts carried over

These facts are ported from the draft. Columns in them are the zero-based columns of the block chapter (C2-B-003, C2-B-004), not the columns of `pos`.

| Fact | On the entry of | Value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `markerRaw` | a `list_item`, a `definition_term`, a `definition_description`, a `heading`, a `thematic_break`, a definition | the marker as typed, without the space after it |
| `markerColumn` | the same | the column of the marker's first character |
| `contentColumn` | a `list_item`, a `definition_description`, a `footnote` | the content column |
| `continuationStyle` | a `list_item`, a `definition_description` and a `footnote` (C2-L-052) | `lazy`, `indent`, `marker_line` or `none` |
| `blankLinesBefore`, `blankLinesAfter` | the nodes named in C2-L-047 | the number of blank lines around the node inside its container |
| `openerRaw`, `closerRaw` | a `code_block`, a `div`, an `admonition`, a `directive`, a `line_block`, a fenced `block_quote`, a block `comment`, a `raw_block`, `frontmatter` | the delimiter runs as typed, without the info string |
| `metadataSeparatorRaw` | a definition, a `definition_term` | the separator between the label or term and its body, whitespace included |
| `attachment` | a `caption` | `preceding` or `none` |

**C2-L-024** `markerRaw` is the exact source text of the marker that opened the node. For a heading it tells `#` from `=`, and for a fence `openerRaw` gives the length of the run.

**C2-L-025** `continuationStyle` has one value, chosen in this order: `lazy` when a paragraph line stands left of the content column, else `indent` when a later line reaches the content column, else `marker_line` when all content is on the marker line, else `none`.

**C2-L-026** `blankLinesBefore` and `blankLinesAfter` are the authored counts, not a normalized 0 or 1.

**C2-L-027** `openerRaw` and `closerRaw` come as a pair. An unclosed block has `closerRaw` present and empty. `openerRaw` is never empty.

**C2-L-028** `continuationStyle` has no value for a list continuation marker and `attachment` has none for a block attached by one, since 0.2 has no such marker. No fact records a leading or a trailing pipe, since a row always starts and ends with a pipe (C2-B-166).

**C2-L-029** A fact that the schema declares and this document does not define is a defect.

**C2-L-055** An include entry may carry `optionSpelling`, a closed object keyed by the option names of `data/include-options.json`; each value is the exact quoted or bare source spelling of that option value. The tree keeps the decoded typed value (C2-A-181), and the formatter uses this fact only when it decodes to the same value.

## Defaults

A writer that starts from a tree with no sidecar, or with a sidecar that lacks a fact, writes the canonical form of each spelling.

**C2-L-030** A decimal ordered list whose delimiter is the period is written with the bare dot on every item, the first included. A list that does not start at 1 carries its start value in a `start` attribute on the attribute line above it (C2-B-045): a number on the first marker would be read back as the numbered form. The writer clause names the exceptions (C2-W-044).

**C2-L-031** Every other ordered list is written with its numbers, letters or numerals in sequence from the start value: a list whose `marker.style` is not `1`, and a list with the `)` delimiter, since a bare `)` is not a marker (C2-B-036). A first marker that could read as another style is written as C2-W-045 says.

**C2-L-032** A bullet list is written with the character in `marker.char`. A writer writes `-` only where the tree says `-`, and does not change the character to separate two lists.

**C2-L-033** A quote is written with `>` lines.

**C2-L-034** A div with the class `hardbreaks` is written with the hard-break opener when every line break inside it is a `hard_break` and `hardbreaks` is the last of its classes, and in the class form otherwise. The opener adds the class last (C2-A-068), so the opener form on any other div would change the order of its classes.

**C2-L-035** A table row is written on one line, with no continuation rows.

**C2-L-036** A table is written as a pipe table. A table with no rows is written as a delimited table, because a pipe table needs a row.

**C2-L-037** A code block is written with the shortest run of at least three backticks that is longer than every bare backtick run on a line of its `value`, at any indent (C2-W-038). A fenced container is written with a colon run of the smallest length of at least three that is longer than the runs of the divs inside it (C2-W-039).

**C2-L-038** A heading is written with `=`.

**C2-L-039** A thematic break is written as `***`.

**C2-L-040** A reference is written from the tree: its text, then `[key]` for the form `full` or `[]` for the form `collapsed`. The form `shortcut` writes only its text in brackets, with no label tail. C2-W-075 spells a key that starts with a caret or an at-sign.

**C2-L-041** The remaining layout is the canonical layout of the Writer document: one blank line between blocks where the tree's `spacing` does not say otherwise, content indented to the content column, a bare `---` for YAML frontmatter, double quotes for a title.

| Spelling | Default with no fact | With a fact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ordered numbering | bare dot for a decimal list with the period, written numbers otherwise | kept: bare dot or written numbers |
| quote | `>` lines | kept: lines or fence |
| hard-break block | opener when all breaks are hard and the class is last, else class form | kept, when the tree allows it |
| table row | one line | kept: continuation rows at the recorded places |
| table form | pipe table, delimited when it has no rows | kept, when the tree allows it |
| head count of a delimited table | `header-rows` only where the head is not the first row (C2-W-066) | kept, when it equals the head |
| code fence | backticks, shortest safe length | normalized to the default |
| heading marker | `=` | normalized to `=` |
| thematic break | `***` | normalized to `***` |
| bullet character | from the tree | from the tree |

**C2-L-042** Where 0.2 has two equal forms, the formatter keeps the form the sidecar records: ordered numbering, the quote form, the hard-break form, the table form, a declared head count and continuation rows.

Where 0.2 has one canonical form, the formatter writes it whatever the sidecar records (C2-W-085).

**C2-L-045** `markerColumn` on the entry of a `comment` that came from a comment-only line inside a quote is the column of the quote mark on that line. No writer rule reads it.

**C2-L-046** The writer reads nine facts: `bare`, `fenced`, `hardBreakOpener`, `wraps`, `continuationLines`, `sourceFormat`, `headerRows`, `rawRef` and `optionSpelling` (C2-W-083, C2-W-084). The measured facts of the section "Measured facts carried over" have no reader in the 0.2 documents. They are for editors and other tools that need the layout as typed.

**C2-L-047** Every node in a list of blocks of the top-level document (C2-A-051), outside a caption and a table cell, and every `list_item`, `definition_term`, `definition_description` and `caption` has an entry with `blankLinesBefore` and `blankLinesAfter`, 0 included, since an absent fact means unknown. Table groups, rows and cells, the blocks inside a cell, the lines of a line block and the blocks inside a caption have no such facts, and the blocks of a `fallback` have no entry (C2-L-011). The blocks in the children of an expanded include have no entries (C2-N-082). An inline node has an entry only when it has a fact. The examples of this document show only the entries and facts under discussion.

**C2-L-048** The `wraps` of a cell are sorted by `line`, and those of one line by `row`; a cell that spans rows has `row` on every wrap, 0 for its own row. A cell whose content starts in a continuation row has no joining space: its wrap for that row names its first inline node with `offset` 0.

**C2-L-049** `rawRef` starts at the opening bracket, without the `!` of an image, and ends at the bracket that closes the reference, without an attribute block. In the full and collapsed forms this is the label's closing bracket; in the shortcut form it is the text pair's closing bracket. It is read without the prefixes of the lines it crosses, and the pieces are joined by a line feed.

**C2-L-050** `markerRaw` of a definition is its label with the colon, as `[^n]:`, `[r]:` and `*[A]:`, and its `metadataSeparatorRaw` is the colon with the spaces behind it, so the colon is in both. For a `definition_term`, `markerRaw` is `::` and the separator is the run of spaces between the mark and the term text.

**C2-L-051** A task box and the attribute blocks glued to a marker are not content of the item: `contentColumn` of `- [x] a` is the column of `a`. This is a fact of the layout record only: the marker tests of the block chapter read the text behind the marker before the box is taken out (C2-B-229).

**C2-L-052** `continuationStyle` stands on every `list_item`, `definition_description` and `footnote`, with `marker_line` when the node has no later line. `lazy` is a later line of a paragraph inside the node, at any depth, that stands left of the content column; `indent` is a later line at or right of it. A parse never gives `none`, which occurs only in a supplied record, as for `attachment` (C2-L-054).

**C2-L-053** A line is blank inside a quote when it carries exactly the marks of the open quotes and nothing else. Blank lines behind the last content of a quote that still carry its mark are counted as `blankLinesAfter` of the last block of the quote; a blank line without the mark is outside the quote and counts for the blocks around the quote.

**C2-L-054** A `figure_group` and a delimited table have no `openerRaw` and no `closerRaw`. A parse gives every `caption` the `attachment` `preceding`; `none` occurs only in a supplied record. A comment whose line lacks the mark of its quote has no `markerColumn`. `lineEndings` reports what the source holds, a lone CR included, although a lone CR ends no line (C2-B-010).

**C2-L-059** A comparison of a parse with layout against stated facts, as a test makes, holds these facts required: `source`, `lineEndings`, `bom` and the ranges of each entry; `blankLinesBefore` and `blankLinesAfter` where C2-L-047 gives them; `continuationStyle` where C2-L-052 gives it; and the `attachment` of a `caption` (C2-L-054). A required fact the producer omits fails the comparison. Every other fact is optional (C2-L-014): a stated optional fact is compared where the producer records it, and its absence passes.

## Schema

[`data/layout-schema.json`](data/layout-schema.json) defines the closed version 2 layout record.

## Counts

The document has 54 clauses. The reduction of 17 November 2026 deleted C2-L-001, C2-L-002, C2-L-043 and C2-L-044, whose rule other clauses state or give; their ids are not reused.

# Carve 0.2 Syntax: block structure Status: part of the freeze candidate of Carve 0.2 on `next2`, frozen with the rest of the core (`STATUS.md` names the candidate). This chapter defines how the lines of a Carve document form blocks. Inline content, HTML rendering, the tree and the writer have their own documents. Where a clause states rendered output, it does so because the output is the only visible sign of a block decision. Conventions: - A clause is a paragraph that starts with an id of the form `C2-B-nnn`. The prefix is new in 0.2. No 0.1 clause id is reused. - A clause that starts with the word "Exception" is a carve-out from a more general clause, or a named interaction between two constructs. Exceptions are counted at the end of the chapter. - Each example is a `compare` container that holds the Carve input and the expected HTML. The line above it gives its number and its status. *Generated* means the HTML was produced by the 0.1 reference engine, because the 0.2 rule equals 0.1 behavior for that input. *Unverified* means the HTML was written by hand from the clauses and has not been run through any engine. - "Lint" and "diagnostic" name reports. They never change the blocks. ## Preliminaries Terms: - A *line* is a run of characters up to a line end (C2-B-010). A *blank line* holds only spaces and tabs. - A *container* is a block that holds other blocks: a quote, a list item, a description, a footnote body, a div. A *leaf* holds text: a paragraph, a heading, a term, a caption, a code block, a table row. - The *container stack* is the list of containers open at a line, outermost first. - A *marker* is a list marker, a description mark (`:`), a term mark (`::`) or a footnote definition marker. The *marker column* is the column of its first character. The *content column* is the column of the first content character on the marker line. - A *prefix* is what a line carries to stay inside an open container: the quote mark for a quote, indent for an item, a description or a footnote body. - The *indent* of a line is the column of its first character that is not a space or a tab. Indent that remains after the prefixes of the open containers is skipped before the shape of a line is tested, so a heading, a quote, a table row or a list marker may stand at any indent. The clauses that pin a column say so: a definition and a frontmatter opener stand at column 0 (C2-B-081, C2-B-161). - A marker, a mark or an opener that needs *content* needs at least one character that is not a space or a tab behind it on its line. Spaces and tabs alone are no content, since they are dropped at the end of a line (C2-I-002). **C2-B-001** The role of a line depends only on that line, the stack of open blocks and five facts the scanner keeps about the lines directly above. The stack of open blocks is the open containers and, innermost, the open leaf with what its opener set: the kind of the leaf, the first line and the line count of a text leaf (C2-B-017, C2-B-157), the marker column of a heading (C2-B-154), the closer and the opener column of a fence (C2-B-109, C2-B-110), and the rows and head of a table (C2-B-178, C2-B-187). The five facts are: whether the line is line 1 of the document (C2-B-161), the pending attribute lines (C2-B-090), the number of blank lines directly above (C2-B-052), the block that closed directly above, for a caption (C2-B-146), and the blank lines held back at the end of an opaque body (C2-B-113). A pending attribute line waits for the next line (C2-B-092); no other block fact waits for a later line. **C2-B-003** Columns count code points from 0, starting after the quote marks of the open quotes: column 0 of quoted content is the column directly behind the innermost quote mark and its one space. **C2-B-004** A leading tab advances the column to the next multiple of 4, for counting only: the bytes are kept as written, also in code. **C2-B-005** Tab stops count from the start of the line, not from a container's content column. **C2-B-007** Indent stripping removes whole characters, so a tab that straddles the strip column is kept. **C2-B-008** Prefixes are read outside-in, in the order the containers were opened: for a quote inside a list item the quote mark sits past the item's marker. **C2-B-009** A blank line belongs to no container: the next line that is not blank decides which containers stay open, so an indented line belongs to its item after any number of blank lines. A quote is the exception: a blank line without its mark ends it at once (C2-B-032). **C2-B-218** A U+0000 in the source is read as U+FFFD, in text, in code and in every other value, so a tree from a parse never holds U+0000 (C2-A-044). Offsets count the bytes of the source as it stands. An unpaired surrogate in the string a host passes is read as U+FFFD in the same way and counts three bytes. A source given as bytes is decoded as UTF-8 by the WHATWG decoder: each maximal subpart of an ill-formed sequence is read as one U+FFFD, and offsets still count the source bytes, so the U+FFFD spans the bytes it replaces, and a layout sidecar keeps such a source as bytes (C2-L-056). The bytes `61 FF 62` give the paragraph `a`, U+FFFD, `b`, whose characters span offsets 0 to 1, 1 to 2 and 2 to 3; the bytes `61 E2 82 62` give `a`, one U+FFFD over offsets 1 to 3, and `b`. A source is never refused for its encoding. **C2-B-010** A line ends at LF, a CR directly before that LF is not part of the line, and a lone CR is not a line end. The second paragraph below starts with a tab, which counts as indent to column 4. Example 1 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve - a b ``` ```html

    b

``` ::: ## Paragraphs and interrupters **C2-B-011** A line that opens no other block opens a paragraph. **C2-B-012** An open paragraph takes every line that is not blank, whatever its indent or prefix, and such a line is a *lazy line*. **C2-B-013** A paragraph closes at a blank line, at an interrupter or with its container. An *interrupter* is a line that ends an open paragraph without a blank line. There are six. **C2-B-014** Interrupter (a): a fence line, which is a run of three or more backticks, colons or percent signs that opens or closes a fence, a div or a comment block (C2-B-108). **C2-B-015** Interrupter (b): a list marker with content at an open list's column continues that list when its marker matches under C2-B-049. A marker left of every open list continues the outermost open list when its marker matches under C2-B-049 and the container that holds that list owns the line (C2-B-025); otherwise it closes the open lists and opens a new one, whatever its value, in the innermost container that owns the line (C2-B-228).
