The whole value is checked before any entry is applied: every entry, one past the last column included, must have this form, and an empty or malformed entry makes the whole value invalid, so that it sets no column. Entries past the last column set nothing. Fewer entries than columns are valid: the remaining columns stay unset, and `table-column-arity` reports it. `valigns` is the same list for the vertical axis: an entry is `top`, `middle` or `bottom` and sets `valign` of that `table_column`. **C2-B-212** `widths` is a list of entries separated by commas, by position like `aligns`, and its whole value is checked in the same way before any entry is applied (C2-B-211). An entry is a decimal number greater than 0 and at most 100. It is a percentage of the table width, and sets `width` of that `table_column` to the number divided by 100: `25` gives `0.25`. An empty entry or any other entry makes the whole value invalid, so that it sets no column. Entries past the last column set nothing, and fewer entries are valid. The widths need not total 100; `table-width-total` reports a total above 100. **C2-B-220** A decimal number in a `widths` entry is one or more ASCII digits, optionally followed by a dot and one or more ASCII digits. `30.5` and `5` are entries; `.5`, `5.`, `1e1` and `+5` are not, and such an entry makes the value invalid (C2-B-212). **C2-B-213** The alignment of a cell is resolved for each axis on its own. The cell's own mark for that axis (C2-B-182) wins. Then comes the mark for that axis of the last header cell in the head that starts in the cell's column and carries a mark for that axis, then the entry of that column in `aligns` for the horizontal axis and in `valigns` for the vertical axis. Otherwise the cell has no alignment on that axis. A mark on any other cell applies to that cell only, and a header cell that spans several columns gives its marks only to the column it starts in. Where a head mark and an `aligns` or `valigns` entry set the same axis of a column, `table-column-overlap` reports it. Example 273 (generated) ::: compare ```carve {valigns="top,bottom" aligns="left,right"} |= A |={?^} B | | a | b | ``` ```html
AB
ab
``` ::: Each axis resolves on its own: column 2 takes its horizontal alignment from `aligns` and its vertical alignment from the head mark `^`, which wins over the `bottom` of `valigns`. Both keys are consumed and not written to HTML (C2-B-227, C2-H-153). Reported: `table-column-overlap`. **C2-B-214** `header-cols` has no effect on a pipe table or a delimited table: there it is an ordinary key. **C2-B-227** A table reads `aligns`, `valigns`, `widths`, `header-rows`, `footer-rows`, `body-rows`, `body-header-rows` and `body-header-cols` from its `attrs`. A key whose value is valid and that applies to the table form is removed from `attrs` once its effect is recorded in the tree, in the groups or in the column fields (C2-A-088, C2-A-089). A valid count that the table clamps (C2-B-187, C2-B-209) is consumed too. A key whose value is invalid (C2-B-210 to C2-B-212, C2-B-230), and `header-rows` on a pipe table (C2-B-186), has no effect and stays in `attrs`. Lint reports a kept invalid value as `table-attribute-invalid`; `deprecated-table-attribute` reports `header-rows` on a pipe table. **C2-B-230** `body-rows` splits the rows between the head and the foot into bodies, one `table_body` each in source order. Its value is a list of entries separated by commas, spaces around an entry ignored, one entry per body giving its data rows. An entry of `body-rows` and of `body-header-rows` is one or more decimal digits; unlike a count (C2-B-210) it has no empty form. `0` is an empty body, and an empty value gives no body. `body-header-rows`, one entry per body, puts that many rows before the data rows of its body, and every cell of such a row is a header cell. `body-header-cols`, one entry per body, sets `rowHeadColumns` of its body (C2-A-088), and an empty entry sets none; the cells of those columns stay data cells in the tree and are written as header cells (C2-H-056). `body-rows` can stand alone. The two header lists need `body-rows` and exactly one entry per body, and the header and data rows of the bodies must be exactly the rows between the head and the foot; where a value breaks one of these rules, none of the three keys has an effect. The head stays that of C2-B-178 or C2-B-209, so a pipe table writes its head with header marks, not `header-rows` (C2-B-186). The body keys split the rows below the head into two bodies; the second body starts with a header row, and the first body's first column holds row headers (C2-B-230). The cells of the header row are header cells of a body, so they take `scope="row"` (C2-H-056). Example 277 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve {body-rows=1,1 body-header-rows=0,1 body-header-cols=1,0 footer-rows=1} |= Item |= Qty | | tea | 2 | | Later | | | milk | 1 | | Total | 3 | ``` ```html
ItemQty
tea2
Later
milk1
Total3
``` ::: Example 229 (generated) ::: compare ```carve {aligns="left,left,center" widths="25,25"} |={>} Name |={<} Qty |= Note | | tea |{~} 2 | hot | | milk | 3 | cold | ``` ```html
NameQtyNote
tea2hot
milk3cold
``` ::: One malformed entry makes each list invalid, so no column is set and both keys stay in `attrs`. No key is written as an HTML attribute (C2-B-227, C2-H-153). Example 239 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve {aligns=right,x widths=25,,25 footer-rows=two .t} | a | b | | c | d | ``` ```html
ab
cd
``` ::: Example 230 (unverified) :::: compare ````carve {table} ```csv Name,Price tea,2 ``` {table header-rows=0} ```csv a,b ``` {table header-rows=5} ```csv a,b c,d ``` ```` ```html
NamePrice
tea2
ab
ab
cd
``` :::: A pipe table and a delimited table with the same cells in the same groups give equal trees, also where the delimited table declares its partition (C2-A-088, C2-L-023): Examples 267 and 268 have the same tree and the same HTML. The count `0` is a fact of the sidecar of Example 268 (C2-L-057). Example 267 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve | a | b | | 1 | 2 | ``` ```html
ab
12
``` ::: Example 268 (unverified) ::: compare ````carve {table header-rows=0} ```csv a,b 1,2 ``` ```` ```html
ab
12
``` ::: **C2-B-226** The body of a delimited table is read as records, in the manner of RFC 4180. The separator is a comma for `csv` and a tab for `tsv`. The language word is matched as written, so a `CSV` fence is a code block that keeps its attribute. A line ending ends a row, except inside quotes. A cell that starts with `"` is quoted up to the next `"` that is not doubled: a doubled `""` stands for one `"`, and separators and line endings inside are part of the cell; what stands between the closing quote and the next separator or line ending is added to the cell as written. A `"` anywhere else is an ordinary character. Cells are not trimmed. A cell is plain text: no inline form is read in it, and its `cell_paragraph` holds one `text` node (C2-A-215), or none for an empty cell. A separator always starts another cell, so a row that ends in one has an empty last cell. An empty line is a row of one empty cell, except that one empty line at the end of the body is dropped. An empty body has no rows. The cells keep their spaces and their stars, a doubled quote is one quote, and a quoted cell holds a line break (C2-B-226). Example 234 (unverified) ::: compare `````carve {table} ```csv a,"b ""q"" c", d *x*, "m n"x,y ``` {table} ```CSV a,b ``` {table} ```tsv a b,c ``` ````` ```html
ab "q" c d
*x*
m nxy
 
a,b
ab,c
``` ::: A trailing comment after a row attribute and after a bare closing pipe leaves the line a row (C2-B-167). The comments are in the tree and write nothing. Example 235 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve | 1 | 2 |{.r} %% note | 3 | 4 | %% n2 ``` ```html
12
34
``` ::: ## The fallback rule A line that is not a valid opener is text (C2-B-011). **C2-B-189** Whether a line is an opener is decided on that line alone and never by whether a closer follows, so a construct with a closer of its own always opens (C2-B-111). **C2-B-190** Block nesting stops at depth 200: each open quote, list, item, description list, description, footnote body and div counts one, and while 200 are open an opener of one more is text. Inline nodes do not count; inline content has its own limit (C2-I-118). A marker that opens two containers at once, a list and its item or a description list and its first description, is tested as one: when both do not fit, the whole marker is text and neither opens. Example 247 (unverified) The input is one line of 201 quote marks, each `>` and one space, followed by `x`. The first 200 marks open 200 nested quotes. The last mark is text, so the innermost quote holds `

> x

`. With 200 marks it holds `

x

`. Example 221 (generated) ::: compare ```carve -a >c :d ======= ``` ```html

-a

>c

:d

=======

``` ::: Example 222 (generated) ::: compare ```carve ::: note text ``` ```html

text

``` ::: Example 223 (generated) ::: compare ```carve %%% hidden ``` ```html ``` ::: ## Facts set at close **C2-B-191** Five facts are set on a node when its block closes and are not roles of a line: the promotion of a block image (C2-B-157), a math block (C2-B-158), the attachment of a caption (C2-B-147), the tightness of a list (C2-B-062) and the footer rows of a table (C2-B-187). A streaming writer therefore buffers one paragraph, one captioned block, one list or one table. The last row becomes the footer when the table closes. Example 224 (generated) ::: compare ```carve {footer-rows=1} | a | | b | | c | ``` ```html
a
b
c
``` ::: The list is loose from its first item, though the blank line comes after it. Example 225 (generated) ::: compare ```carve - one - two - three ``` ```html

  • one

  • two

  • three

``` ::: ## Counts Budget: at most 25 exceptions. Every normative statement of the chapter has a clause id. | Construct | Clauses | Exceptions | Examples generated | Examples unverified | |---|---|---|---|---| | Preliminaries | 9 | 0 | 4 | 4 | | Paragraphs and interrupters | 14 | 2 | 6 | 4 | | Container ownership and stripping | 7 | 0 | 3 | 7 | | Block quotes | 2 | 0 | 5 | 0 | | Bullet lists | 3 | 0 | 3 | 0 | | Ordered lists | 11 | 1 | 10 | 4 | | Task items | 3 | 0 | 1 | 5 | | Siblings, adjacency and the three-blank-line boundary | 7 | 1 | 6 | 1 | | Nested lists and the marker line | 5 | 0 | 5 | 1 | | Tightness | 3 | 0 | 2 | 3 | | Description lists | 14 | 0 | 12 | 5 | | Definitions | 8 | 0 | 7 | 7 | | Attribute lines | 17 | 1 | 12 | 11 | | Fences, divs and comment blocks | 10 | 0 | 6 | 6 | | The fence opener and titles | 7 | 1 | 4 | 9 | | Sigil divs | 10 | 0 | 11 | 3 | | Comments | 12 | 2 | 14 | 10 | | Captions | 6 | 0 | 12 | 3 | | Headings | 5 | 0 | 3 | 6 | | One-line constructs | 11 | 0 | 8 | 5 | | Thematic break | 2 | 0 | 4 | 1 | | Frontmatter | 5 | 0 | 5 | 2 | | Tables | 35 | 0 | 22 | 21 | | The fallback rule | 2 | 0 | 3 | 1 | | Facts set at close | 1 | 0 | 2 | 0 | | **Total** | **209** | **8** | **170** | **119** | The chapter has 209 clauses, and 8 exceptions against a budget of 25. The clause count includes the exceptions. Clause ids are stable: a clause added after id 191 takes the next free number and stands at the end of its section, so ids are not in document order from there on. Freeze candidate 4 deleted C2-B-006, C2-B-023, C2-B-047, C2-B-056, C2-B-134, C2-B-139, C2-B-142, C2-B-143 and C2-B-177, and freeze candidate 5 deleted C2-B-086, whose general rules give the same result; their ids are not reused. The reduction of 17 November 2026 deleted C2-B-002, C2-B-063, C2-B-064, C2-B-094, C2-B-099, C2-B-103, C2-B-114, C2-B-129, C2-B-144 and C2-B-150, whose rule other clauses state or give; their ids are not reused. ## Not covered The chapter has no example for a list-table or for a lone CR.
text.carve://spec/syntax-inline:
# Carve 0.2 Syntax: inline content Status: part of the freeze candidate of Carve 0.2 on `next2`, frozen with the rest of the core (`STATUS.md` names the candidate). This chapter defines how inline content becomes inline nodes. Block structure, HTML rendering, the tree and the writer have their own documents. Where a clause states rendered output, it does so because the output is the only visible sign of an inline decision. Conventions: - A clause is a paragraph that starts with an id of the form `C2-I-nnn`. The prefix is new in 0.2. No 0.1 clause id is reused. Ids of the form `C2-B-nnn` name clauses of the block chapter. - A clause that starts with the word "Exception" is a carve-out from a more general clause, or a named interaction between two constructs. Exceptions are counted at the end of the chapter. - Each example is a `compare` container that holds the Carve input and the expected HTML. The line above it gives its number and its status. *Generated* means the HTML was produced by the 0.1 reference engine, because the 0.2 rule equals 0.1 behavior for that input. *Unverified* means the HTML was written by hand from the clauses and has not been run through any engine. - "Lint" and "diagnostic" name reports. They never change the nodes. ## Preliminaries Terms: - *Leaf* and *container* have the meaning of the block chapter. Inline content is read in a paragraph, a heading, a term, a caption, a line of a line block and each cell of a table row. - The *content* is the text of one of these, as the block pass left it. A table row is split into cells first, and each cell has a content of its own. Every rule below works on one content. - A *form* is one spelling of a construct, such as the braced form of emphasis. The `form` field of a reference node is written as a code word. - A *word character* is a Unicode letter or number (general category L or N, of the version C2-I-127 pins). - *Whitespace* is a space, a tab or a line break. The start and the end of the content count as whitespace. Where a rule tests the character before or after a position (C2-I-023, C2-I-047, C2-I-048, C2-I-104), a no-break space counts as whitespace too, written as a backslash and a space (C2-I-011) or as the character U+00A0. It does not count where a rule needs a space as a separator, such as after a block marker. - Two things are *glued* when no character stands between them. - An *atom* is a form whose characters are taken as one token. The atoms are listed under C2-I-005. - A *bracket construct* is a form built on a bracket pair: a span, a link, an image, a reference, an inline footnote, an inline extension. - A *host* is an inline node that an attribute block can attach to (C2-I-036). The program that embeds Carve is called the application. **C2-I-001** Inline content is parsed one content at a time, after the block pass has settled every line of the document: no block decision depends on inline content, and every definition and heading is known when the first content is read. **C2-I-002** A content is the list of its source spans in order, one per line, without the prefixes of its containers, without markers and without indent. Spaces and tabs at the end of a line of the content are not part of it, on the last line as on the others; a space that a backslash escapes is not such a space (C2-I-011). They are removed before any inline form is read, so the rule holds inside a code span, a math span, a literal span, a raw span and a comment as in text. The test is lexical: a space behind an odd run of backslashes is kept, also inside a form that reads no escapes (C2-I-013). A tab behind a backslash is removed like any other tab at the end of a line. In a table cell the padding before the closing pipe is removed first, so a backslash that stands before that padding ends the cell and is a hard break (C2-I-102). A no-break space at the end of a cell therefore has no spelling (C2-W-117). A code span over two lines, whose first line is `` `a\ ``, which ends in a backslash and one space, and whose second line is `` b` ``, has the value `a\ `, a line feed and `b`. With a tab in place of that space the value is `a\`, a line feed and `b`. The two spaces before the pipe are padding and are removed first, so the backslash ends the cell and is a hard break (C2-I-002, C2-I-102). Example 120 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve | a\ | ``` ```html
a
``` ::: **C2-I-003** Two neighboring spans are joined by one line break. **C2-I-004** The content is read in one left-to-right scan with four steps in a fixed order of precedence: atoms, the bracket stack, the delimiter stack, attachment. **C2-I-005** At each position the scan tries the atoms first. An atom that matches is taken whole: no bracket, delimiter or other atom opens, closes or is matched inside it, and of two atoms the one that starts first wins. The atoms, each defined in its own section: - a backslash escape; - a code span, with its `!`, `$` or `$$` prefix and with a raw-format marker; - an autolink and a cross-reference; - a valid attribute block; - a braced comment, an editorial comment and a line comment; - a link tail, which is the parenthesized destination and title glued to the closing bracket of a pair; - a mention, a tag and a symbol. **C2-I-006** An opening bracket is pushed on the bracket stack. A closing bracket pairs with the nearest open one, and what is glued to the closing bracket decides the construct. Where no glued tail forms another construct, C2-I-072 tests the pair for a defined shortcut. A pair that forms no construct is plain text: its content is read as inline content all the same, and it bounds nothing. A closing bracket with no open bracket is text. **C2-I-007** A bracket construct is settled before delimiters pair: a delimiter inside its content pairs only inside it, and a delimiter outside it pairs only outside it. **C2-I-008** Emphasis, strong and the braced forms pair on one delimiter stack (C2-I-051, C2-I-059). **C2-I-009** Attachment comes last: an attribute block attaches only to a host that has already formed. The backtick opens a code span before the star can close, so the strong span never forms. The block pass comes first: the blank line ends the paragraph, and neither the star nor the code span reaches across it. Example 1 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve *a b* and `c d` ``` ```html

*a

b* and `c

d`

``` ::: The quote marks are no part of the content, so the strong span crosses the line break. Example 2 (generated) ::: compare ```carve > *a > b* c ``` ```html

a b c

``` ::: Example 3 (generated) ::: compare ```carve *a `b* c` ``` ```html

*a b* c

``` ::: The link forms first. The star inside it has no partner inside, and the star outside has none outside. Example 4 (generated) ::: compare ```carve *a [b* c](/u) ``` ```html

*a b* c

``` ::: The brackets form no construct, so the stars pair across them. Example 5 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve *a [b* c] d ``` ```html

a [b c] d

``` ::: **C2-I-127** Every general category and every character property that a clause of the 0.2 documents names is that of Unicode 18.0.0, whatever Unicode version the host runtime has. `data/unicode-categories.json` lists the code points of the categories L, M, N and Cf of that version, generated from its `UnicodeData.txt`; a code point that Unicode 18.0.0 leaves unassigned is in none of them. The display width of the writer reads the same version (C2-W-119). U+3D000 is a letter that Unicode 18.0.0 assigned. The star behind it does not open, so no strong span forms (C2-I-047, C2-I-127). Example 110 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve 𽀀*𰨌* ``` ```html

𽀀*𰨌*

``` ::: ## Backslash escapes **C2-I-010** A backslash before an ASCII punctuation character makes that character literal text: it opens, closes and starts nothing. **C2-I-011** A backslash before a space is a no-break space, except at the end of a line, where the two are a hard break (C2-I-102). In every test of the character before or after a position it counts as whitespace, as U+00A0 does: in `a\ "b"` the first quote opens (C2-I-104), and `*\ a*` holds no strong. **C2-I-012** A backslash before any other character is a literal backslash, except at the end of a line, where it is a hard break (C2-I-102). **C2-I-013** Escapes are not read inside a code span, an autolink, a cross-reference, a comment or an editorial comment. A link destination reads only the escaped parenthesis and the escaped backslash. A link title and a quoted attribute value read escapes. Example 6 (generated) ::: compare ```carve \*not strong\* and \# and a\ b and \a and C:\dir ``` ```html

*not strong* and # and a b and \a and C:\dir

``` ::: Example 7 (generated) ::: compare ```carve `a\*b` and [x](/a\(b) and \[not a span]{.c} ``` ```html

a\*b and x and [not a span]{.c}

``` ::: ## Code spans **C2-I-014** A run of one or more backticks opens a code span. The opener is the whole run. **C2-I-015** The span closes at the next backtick run of exactly the opener's length. Everything between is code: no escape and no other form is read there, and a line break is content. The spaces and tabs at the end of each line are removed before the span is read (C2-I-002): `` `a ``, two spaces, a line break and `` b` `` give the value `a`, a line feed and `b`. **C2-I-016** When the content of a closed span starts and ends with a space and holds a character that is not a space, one space is removed from each end. Content of spaces only is kept as it is. **C2-I-017** A backtick run with no closing run of its length later in the same content opens nothing (C2-I-119): the run is text, and so is a `!`, `$` or `$$` glued before it. The scan goes on behind the run, so a shorter or longer run after it may open a span. This holds for a code span, a literal-text span and a math span alike, and in a table cell as anywhere: the cell `` | x `a | `` holds the text `` x `a ``. For this test a comment-only line ends the content (C2-B-138). **C2-I-018** A `!` glued before the opening run makes a literal-text span: its content is written as escaped text with no code element. With an attribute block it is written as a span element that carries the attributes. A literal `!` before a code span is written with a backslash. Example 8 (generated) ::: compare ```carve `code` and `` a ` b `` and ` x ` and `*a*` ``` ```html

code and a ` b and x and *a*

``` ::: Example 9 (generated) ::: compare ```carve a `b c` d ``` ```html

a b c d

``` ::: Example 10 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve see `unclosed *x* and [y](/u) ``` ```html

see `unclosed x and y

``` ::: Example 11 (generated) ::: compare ```carve !`/kaet/` and !`a`{.ipa} and \!`x` ``` ```html

/kaet/ and a<b> and !x

``` ::: ## Math spans **C2-I-019** A `$` glued before a code span makes inline math, and `$$` makes display math. The content is the span's verbatim text. A `$` with no backtick run after it is text. Example 12 (generated) ::: compare ```carve $`x^2` and $$`E = mc^2` and $5 and $`x`{.c} ``` ```html

\(x^2\) and \[E = mc^2\] and $5 and \(x\)

``` ::: Example 13 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve the sum $`a + b ``` ```html

the sum $`a + b

``` ::: ## Raw inline **C2-I-021** A closed plain code span with `{=name}` glued to it, `name` a raw format name (C2-B-225), is raw inline; the marker is tried together with the attribute block, before the highlight opener. The content is written unescaped to the output format of that name and dropped for every other format. Anywhere else, after a literal-text span or a math span too, `{=` is read as a braced opener (C2-I-043). A raw format name starts with an ASCII letter, so `{=_a}` makes no raw span. Example 123 (generated) ::: compare ```carve `x`{=_a} ``` ```html

x{=_a}

``` ::: Raw HTML is written only when the `rawHtml` option allows it. That is a rendering rule. Example 14 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve a `
`{=html} b ``` ```html

a <br> b

``` ::: Example 15 (generated) ::: compare ```carve `
`{=html .c} and [s]{=html} and $`x`{=html} ``` ```html

<br>{=html .c} and [s]{=html} and \(x\){=html}

``` ::: ## Comments Carve has three comment forms. The block form `%%%` is defined in the block chapter. The line form and the braced form are inline atoms. **C2-I-023** `%%` at the start of a line of the content or after whitespace starts a line comment. It runs to the end of that line and renders nothing, and the spaces before it are dropped with it. Elsewhere `%%` is text, also directly after the opener of a bracket or a braced form: the start of their content is neither a line start nor whitespace. **C2-I-024** A line comment takes the rest of its line, every closer on it included. A form that is open at the comment stays open: a matching closer on a later line of the same paragraph closes it, and an opener that never closes is text. Example 128 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve a ^[see b %% check *this*] c ``` ```html

a ^[see b

``` ::: Inside an atom that started earlier on the line, `%%` is content (C2-I-005): in a code span, in a link tail and in a quoted attribute value. The limits in a table row, in an opaque body such as a code fence, and in a line block are block clauses (C2-B-169, C2-B-135). **C2-I-025** `{%` opens a braced comment that closes at the first `%}` in the content. It may cross line breaks, it does not nest, and it renders nothing. **Exception C2-I-026** A braced comment counts as nothing for its neighbors: the characters on its two sides are tested as if they were glued, for delimiter conditions (C2-I-047), for the sigil boundary (C2-I-090) and for typography. For delimiter conditions this is carried over from 0.1; 0.1 read a braced comment as a boundary before a sigil and before a single quote, so `a{%%}#tag` gave a tag and `a {%%}'word` an apostrophe (U-363, U-364). Example 16 (generated) ::: compare ```carve a %% comment b and 50%% and a%%b ``` ```html

a b and 50%% and a%%b

``` ::: The comment takes the closing star. The strong span closes on the next line. Example 17 (generated) ::: compare ```carve *a %% b* c* d ``` ```html

a c d

``` ::: The comment takes the closing bracket, so the link does not form (C2-I-024). Example 18 (unverified) ::: compare ```carve [a %% b](/u) c ``` ```html

[a

``` ::: Example 19 (generated) ::: compare ```carve `a %% b` and [a](/u%%20c) and [a]{k="a %% b"} ``` ```html

a %% b and a and a

``` ::: Example 20 (generated) ::: compare ```carve a {% one two %} b and *bo{% c %}ld* and a {% oops ``` ```html

``` ::: ## Smart typography Smart typography reads the text that the scan left as text and never reads inside an atom. Each match is a `smart_punctuation` node that keeps the typed characters in its `source` field (C2-A-098). The node is always built. The `smartTypography` option is a render option: it selects the glyph or the typed characters when the node is written (C2-H-078), and it does not change the tree. Where a clause below says that characters become a glyph, it names the glyph of that node. **C2-I-104** A straight quote, `"` or `'`, is read from its two neighbors alone, as C2-I-117 defines them: the characters of the same text on each side of it. A mark of a delimiter, a bracket that belongs to a construct and an atom are no neighbors, and a braced comment is transparent (C2-I-026). A no-break space and a hard break are whitespace (C2-I-011, C2-I-102). A quote opens when the neighbor before it is whitespace or opening punctuation, or when it has none because the quote stands at the start of the content or directly behind an opening mark or bracket. Otherwise it closes, also directly behind a closing mark, a closing bracket or an atom. Opening punctuation is one of `(`, `[`, `{`, `=`, `:`, `“` and `‘`, or a straight quote that opens. No quote looks past its neighbors and none depends on another quote that is not its neighbor: quotes do not pair, so an opening quote without a closing quote stays an opening quote. **Exception C2-I-105** A single quote before an ASCII digit closes, also where C2-I-104 would open it. A single quote between two word characters closes by C2-I-104. Both are the apostrophe, which has the kind and the glyph of a closing single quote. Where the guess is wrong, the author types the curly character. **C2-I-111** A run of two or more hyphens becomes dashes: a length divisible by three gives em dashes, otherwise a length divisible by two gives en dashes, otherwise one em dash followed by the rest under the same rule. The rule has no exception for the place of the run: `run --verbose` holds an en dash, and a command-line flag in prose is written in a code span or with an escape, `-\-verbose`. In 0.1 a run after whitespace and before a letter stayed as typed, and `{--}` spelled the en dash there; both are gone, and `{--}` is now an opening brace, an en dash and a closing brace. **C2-I-114** Three dots become an ellipsis. **C2-I-115** Six runs become arrows: `-->`, `<--`, `<-->`, `==>`, `<==` and `<=>`. The longest match is taken, among these runs and the runs of C2-I-117 together, so `<=>` is the arrow and not `<=` followed by `>`. The single forms `->`, `<-` and `=>` are text. Only replaced runs take part in the match: `->`, `<-` and `=>` take no characters, so `->=` holds the text `-` and the sign for `>=`. **Exception C2-I-116** An arrow is matched before a hyphen run is split, and an arrow of hyphens needs its exact run: a longer hyphen run next to `<` or `>` is a dash run. That test reads a shape, not parsed inline content. **C2-I-121** A display math span is `$$`, a backtick run, the content and a closing backtick run of the opener's length (C2-I-019, C2-I-015). A line consists of exactly one display math span when it starts with `$$` and the opening run, the closing run stands on the same line, and nothing follows it but attribute blocks glued to it and trailing whitespace. Example 107 (generated) ::: compare ```carve $$`E = mc^2` text $$`E = mc^2` ``` ```html

\[E = mc^2\]

text \[E = mc^2\]

``` ::: ## Counts There is no fixed budget for the inline chapter. | Construct | Clauses | Exceptions | Examples generated | Examples unverified | |---|---|---|---|---| | Preliminaries | 10 | 0 | 3 | 4 | | Backslash escapes | 4 | 0 | 2 | 0 | | Code spans | 5 | 0 | 3 | 1 | | Math spans | 1 | 0 | 1 | 1 | | Raw inline | 1 | 0 | 2 | 1 | | Comments | 4 | 1 | 4 | 2 | | Attribute blocks | 12 | 2 | 7 | 5 | | The opening brace | 1 | 0 | 3 | 1 | | Emphasis and strong | 8 | 3 | 7 | 6 | | Braced delimiters | 9 | 1 | 6 | 4 | | Spans | 1 | 0 | 2 | 0 | | Links and images | 12 | 1 | 6 | 2 | | Reference resolution | 13 | 3 | 5 | 17 | | Footnotes | 3 | 0 | 1 | 2 | | Mention, tag, symbol and inline extension | 6 | 0 | 3 | 3 | | Cross-references | 2 | 0 | 1 | 1 | | Abbreviations | 3 | 1 | 1 | 0 | | Citations | 1 | 0 | 0 | 1 | | Hard break and soft break | 2 | 0 | 3 | 1 | | Smart typography | 7 | 2 | 7 | 6 | | The depth limit | 1 | 0 | 0 | 3 | | The fallback rule | 2 | 0 | 2 | 0 | | The display math line | 1 | 0 | 1 | 0 | | **Total** | **109** | **14** | **70** | **61** | The chapter has 109 clauses, 14 of them exceptions, and 131 examples. The clause count includes the exceptions. Freeze candidate 4 deleted C2-I-027, C2-I-037, C2-I-038, C2-I-044, C2-I-054 and C2-I-065, whose general rules give the same result; their ids are not reused. The reduction of 17 November 2026 deleted C2-I-022, C2-I-041 and C2-I-045, whose rule other clauses state or give; their ids are not reused. For comparison, counted with the rubric of the inline review (one atomic statement per rule): | Document | Inline rules | Exceptions | |---|---|---| | Carve 0.1 | about 204 | 30 | | CommonMark 0.31.2 | about 80 | 6 | | Djot | about 50 | 2 | | This chapter | 119 | 22 | The numbers are not like for like. Several clauses here join two or three atomic statements, as the first draft of the block chapter did, so a strict recount lands higher. Carve also has about 35 inline constructs against 20 in Djot and 11 in CommonMark. ## Not covered The citation syntax itself is defined with its extension. The element a span becomes for the keys `kbd`, `abbr` and `time`, footnote numbering, the links of mentions and tags, the `mailto:` link of an email autolink, the symbol table and URL filtering belong to the HTML rendering document. That a line of a line block keeps its leading spaces is a block rule.

# Carve 0.2: tooling

Status: part of the freeze candidate of Carve 0.2 on `next2` (`STATUS.md`).

This document defines what every engine offers a caller: the library calls and the command line program built on them, with its flags, streams, exit codes and reports. The options are the rows of `data/options.json` (C2-H-137); this document only says how each command reads them. The commands, flags, categories, calls and entry fields are also in `data/cli.json`.

## Scope

**C2-T-001** Every engine offers the calls of the section "Library" and the program of the section "Commands". A port spells a call, a result field and an error by the convention of its language, as it spells an option (C2-H-137).

**C2-T-002** The program is `carve`.

**C2-T-003** Outside this specification are the Markdown, GFM and Djot importers of the reference engine (`--from markdown`, `gfm` and `djot`), its `upgrade` command, which is part of the JavaScript engine only and is described in `UPGRADING.md` ("Running the rewrite tool"), its `diff` command, which the calls of C2-T-043 to C2-T-046 serve on the command line, the directory import and the editor adapters of its `import` command (C2-M-100), and its scanner and event helpers. Every engine also offers Markdown, plain-text and ANSI export renderers through its library API and `carve render --to markdown`, `--to plain` and `--to ansi`. Their output, options and export-only loss codes are engine behavior outside this specification; those codes are outside `data/lint-rules.json` (C2-W-106). An engine may offer further commands, flags, flag values and calls; none of them takes a name of `data/cli.json` with another meaning.

**C2-T-004** `data/cli.json` holds the commands, flags, failure categories, calls and entry fields of this document. A row is normative together with the clauses it cites; where a row and its clause disagree, the clause wins.

## Library

**C2-T-005** An engine offers the calls of this table. Each reads the options of `data/options.json` whose `read_by` names a stage the call runs and refuses the others (C2-H-137). `decodeTree` and `validateTree` read `extensions` as the registered standard extensions for their tree reader checks (C2-X-038).

| Call | Takes | Returns | Clauses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `parse` | Carve source as text or bytes, the parse and resolution options, `positions` (default on) | the resolved tree | C2-A-106, C2-B-218 |
| `parseWithDiagnostics` | as `parse` | the tree, the diagnostics record and `suppressedDiagnostics` | C2-A-172, C2-T-024 |
| `parseWithLayout` | as `parse` | the tree, the layout sidecar and the record | C2-A-003 |
| `render` | Carve source or a tree, the parse, resolution and render options | HTML | C2-H-137 |
| `renderWithDiagnostics` | as `render` | HTML, the record and `suppressedDiagnostics` | C2-A-172, C2-H-130 |
| `format` | Carve source, `alignTables`, `normalize`, `extensions` | Carve source | C2-W-001, C2-W-134 |
| `formatWithDiagnostics` | as `format` | Carve source and the record | C2-W-134 |
| `write` | a tree, optionally its sidecar, `alignTables`, `extensions` | Carve source | C2-W-001, C2-W-102 |
| `writeWithDiagnostics` | as `write` | Carve source and the record | C2-W-134 |
| `lint` | Carve source, `rules`, `platforms`, `includes`, `extensions`, `headingIds` | the record | C2-W-103, C2-W-109, C2-N-085, C2-T-042 |
| `importDocument` | HTML text, `from: "html"`, `rawHtml`, `strictLosses`, `labels` | the tree, its Carve source and the record | C2-M-001, C2-M-066, C2-M-082, C2-M-100 |
| `includeDependencies` | a tree | its dependencies | C2-N-083 |
| `encodeTree` | a tree | its JSON text | C2-A-012, C2-A-217 |
| `encodeEnvelope` | a tree | the JSON text of its envelope | C2-A-012 |
| `decodeTree` | the JSON text of a 2.0 tree or envelope, `extensions` | the tree | C2-A-188 |
| `validateTree` | a tree, `extensions` | nothing, or the refusal | C2-A-188 |
| `migrateTree` | the JSON value of a 1.x or draft tree, bare or in an envelope | the 2.0 tree, its envelope where the input was one, and the record | C2-A-178, C2-A-180 |
| `positionOf` | Carve source as text or bytes, an offset in its UTF-8 bytes | `line` and `column` | C2-T-019, C2-T-041 |
| `diffTree` | two trees | a JSON Patch | C2-T-043 |
| `applyPatch` | a tree, a JSON Patch, optionally `fingerprint`, `extensions` | a tree | C2-T-044, C2-T-045 |
| `sourceFingerprint` | Carve source as text or bytes | a fingerprint | C2-T-046 |
| `treeFingerprint` | a tree | a fingerprint | C2-T-046 |

**C2-T-006** A call refuses with the typed error of its row in the table of C2-T-040, and with no other error; the command line turns that error into the category of the row.

**C2-T-043** `diffTree` takes two trees and returns a JSON Patch (RFC 6902): a list of operations that, applied in order by `applyPatch` to the first tree, give a tree whose JSON value is that of the second. Every `path` and `from` is an RFC 6901 pointer into the JSON value of `encodeTree` of the tree the operation applies to, the form of the `path` of a diagnostic (C2-A-173). Two trees whose JSON values are equal give the empty list. The operations an engine chooses and their order are not fixed, so two engines may give two patches for one pair of trees; a host compares the trees a patch gives, not patches.

**C2-T-044** `applyPatch` applies the operations of RFC 6902 (`add`, `remove`, `replace`, `move`, `copy`, `test`) in order to the JSON value of `encodeTree` of the tree and decodes the result as `decodeTree` does (C2-A-188), with the standard extensions of `extensions` registered. It returns the decoded tree and leaves the given tree unchanged. There is no reversible patch and no three-way merge.

**C2-T-045** `applyPatch` refuses with one `CarvePatchError` that carries `path` and `reason`, and applies nothing, in three cases. When `fingerprint` is given and is not the `treeFingerprint` of the tree, `path` is the empty pointer. When an operation is no operation of RFC 6902, its `path` or `from` names no member, or a `test` fails, `path` points into the patch, at the field of that operation (`/0/op`, `/0/path`, `/0/value`). When the result is no tree of contract 2.0, `path` points into the result, at the place where `decodeTree` refuses it.

**C2-T-046** A fingerprint is `sha256:` followed by the 64 lower-case hex digits of the SHA-256 of bytes: for `sourceFingerprint` the UTF-8 bytes of the source as given, text encoded and bytes hashed as they are, with no normalization, so the text and the bytes of one source give one fingerprint; for `treeFingerprint` the UTF-8 bytes of `encodeTree` of the tree (C2-A-217).

## Commands

**C2-T-007** A command line is `carve [COMMAND] [FLAG...] [FILE...]`, and its commands are the rows of this table. With no command it is `render`.

| Command | Reads | Writes on standard output | Clauses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `render` | Carve source, or a tree in JSON with `--from-ast` | HTML and a line feed for each file | C2-H-137 |
| `ast` | Carve source | the tree in JSON and a line feed | C2-A-012 |
| `fmt` | Carve source, or a tree in JSON with `--from-ast` | the canonical source | C2-W-100 |
| `lint` | Carve source | the entries of the call `lint` | C2-W-103 |
| `diagnostics` | Carve source | the entries of the parse channel | C2-A-172 |
| `import` | HTML | the Carve source of the imported tree | C2-M-001 |
| `migrate-ast` | a 1.x or draft tree in JSON | the 2.0 tree in JSON and a line feed | C2-A-180 |
| `flatten` | Carve source | the expanded tree as canonical Carve source | C2-T-047 |
| `fix` | Carve source | what `lint --fix` writes | C2-T-049 |
| `upgrade` | 0.1 source | outside this specification (C2-T-003) | |

**C2-T-008** A flag is `--name value` or `--name=value`. A switch is `--name` and takes no value; `--no-name` turns it off. `--` ends the flags, and every argument after it is a file. A flag that the table of its command does not list is refused with the category `usage`.

**C2-T-009** A flag given twice takes its last value, except `--allow-loss`, which collects every value. `--ignore` collects every value too.

**C2-T-010** A flag that sets an option is named by the option in lower case with hyphens, so `urlPolicy` is `--url-policy`: a `boolean` option is a switch, an `enum` option takes one of its values, and a `list`, `map` or `structure` option takes JSON text. The one option set otherwise is `includes`, which `--includes` and `--include-root` set (C2-T-018). `allowLosses` and `maxLosses` keep the 0.1 flags: `--allow-loss` gives one code per instance (C2-T-027) and `--max-render-losses` the count (C2-T-029). `extensions` and `renderers` take host code, which JSON text cannot name, so they have no flag: they are options of the library calls only (C2-T-005). `codeBlockRenderer` takes host code as well and has no flag either. A value the option refuses is refused with the category `usage`. An option that the table of a command lists no flag for, or whose flag is not given, has its default; for `includes` C2-T-018 says what holds.

## Input and output

**C2-T-011** A file is a path, or `-` for standard input. A command with no file reads standard input. The files are read in order, and the outputs of the files follow each other on standard output.

**C2-T-012** Carve source is read as bytes and is never refused for its encoding (C2-B-218). A tree in JSON is read as strict UTF-8, and a file that is not is refused with the category `input-unreadable`. HTML is read as UTF-8.

**C2-T-013** A line or a report names a file by its path as given and standard input as `<stdin>` (C2-W-100).

**C2-T-014** Standard output carries the product of the command and nothing else. The product of `lint` and `diagnostics` is their entries, as lines or as a report, and that of `fmt --check` and `fmt --diff` the report of C2-W-100; every other line of a diagnostic, a note or a failure goes to standard error.

**C2-T-015** A report flag takes a path, or `-` for standard error. The report is one JSON document for the whole run, followed by a line feed. After repeated instances of one flag have been reduced by C2-T-009, the collision and order rules of this clause apply. Two report flags of one run whose paths resolve to the same absolute path, against the working directory and with `.` and `..` segments removed, are refused with the category `usage` before any input is read. Two report flags with `-` are not refused: both reports go to standard error at the end of the run, in the order of the flags on the command line.

**C2-T-016** `--write` replaces each file whose output differs from it and leaves the others untouched. With standard input among the files it is refused with the category `usage`.

**C2-T-053** `--output` (`-o`) on `render`, `fmt`, `import` and `flatten` takes a path and writes the product of the run to that file instead of standard output, the products of the files before a failure of status 2 included (C2-T-017). `fmt` refuses it with `--write`, `--check` or `--diff`, and a run whose output path resolves to the path of a report flag, as C2-T-015 compares two report paths, is refused, both with the category `usage` before any input is read. A file it cannot write ends the run with the category `output-unwritable`.

**C2-T-017** A failure of status 2 stops the run at its file; what earlier files wrote stays written. Otherwise the status of a run is the highest status of its files.

**C2-T-018** `render`, `ast`, `lint` and `diagnostics` expand includes as C2-N-004 and C2-N-085 state, through the resolver of C2-N-012. `--no-includes` turns expansion off and `--include-root` names the root. `fmt`, `import` and `migrate-ast` expand nothing (C2-N-005), and neither does a command that reads a tree with `--from-ast`.

## Diagnostics and reports

**C2-T-019** A diagnostic line is `FILE:LINE:COLUMN: SEVERITY CODE MESSAGE`, and an entry with no range is written `FILE: SEVERITY CODE MESSAGE`. FILE is the `file` of the entry where it has one (C2-N-063) and the input otherwise. LINE counts line feeds from 1, and COLUMN counts the code points of that line from 1, both at the start of the range.

**C2-T-020** An entry of the record (C2-A-173) is a JSON object with the fields of this table. The library gives every field but `line` and `column`; the command line adds those two where the entry has a range, and to each object of `includedBy`. `includedBy` is the 0.1 field of that name; an engine may give it and a comparison does not require it. The `message` is the text of the engine, for which the catalog row gives the reference wording (C2-W-106); a comparison of two reports does not compare it. A conformance case that states `messageWhen` compares the selected catalog condition separately, as C2-W-106 defines it.

| Field | Value | Present | Clauses |
|---|---|---|---|
| `code` | a code of `data/lint-rules.json` | always | C2-W-106 |
| `severity` | `hint`, `warning` or `error` | always | C2-W-105 |
| `channel` | `parse`, `render-loss` or `lint` | always | C2-W-104 |
| `message` | text | always | C2-A-173 |
| `path` | an RFC 6901 pointer into the tree | where the entry is about a node | C2-A-173 |
| `range` | an object of `startOffset` and `endOffset`, in UTF-8 bytes | where the entry has a position in source | C2-A-173 |
| `file` | the id of the included file the range is counted in | where that is not the top-level document | C2-N-063 |
| `foreignType` | the name of the HTML node | on an entry of the importer that has one | C2-M-081 |
| `includedBy` | the include chain: a list of objects of `file`, absent for the top-level document, and `range`, one per include node from the top-level document inward to the one that read `file` | optional, on an entry that has `file` | C2-N-063 |
| `line` | the LINE of C2-T-019 | on the command line, with `range` | C2-T-019 |
| `column` | the COLUMN of C2-T-019 | on the command line, with `range` | C2-T-019 |

**C2-T-021** A diagnostics report is `{"files": [...]}` with one object per file in order: `file`, the name of C2-T-013; `diagnostics`, the retained entries in the order of the record; and `suppressed`, the number of entries of that file a cap held back (C2-T-024, C2-T-029). `diagnostics --json`, `lint --json` and `--report-losses` write it.

**C2-T-022** An include report is `{"files": [...]}` with one object per file in order: `file`, and `dependencies`, the dependencies of its tree (C2-N-083), each an object of `path`, `from` (the including file, absent for the top-level document), `file` (absent where the include was not read) and `read`. A host that watches files reads it as C2-N-084 says. `--report-includes` writes it.

**C2-T-023** Reports are compared as JSON values: the order of the members of an object is no contract, and the order of a list is.

**C2-T-024** An expansion retains at most `include_diagnostics` of `data/limits.json`, 100, entries whose code is the code of a cause in `data/includes.json`, the first in the order the failures occur. The result of a call that returns a record gives the number of the others as `suppressedDiagnostics`, 0 where there are none, and the command line counts them in `suppressed` (C2-T-021). An include whose entry is held back stays unexpanded as C2-N-061 says.

**C2-T-041** `positionOf` takes a source as `parse` takes it and an offset in its UTF-8 bytes, counted as the offsets of a range are (C2-A-141, C2-B-218), and returns `line` and `column`: the LINE and COLUMN of C2-T-019 for a range that starts at that offset, so a library host shows the positions the command line writes. `line` is 1 plus the number of line feeds before the offset; a carriage return is no line feed. `column` is 1 plus the number of code points between the offset and the last line feed before it, or the start of the source; a U+FFFD that replaces an ill-formed sequence or a U+0000 counts as the one code point it is (C2-B-218). An offset equal to the length of the source gives the position after its last character. An offset that is negative, no integer, greater than the length, or inside the bytes of one code point, an ill-formed sequence that one U+FFFD replaces included, is refused with `CarveOptionError` naming `offset`. The call reads no option.

## Command flags

### Every command

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--help` | switch | writes the usage of the command on standard output and exits with status 0 |
| `--version` | switch | writes the version of the engine and a line feed on standard output and exits with status 0 |

### `carve render`

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--heading-ids` | `off`, `keep-case`, `lower`, `ascii`, `ascii-lower`, `ascii-strict`, `ascii-strict-lower` | the option `headingIds` |
| `--labels` | JSON | the option `labels` |
| `--mode` | `interactive`, `static` | the option `mode` |
| `--profile` | `full`, `article`, `comment`, `minimal` | the option `profile` |
| `--raw-html` | switch | the option `rawHtml` |
| `--roundtrip` | switch | the option `roundtrip` |
| `--sections` | switch | the option `sections` |
| `--smart-typography` | switch | the option `smartTypography` |
| `--social` | JSON | the option `social` |
| `--soft-break` | `newline`, `space`, `br` | the option `softBreak` |
| `--source-lines` | switch | the option `sourceLines` |
| `--strict-losses` | switch | the option `strictLosses`, with the allow list of C2-T-026 |
| `--symbols` | JSON | the option `symbols` |
| `--url-policy` | JSON | the option `urlPolicy` |
| `--from-ast` | switch | reads each file as a tree in JSON (C2-A-188) |
| `--includes` | switch, on | expands includes (C2-T-018) |
| `--include-root` | path | the containment root of includes (C2-N-004) |
| `--report-includes` | path | writes the include report (C2-T-022) |
| `--report-losses` | path | writes the losses as a diagnostics report (C2-T-021) |
| `--allow-loss` | code, repeatable | a code that is no loss (C2-T-027) |
| `--max-render-losses` | count, 100 | the losses retained per file (C2-T-029) |
| `--strict` | switch | ends a file that wrote an entry with status 1 (C2-T-051) |
| `--output` | path | writes the product to a file (C2-T-053); `-o` is the same |

**C2-T-025** A loss is a render-loss entry of a file whose code is not on the allow list. `render` writes each retained loss as a line on standard error, and no entry of the parse or the lint channel, which `diagnostics` and `lint` write (C2-T-031, C2-T-032).

**C2-T-026** With `--strict-losses` and a loss, `render` writes no HTML for that file and the file ends with status 1 and the category `render-loss` (C2-H-130). The command applies the allow list before `strictLosses`, so an allowed code alone never fails a file.

**C2-T-027** `--allow-loss` takes a code of the render-loss channel of `data/lint-rules.json`; any other value is refused with the category `usage`. An allowed code is neither written on standard error nor in the report. The codes of the run are the option `allowLosses` (C2-H-204).

**C2-T-028** `--report-losses` writes the losses of the run, and without a loss it writes the report with empty lists.

**C2-T-029** `--max-render-losses` takes a count, a decimal integer of at least 0, and its default is 100. It sets the option `maxLosses` (C2-H-205). Each file retains its first losses up to that count; the others are counted in `suppressed` and written on no line.

### `carve ast`

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--positions` | switch, on | writes `pos` on the nodes |
| `--envelope` | switch | writes the envelope of C2-A-012 instead of the bare tree |
| `--includes` | switch, on | expands includes (C2-T-018) |
| `--include-root` | path | the containment root of includes (C2-N-004) |
| `--report-includes` | path | writes the include report (C2-T-022) |

### `carve fmt`

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--check` | switch | changes nothing and reports the first changed line (C2-W-100) |
| `--diff` | switch | writes a unified diff (C2-W-100) |
| `--write` | switch | replaces each file (C2-T-016); `-w` is the same |
| `--normalize` | switch | the option `normalize` |
| `--align-tables` | switch | the option `alignTables` |
| `--from-ast` | switch | writes each file read as a tree in JSON (C2-W-102) |
| `--output` | path | writes the product to a file (C2-T-053); `-o` is the same |

**C2-T-030** `fmt` refuses `--write` with `--check` or with `--diff`, `--check` with `--diff`, and `--normalize` with `--from-ast`, with the category `usage`. Without one of `--check`, `--diff` and `--write` it writes the output on standard output. A writer loss of C2-W-134 ends the file with status 1 and the category `writer-refused`.

### `carve lint`

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--rules` | JSON | the option `rules` (C2-W-109) |
| `--platforms` | JSON | the option `platforms` (C2-W-109) |
| `--heading-ids` | `off`, `keep-case`, `lower`, `ascii`, `ascii-lower`, `ascii-strict`, `ascii-strict-lower` | the option `headingIds` (C2-T-042) |
| `--json` | switch | writes a diagnostics report (C2-T-021) instead of lines |
| `--includes` | switch, on | expands includes (C2-T-018) |
| `--include-root` | path | the containment root of includes (C2-N-004) |
| `--fix` | switch | rewrites the findings of the rules that have a fix (C2-T-049) |
| `--write` | switch | with `--fix`, replaces each file (C2-T-016, C2-T-050); `-w` is the same |
| `--strict` | switch | ends a file that wrote an entry with status 1 (C2-T-051) |
| `--ignore` | file, repeatable | drops the entries of that file (C2-T-052) |

**C2-T-031** `lint` writes the entries that the call `lint` returns, as lines or as a report, and ends a file with status 1 when an entry has the severity `warning` or `error`; a run of hints alone ends with 0. The call `lint` returns the record of its run (C2-W-103): the entries of its parse in the parse channel and its findings in the lint channel (C2-W-113), as 0.1 lint reported an unclosed fence. A rule that is off by default, as each `djot-` rule is, is turned on by its id in `--rules`.

**C2-T-042** `lint` reads `headingIds` (C2-H-131), so a host lints with the option map it renders with. A rule that compares a fragment with the ids of the rendered HTML, as `broken-fragment-link` does, compares it with the heading ids that value generates: under `lower` the heading `= Alpha` has the id `alpha`, so a link to `#alpha` reports nothing, and under the default `keep-case` it has the id `Alpha`, so the same link reports the case-only message that names `Alpha`. Under `off` a heading has no generated id.

**C2-T-049** `lint --fix` rewrites each finding of a rule whose row in `data/lint-rules.json` has a `fix` to the one replacement its message names, at the range of the finding; the `before` and `after` of the `fix` show it on one source. A rule whose message names two replacements, as `deprecated-bare-underline` does, has no fix. The command `fix` is `lint --fix` with the same flags. Under `--fix` every rule that has a fix is on unless `--rules` turns it off, and the other rules keep their defaults (C2-T-031). A range that two findings with different replacements report stays as written: in `~t~`, `djot-subscript-tilde` and `deprecated-bare-strike` disagree, and `--rules` turning one of them off picks the other. A fix is kept only where the fixed source, parsed again, has the construct of its replacement where the finding started: `+ item` directly below a line of paragraph text opens no list with `-` either, so it stays. The fixes repeat until a pass changes nothing.

**C2-T-050** Without `--write`, `lint --fix` writes the fixed source of each file on standard output and the entries that remain as lines on standard error. With `--write` it replaces each file whose fixed source differs from it (C2-T-016), and the entries that remain are its product, as lines or, with `--json`, as a report. A file ends with the status that `lint` gives its fixed source (C2-T-031). `--write` without `--fix`, and `--json` with `--fix` but without `--write`, are refused with the category `usage`.

**C2-T-051** `--strict` on `render` and `lint` ends a file that wrote any entry with status 1 and no category, a hint included. `render --strict` still writes the HTML; `--strict-losses` is the flag that withholds it (C2-T-026).

**C2-T-052** `lint --ignore` takes a file and drops every entry whose `file` (C2-N-063) is that id, and every entry of an entry file whose name as given (C2-T-013) is that value.

### `carve flatten`

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--include-root` | path | the containment root of includes (C2-N-004) |
| `--output` | path | writes the product to a file (C2-T-053); `-o` is the same |

**C2-T-047** `flatten` writes each file as one Carve document: it expands includes as `render` does (C2-T-018) and writes the expanded tree through the canonical writer (C2-W-100), so every include directive is replaced by the blocks it expanded to. It is the one command with Carve source as its product that expands (C2-N-005). The frontmatter of an included file is not written, since it renders nothing.

**C2-T-048** A file of `flatten` writes no source and ends with status 1 in three cases: with the category `include-unresolved` when an include did not expand, and the entries of its causes follow as lines on standard error; with `flatten-changed` when the HTML of the flattened source with the default options differs from that of the expanded tree, as when two included files each define one footnote, link reference or abbreviation key, which are looked up per file (C2-N-054, C2-N-055); and with `writer-refused` for a writer loss of C2-W-134.

### `carve diagnostics`

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | switch | writes a diagnostics report (C2-T-021) instead of lines |
| `--includes` | switch, on | expands includes (C2-T-018) |
| `--include-root` | path | the containment root of includes (C2-N-004) |
| `--report-includes` | path | writes the include report (C2-T-022) |

**C2-T-032** `diagnostics` writes the entries of the parse channel and ends with status 0 whatever they report.

### `carve import`

| Flag | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `--from` | `html` | the input format; required |
| `--raw-html` | switch | the option `rawHtml` of the importer (C2-M-065, C2-M-066) |
| `--strict-losses` | switch | the option `strictLosses` of the importer (C2-M-082) |
| `--report-losses` | path | writes the losses as a diagnostics report (C2-T-021) |
| `--allow-loss` | code, repeatable | a code that is no loss (C2-T-027) |
| `--max-render-losses` | count, 100 | the losses retained per file (C2-T-029) |
| `--output` | path | writes the product to a file (C2-T-053); `-o` is the same |

**C2-T-033** `import` without `--from` is refused with the category `usage`. The value `html` reads the input as C2-M-001 states; the reference engine also takes `markdown`, `gfm` and `djot` (C2-T-003).

**C2-T-034** `import` applies C2-T-025 to C2-T-029 to the entries of the importer (C2-M-080) and of the writer: with `--strict-losses` a loss of either fails the file with the category `render-loss` and writes no source. Without it, a writer loss of C2-W-134 fails the file with the category `writer-refused`.

**C2-T-035** An HTML input the importer refuses ends the run with status 2 and the category `import-input-invalid` (C2-M-006). A tree of the importer that fails the reader checks (C2-A-188) is a defect of the importer, and the file ends with status 1 and the category `import-tree-invalid`.

### `carve migrate-ast`

`migrate-ast` takes no flag beyond those of every command.

**C2-T-036** `migrate-ast` writes the migrated tree, as an envelope when the input was one (C2-A-012), and writes each entry of the migration record as a line on standard error (C2-A-180). It ends with status 0, and with status 2 and the category `ast-json-invalid` for an input it cannot read as a tree.

## Exit codes

**C2-T-037** A run ends with status 0 when every file did what was asked and nothing it gates on was found.

**C2-T-038** A run ends with status 1 and no category when `fmt --check` or `fmt --diff` finds a file that would change (C2-W-100), or `lint` finds an entry of severity `warning` or `error` (C2-T-031), or `--strict` finds any entry (C2-T-051).

**C2-T-039** Every failure with a category in C2-T-040 writes as its first line on standard error `carve[CATEGORY]:` and a message (C2-W-101).

**C2-T-040** The failure categories, their status and the library error each comes from are the rows of this table.

| Status | Category | Error | When |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `render-loss` | `CarveRenderError` | a loss under `--strict-losses` (C2-H-130, C2-M-082) |
| 1 | `writer-refused` | `CarveWriteError` | a writer loss of C2-W-134 in `fmt` or `import` |
| 1 | `import-tree-invalid` | | the importer returns a tree the reader refuses (C2-T-035) |
| 1 | `include-unresolved` | | an include that `flatten` did not expand (C2-T-048) |
| 1 | `flatten-changed` | | a flattened source that renders differently from the expanded tree (C2-T-048) |
| 2 | `usage` | `CarveOptionError` | an unknown flag, a bad or missing value, a refused combination, `--write` on standard input, an include root that cannot be read |
| 2 | `input-unreadable` | | a file that is missing or unreadable, a tree in JSON that is not UTF-8 |
| 2 | `input-invalid` | `CarveInputError` | a source longer than the `max_length` of its profile (C2-H-163) |
| 2 | `ast-json-invalid` | `CarveTreeError`, `CarveLayoutError`, `CarvePatchError` | a tree or a sidecar the reader refuses (C2-A-188, C2-L-058), a patch `applyPatch` refuses (C2-T-045) |
| 2 | `import-input-invalid` | `ImportInputError` | an HTML input the importer refuses (C2-M-006) |
| 2 | `output-unwritable` | | a file of `--write`, `--output` or a report that cannot be written |

## Not carried over

The 0.1 commands, flags and reports that this document does not carry over are listed in `UPGRADING.md`, Part 2, "Command line and missing features".
